title: Vets market investigation: draft substantive Order and Undertakings
summary: The CMA has published a notice of intention and draft substantive Order for its veterinary services market investigation, alongside a public consultation. It proposes new obligations on veterinary businesses and related requirements for the RCVS to support remedies. This is relevant to firms in the veterinary services market, not general financial services firms. Any consultation deadlines should be checked in the full notice.

title: CMA proposes removing 27 market remedies in part or full following review
summary: The CMA is consulting on a provisional decision to remove, partially remove or retain 33 market remedies, including measures affecting retail banking and current account switching. Interested parties can respond by 5pm on 11 September 2026. A final decision is expected in Autumn 2026.

title: Strategic review of CMA markets remedies
summary: The CMA has launched a consultation reviewing 33 existing markets remedies to decide whether they should be amended or removed. Stakeholders are invited to respond by 2 March 2026. The review concerns remedies across multiple sectors and may lead to a later final decision and notices of amendment or removal.

title: Proposed steering conduct requirement for Google’s mobile platform
summary: The CMA is consulting on a proposed steering conduct requirement for Google’s mobile platform/Play Store, aimed at reducing restrictions on how developers can inform users about offers and direct them to make purchases outside Google’s billing system. It affects developers distributing digital goods and services via the Play Store in the UK. The document is a consultation, so feedback is due by the consultation closing date stated in the full paper if applicable.

title: Proposed steering conduct requirement for Apple’s mobile platform
summary: The CMA is consulting on a proposed steering conduct requirement for Apple’s mobile platform, aimed at restricting Apple’s app-store rules that limit developers’ ability to steer users to offers and purchases outside the App Store. It affects developers distributing digital goods and services in the UK. This is a consultation only, so no immediate obligation arises, but firms should review the proposal and respond by the consultation deadline if relevant.

title: Valuation Methodology Review for Pubs and Hotels
summary: HM Treasury has launched a Call for Evidence on the valuation methodology used for business rates on pubs and hotels in England and Wales. It asks industry, valuers and other stakeholders for evidence and views on current approaches and possible improvements. No binding change is made yet; any accepted changes are intended for the next revaluation.

title: Draft revised guidance on our approach to assessing merger efficiencies
summary: The CMA is consulting on draft revised merger efficiencies guidance that would replace parts of the Merger Assessment Guidelines. It proposes more detail on when efficiencies arise, what evidence the CMA will consider, and how merging parties should engage. This is relevant to businesses involved in mergers and merger control, with responses due under the consultation process stated in the document.

title: Suspected anti-competitive conduct in relation to hotel accommodation services
summary: The CMA has opened an investigation into suspected anti-competitive information sharing among competing hotel providers under Chapter I of the Competition Act 1998. It names several hotel groups and warns that relevant documents must be preserved. This is an ongoing enforcement matter with no finding yet and no compliance deadline stated.

title: Paramount / Warner Bros. Discovery merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a notice confirming that Paramount Skydance’s merger notice for the anticipated acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery meets statutory requirements. The initial merger review period starts on 10 June 2026, and the CMA’s deadline to decide whether to refer the deal to phase 2 is 7 August 2026.

title: Red Driving School: consumer protection enforcement case
summary: The CMA has opened a consumer enforcement investigation into Red Driving School over how mandatory fees are shown in the purchase process for driving lessons. It is an open case only at this stage, with evidence gathering through August 2026 to January 2027 and a next update expected in January 2027. No infringement has been found yet.

title: Trainline: consumer protection enforcement case
summary: The CMA has opened a consumer protection enforcement investigation into Trainline over how mandatory fees are shown in ticket pricing. This is an active case, but no infringement has been found yet. The next case update is expected in January 2027.

title: Virgin Atlantic: consumer protection enforcement case
summary: The CMA has opened a consumer protection enforcement investigation into Virgin Atlantic’s presentation of mandatory fees in package holiday pricing. It is examining whether total prices were shown upfront and whether consumers received a total price when purchasing. This is an open case and no infringement finding has been made; no action date is set beyond a next case update in January 2027.

title: Vandemoortele required to sell UK plant following pastry merger investigation
summary: The CMA published its final report on the Vandemoortele/Délifrance merger, clearing it only subject to remedies. Vandemoortele must sell its Worcester laminated dough plant and current UK sales operations to a suitable purchaser to address competition concerns. The investigation finished about 7 weeks before the 24-week statutory deadline.

title: Aramark / Entier merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has issued an Initial Order in the Aramark/Entier merger inquiry under the Enterprise Act 2002. It restricts integration and requires the businesses to operate separately pending the merger review. Applies to Aramark, Aramark Investments Limited, Aramark Limited and Entier from 25 March 2025.

title: Energy licence modification appeals 2026
summary: Cadent Gas has filed a notice of appeal against GEMA’s RIIO-GD3 licence modification decision, challenging part of the price control and the 1 April 2026 licence changes. The appeal concerns gas transporter licence conditions for Cadent and other gas distribution network operators. This is a court/tribunal process rather than a rule change, but it may affect regulated revenue and obligations.

title: Heating oil review: consumer protection enforcement case
summary: The CMA published an open letter to domestic heating oil suppliers reminding them that consumer contract terms must be fair and transparent, especially where liability is limited or delayed performance is involved. It also reported that its consumer protection review found possible contract breaches and that suppliers have agreed to compensate affected customers.

title: CMA correspondence in relation to early years education and childcare sector
summary: The CMA has launched a market study into early years education and childcare in England and opened a consultation/call for views on its proposed scope. It will examine access, affordability, consumer choice, public bodies and provider types, but it has no direct intervention powers at this stage. No compliance deadline is set; this is an engagement and evidence-gathering exercise.

title: Early years education and childcare market study
summary: The CMA has launched a market study into early years education and childcare services in England. It will examine how the sector works, including funding, competition, information and regulation, and invite comments on the scope and questions raised. This is an evidence-gathering review rather than a binding rule change, so it mainly informs future recommendations for government and regulators.

title: Early years education and childcare market study: providers and professionals
summary: The CMA closed a call for evidence as part of its early years education and childcare market study. It asked for views from childcare providers, families and other interested people, with the call running from 1 July 2026 to 26 July 2026. This is an awareness-only market study publication and does not create obligations for firms.

title: Early years education and childcare market study: families
summary: The CMA opened a closed call for evidence as part of its early years education and childcare market study, seeking views from families, providers and others on how childcare services work and could work better. It covered childminders, nurseries and pre-schools for children from birth to school age. The call ran from 1 July 2026 to 26 July 2026.

title: How to engage with the CMA’s childcare market study
summary: The CMA has launched a market study into early years education and childcare services in England. It invites views on the statement of scope, with responses due by 26 July 2026, and says it will gather evidence through questionnaires, statutory information requests, research and stakeholder engagement before a final report in May 2027.

title: Early years education and childcare market study: other interested people
summary: The CMA closed a call for evidence for its early years education and childcare market study. It asks stakeholders, families and providers about how childcare services for children from birth to school age are working and whether the market could work better. Views were accepted from 1 July 2026 to 26 July 2026.

title: CMA opens probe into childcare sector
summary: The CMA has launched a market study into early years education and childcare in England, covering access, affordability, information and provider types. It is seeking input through a call for views, with provisional findings expected by early 2027. The study may lead to recommendations to government and guidance for businesses or consumers, but it does not itself create new obligations.

title: Heating oil market study
summary: The CMA has launched a market study notice into the domestic heating oil market in the UK and invites representations by 8 April 2026. The CMA says it must publish its market study report by 19 March 2027 and may consider a market investigation reference. This is a market study, so it is mainly an awareness item for firms with exposure to the sector.

title: Review of the interaction between the Market Access Principles and England’s Air Quality (Domestic Solid Fuels Standards) Regulations 2020
summary: The CMA’s Office for the Internal Market published its final report on how the Market Access Principles interact with England’s ‘Ready to Burn’ scheme for certain manufactured solid fuels and house coal. It follows a joint referral from UK and devolved administrations and is now closed. No new obligations or deadlines are created; the report is for market participants and policymakers.

title: How to engage with the CMA’s private dental services market study
summary: The CMA has launched and is updating a market study into private dental services in the UK. It is gathering evidence, will consult on emerging thinking and remedies in October to November 2026, and expects a final report by 4 March 2027. Dental businesses and related stakeholders may be asked for information and views.

title: Unfair contract terms
summary: The CMA has published updated guidance on unfair contract terms under the Consumer Rights Act 2015. It explains how the Part 2 rules apply to businesses using consumer terms and notices, including fairness, transparency, prohibited terms and enforcement. It is guidance only, but businesses should use it to review consumer contracts and notices now.

title: Transparency and disclosure - statement of CMA’s policy and approach: CMA6
summary: The CMA has issued its statement of policy and approach on transparency and disclosure (CMA6), covering how it handles information requests, disclosure, confidentiality, public authority cooperation and data protection across CMA cases and functions. It applies to CMA cases under competition, consumer enforcement and subsidy control regimes, plus motor fuel information gathering. The document re-issues overseas investigative assistance guidance unchanged, effective since 2024-12-19.

title: Sky / ITV merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has opened an invitation to comment on Sky’s anticipated acquisition of ITV, in the communications sector. Interested parties can submit views on competition issues by 6 August 2026. This is an early-stage merger review and not yet a formal investigation or decision.

title: Google search publisher conduct requirement
summary: The CMA has issued Google’s reporting notice for the Publisher Conduct Requirement under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024. It sets the form, content and timing of compliance reports, and requires Google to appoint a Nominated Officer and submit reports to the CMA within the first month after receiving the notice. It applies to Google’s general search services.

title: Strategic review of CMA markets remedies
summary: The CMA is reviewing 33 market remedies, including undertakings and orders across financial services and other sectors, and has published a provisional decision consultation. Views are invited by 11 September 2026, with final decision due in October 2026. Firms affected by any reviewed remedies should assess whether changes could alter market conduct or product arrangements.

title: Provisional decision: strategic review of CMA markets remedies
summary: The CMA has issued a provisional decision in its strategic review of legacy market remedies and undertakings, proposing to revoke, release or vary several remedies under the Enterprise Act 2002. It is not a banking rule, but it may affect firms subject to any named remedies and their legal/compliance teams. No single compliance date is stated in the excerpt.

title: nexfibre / Substantial merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has referred Liberty Global/Telefónica/InfraVia’s nexfibre acquisition of Substantial for a phase 2 merger investigation under the Enterprise Act 2002. This is a market competition decision affecting the parties to the transaction, with no direct conduct obligations for regulated firms. The decision was made on 1 July 2026 and published on 14 August 2026.

title: Vets market investigation: draft Funding Order and Undertakings
summary: The CMA has published a draft Funding Order and related undertakings for the veterinary household pets market investigation, alongside a consultation on the draft Order. It sets out a proposed funding mechanism for the RCVS to carry out monitoring and other activities, funded by levies on veterinary businesses, and invites representations before the CMA decides whether to proceed.

title: Veterinary Services Market Investigation (Funding) Order 2026 and Veterinary Services Market Investigation Royal College of Veterinary Surgeons (Funding) Undertakings 2026
summary: The CMA has made a funding order and related RCVS funding undertakings for its veterinary household pets market investigation remedies package. The notice explains how veterinary businesses will fund RCVS activities through a levy and associated collection/estimation processes, alongside separate substantive remedies. No direct bank obligations arise, but it is relevant as a market-study/remedies notice.

title: Schlumberger / ChampionX merger inquiry
summary: The CMA is inviting comments on Schlumberger’s anticipated acquisition of ChampionX as part of its initial merger assessment. Interested parties are asked to submit views by 10 December 2024. This is a preliminary market review and not yet a formal investigation or decision.

title: GXO / Wincanton merger inquiry
summary: The CMA granted derogations from an Initial Enforcement Order in the GXO/Wincanton merger inquiry, allowing limited steps such as de-listing, re-registration, name changes, board changes and insurance arrangements, subject to strict conditions. The notice is addressed to the parties to the merger and does not impose a general rule for banks.

title: Venture capital access expanded for early-stage companies in UK
summary: HMT announces a £100m next phase of the British Business Bank’s Investor Pathways Capital Initiative, with applications for the next cohort opening in Autumn 2026. The news also references prior commitments to microfunds and recent reforms to the Growth Guarantee Scheme, but it is a government news story rather than a rule, consultation or supervisory notice.

title: Aldi and Lidl should be subject to the same rules as major supermarkets
summary: The CMA issued a press release saying it provisionally wants Aldi, Lidl GB and Lidl NI to be covered by the Groceries Market Investigation (Controlled Land) Order 2010, which would restrict certain land agreements used to block rival supermarkets. Stakeholders can submit views by 5pm on 7 September 2026 before a final decision in the autumn.

title: Potential designation of Aldi and Lidl under the Groceries Market Investigation (Controlled Land) Order 2010
summary: The CMA is inviting comments on whether Aldi and/or Lidl should be designated as Large Grocery Retailers under the Groceries Market Investigation (Controlled Land) Order 2010. Stakeholders are asked to provide evidence by 13 April 2026 on their product range, pricing and any competition impacts from not being in scope. This is a consultation-style invitation to comment, not a final designation decision.

title: Vivisol / Air Liquide (home oxygen services business) merger inquiry
summary: The CMA is inviting comments on the anticipated acquisition of Air Liquide’s home oxygen services business by Vivisol. This is a merger case page and invitation to comment for Phase 1, with comments requested by late September 2026. It is an information-gathering notice, not a final decision or binding rule.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy to UDX Development Company Limited by the Department for Culture Media and Sport
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a report on DCMS’s proposed subsidy to UDX Development Company Limited. It evaluates DCMS’s assessment of compliance with the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and invites third-party submissions on the report process; it does not itself create obligations for firms. The report was published on 12 August 2026, and the submission deadline is in the administrative timetable but no exact date is stated here.

title: Google’s mobile platform
summary: The CMA has opened an initial strategic market status investigation into Google’s mobile ecosystem under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024. It covers Android, native app distribution and mobile browser/browser engine activities, and may lead to a revised notice or future designation. No compliance action is required yet, but the matter should be monitored.

title: Apple’s mobile platform
summary: The CMA has issued a notice starting an initial strategic market status investigation into Apple’s mobile ecosystem under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024. It describes the scope of the investigation, including iOS, the App Store and Safari/WebKit, and says the CMA may revise the scope or close the investigation before a final view. No firm action or deadline is imposed on regulated firms.

title: The CMA's programme of work across mobile platforms
summary: CMA guidance page summarises its work on mobile platforms under the digital markets regime, including SMS designations for Apple and Google, ongoing engagement on app review, interoperability, NFC access and app steering, and planned consultations and work in 2026. It is informational and does not itself create new obligations for firms.

title: CMA publishes latest monitoring update on road fuel market
summary: The CMA published a press release on its latest road fuel market monitoring report, saying it found no evidence retailers changed pricing strategies to exploit the Middle East conflict, but remains concerned about sustained high margins. It also said Fuel Finder registration is now very high and that it will keep monitoring prices, with a fuller review due in autumn.

title: Enhanced road fuel monitoring report: August 2026
summary: The CMA published an enhanced monitoring report on UK road fuel prices and margins in response to the Middle East conflict, including its assessment of fuel finder compliance and enforcement activity. It says market conditions improved by June but concerns remain about weak competition and retailer margins. This is an informational market update with no new binding requirements.

title: Trainline, Virgin Atlantic and RED Driving School investigated for drip pricing
summary: The CMA announced consumer-protection investigations into Trainline, Virgin Atlantic and RED Driving School over alleged drip pricing and failure to show mandatory fees upfront. It says the cases are at an early stage and no breach has been found. The press release also reminds firms of the CMA’s wider pricing campaign and possible fines/refunds if the law is broken.

title: Veterinary services for household pets
summary: CMA-commissioned qualitative research report on how pet owners choose, switch and pay for veterinary services, including health plans, prescriptions, referrals, diagnostics and out-of-hours care. It is background research only and does not set rules or deadlines.

title: FirstCash / Ramsdens merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published an invitation to comment on the anticipated acquisition of Ramsdens Holdings PLC by FirstCash Holdings Inc. Interested parties may submit initial views on competition issues by 4 September 2026. This is part of the CMA’s pre-investigation information gathering in a financial services merger case.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy to Ryanair UK Limited by Invest Northern Ireland
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit has opened a referral on Invest Northern Ireland’s proposed £67 million subsidy to Ryanair UK Limited for an MRO facility in Northern Ireland. Third parties may submit comments by the deadline in the timetable. The SAU will publish a report evaluating Invest NI’s assessment of subsidy-control compliance within 30 working days.

title: Treasury to call time on uncertainty for pubs and hotels
summary: HM Treasury announced an independent review and call for evidence on business rates valuations for pubs and hotels. The review, led by Jerry Schurder, will report by the end of March 2027, ahead of implementation at the next revaluation. This is a policy announcement and engagement exercise, not a binding rule change.

title: Referral of the proposed Scottish Zero Emission Truck Fund Scheme by Transport Scotland
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit has accepted a referral from Transport Scotland on the proposed Scottish Zero Emission Truck Fund Scheme and is inviting third-party submissions. The SAU will assess the scheme’s compliance with subsidy control requirements and publish a report within 30 working days. This is an information-gathering notice on a proposed public subsidy scheme for transport.

title: Chancellor statement on Iran sanctions
summary: HMT published a news statement from the Chancellor on further Iran sanctions and UK/US efforts to pressure Iran. It is political and informational, with no new legal text, deadlines or firm obligations in the statement itself.

title: 5 ways drivers can save money and avoid costly mistakes as summer travel peaks
summary: CMA news story giving consumer tips for drivers on cheaper fuel and private parking charges during the summer travel peak. It does not create new rules or deadlines; it is general awareness only.

title: Danone / Huel merger inquiry
summary: The CMA published a merger notice for Danone Holdings (UK)’s anticipated acquisition of Huel Limited under the Enterprise Act 2002. The notice starts the CMA’s initial review period and states the phase 2 referral decision deadline is 11 September 2026. This is an update on a competition case, not a financial-services rule change.

title: NRG Fleet Services / Specialist Fleet Services merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has made an Initial Order in its merger inquiry into NRG Fleet Services Limited’s acquisition of Specialist Fleet Services Limited. The order applies to the acquirer group and SFS from 10 August 2026 and requires them to keep the businesses separate and preserve assets, management, IT, customer/supplier lists and service continuity while the CMA considers the merger.

title: The Brink’s Company / NCR Atleos Corporation merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a notice that a merger notice for The Brink’s Company’s anticipated acquisition of NCR Atleos Corporation meets the requirements of the Enterprise Act 2002. It starts the initial review period on 27 August 2026 and sets the CMA’s phase 2 referral deadline for 22 October 2026.

title: Great British Summer Savings: millions of pounds saved by families
summary: HMT issued a news story promoting the Great British Summer Savings scheme, which says a VAT cut to 5% on kids’ meals and certain attraction tickets will end at midnight on 1 September. It reports on participating businesses and consumer savings, but does not create new obligations for firms.

title: Interim Chair of National Savings and Investments appointment extended
summary: HM Treasury announced an extension to Luke Jensen’s interim chair appointment at National Savings and Investments until 31 October 2026 while a permanent chair is recruited. This is a public news item about a governance appointment, not a rule, consultation, or supervisory requirement.

title: Ministers to boost innovation in payments with new objective for Bank of England
summary: HMT announces plans to give the Bank of England a new secondary objective to support innovation in payment systems and digital money, including stablecoins, while keeping financial stability primary. The change would extend the existing innovation objective for CCPs and CSDs to systemic payment systems. Government says it will be taken forward through amendments to the Financial Services and Markets Bill; no implementation date is given.

title: CMA secures compensation for heating oil customers
summary: CMA press release announcing compensation for heating oil customers after suppliers cancelled orders during a price spike. Affected customers will be contacted directly; some will receive payments for replacement oil, while others will have original orders honoured. No action is needed from eligible customers at this stage.

title: UK leads way in disrupting shadowy Russian sanctions evasion network
summary: HMT and the NCA issued a press release announcing a nationwide alert on the A7 sanctions-evasion network and wider UK action against Russia-linked financial networks. It also says the government will raise the maximum OFSI monetary penalty for sanctions breaches from 50% to 100% of the breach value, but no commencement date is given in the text.

title: £100 million competition to back British AI companies to fix public services
summary: HMT announced a £100 million press-release competition under the Sovereign AI R&D Procurement Scheme to back British AI start-ups developing public-sector solutions, including NHS productivity, compute efficiency, defence, and AI agent security testing. It is an announcement of government funding and procurement activity, not a regulatory rule or supervisory requirement.

title: Three Hundreds of Chiltern
summary: The Treasury announces an appointment to the ceremonial office of Steward and Bailiff of the Three Hundreds of Chiltern. This is a news item with no regulatory requirements, deadlines or impact on regulated firms.

title: 12 new experts to join the CMA's inquiry panel
summary: The CMA announced 12 new appointments to its inquiry panel, with members taking up posts in September and October 2026. The press release describes the appointees’ backgrounds and the panel’s role in market investigations, merger inquiries and regulatory appeals. No direct obligations or compliance actions are set out for firms.

title: E.ON / OVO merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a merger notice for the anticipated acquisition of OVO Energy Ltd by E.ON SE (through E.ON UK Limited). It starts the statutory initial period on 3 September 2026 and sets 28 October 2026 as the deadline for the CMA to decide whether to refer the merger for a phase 2 investigation.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy to EDF Energy Nuclear Generation Ltd by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a report on DESNZ’s proposed subsidy to EDF Energy Nuclear Generation Ltd for the Sizewell B lifetime extension. It is an advisory publication on a specific subsidy control case, not a rule, enforcement action, or supervisory requirement. Third parties could submit comments by the timetable date stated in the report.

title: Merger assessment guidelines
summary: The CMA updated its merger assessment guidelines, including the section on merger efficiencies. The new version took effect on 3 September 2026 and applies to merger cases where the formal Phase 1 investigation starts on or after that date.

title: Seras / Enva (dedicated waste wood business) merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a merger notice for the anticipated acquisition by Seras Energy Ltd of G.I. Hadfield & Son Limited and confirmed the initial merger review period has started. The CMA’s deadline to decide whether to refer the merger for phase 2 is 14 August 2026.

title: Referral of the proposed Contracts for Difference for Renewables Allocation Round 8 scheme by DESNZ
summary: CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a final report on DESNZ’s proposed Contracts for Difference Allocation Round 8 scheme. It explains the scheme, the eligible technologies and changes following consultation, but does not itself create rules for firms. The report was published on 4 September 2026.

title: Chancellor takes axe to delays holding back growth
summary: HM Treasury issued a press release on measures to speed up growth, including new sandboxing powers, changes to judicial review for nationally significant infrastructure projects, reduced consultation and reporting requirements, and a review of rail infrastructure costs. It also announced ambitions for UK unicorns, the Northern 500 and a British Business Bank fund. No direct obligations are imposed on firms in this publication.

title: First ever Entrepreneurship Advisor appointed to the Treasury
summary: HM Treasury announced the appointment of an Entrepreneurship Adviser to support the Chancellor on entrepreneurship policy, including access to finance, regulation, procurement, talent, innovation and competitiveness. It is a news item about an advisory appointment and stakeholder engagement, not a rule change. The role begins on 23 June and runs until Budget 2025.

title: Chancellor John Healey's Growth Speech 2026
summary: The Chancellor gave a speech on the government’s growth agenda, fiscal discipline and investment priorities. It is informational only and does not create or change rules, deadlines or obligations for firms. Financial services is mentioned as one of the UK’s strengths, but there is no direct regulatory action.

title: On track: delivering the promises of the digital markets regime
summary: CMA speech setting out progress on the UK digital markets regime, including how it is using conduct requirements, commitments and voluntary engagement with major tech firms. It is an update on the authority’s approach and achievements, not a new rule or formal supervisory notice.

title: Economic Secretary to the Treasury speech at UK Finance
summary: HMT’s Economic Secretary gave a speech at UK Finance supporting the digitalisation and tokenisation of wholesale financial markets. She highlighted progress on the Digital Securities Sandbox, DIGIT and payments modernisation, and said government will work with industry and regulators on further changes. No new rule, deadline or obligation is created by the speech.

title: Competition and Markets Authority
summary: CMA homepage/publications landing page listing guidance, speeches, policy papers, research, transparency items and contact information. It does not impose new obligations or set deadlines; it simply signposts current CMA materials, including consumer, business and procurement-related content.

title: Public procurement in the national interest: Reflections from the CMA
summary: The CMA delivered a speech reflecting on public procurement and two accompanying reports. It discusses how government procurement could better support growth, innovation, resilience and competition, including by reducing fragmentation and barriers to entry, and highlights bid rigging risks. It is commentary only and does not create binding requirements for firms.

title: Public procurement and competition: supporting growth and innovation
summary: The CMA published a reflections paper on using public procurement more strategically to support growth, innovation and resilience, and separately highlights bid-rigging risks in public procurement. It sets out recommendations for government and public bodies, but does not itself change rules or create obligations for firms. No compliance date is stated.

title: Procurement in the national interest
summary: The CMA published two research and policy papers on public procurement, covering how government can use procurement to support growth, innovation and economic security, and arguing for stronger action on bid rigging through better data collection and use. It is informational only and does not impose requirements on firms.

title: Information Commissioner's Office
summary: This is the ICO publication landing page, highlighting a mix of news, research, guidance, consultations, and corporate reports. The named items include a press release, a call for input, consultation outcomes, guidance, and a memorandum of understanding, but the page itself does not create new obligations.

title: Economic Secretary to the Treasury speech at UK Private Capital
summary: HMT’s Economic Secretary gave a speech on private capital, growth and the government’s financial services strategy. It highlights ongoing and planned reforms affecting asset management, private markets, AI and pensions, but it does not create new rules or deadlines.

title: New members appointed to NISTA Expert Advisory Council
summary: HM Treasury announces five new appointments to NISTA’s Expert Advisory Council. The press release says the council will provide independent advice and challenge on infrastructure delivery, finance and service transformation, supporting the government’s 10 Year Infrastructure Strategy and wider project delivery reforms. It is advisory only and does not create obligations.

title: Referral of the proposed Critical Chemicals Resilience Fund subsidy scheme by the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit has accepted a referral from the Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade on the proposed Critical Chemicals Resilience Fund. The notice explains the scheme, invites third-party submissions, and says the SAU will publish its report within 30 working days. This is an information notice about a subsidy control review, not a rule or obligation for firms.

title: Heating oil suppliers: using fair terms and conditions
summary: The CMA published an open letter reminding domestic heating oil suppliers that consumer contract terms and conditions must be fair and transparent, especially where liability is limited or removed. It is an information notice rather than a binding rule change, and it follows CMA intervention and voluntary compensation linked to cancelled orders during a price surge.

title: Monitoring of the commitments given by IAG to the European Commission in relation to its acquisition of bmi
summary: The CMA published a notice saying it is monitoring commitments given by IAG to the European Commission in connection with IAG’s 2012 acquisition of bmi. It is an informational notice about an existing commitments monitoring process, with no new requirements or deadlines stated.

title: Hundreds of new officers to hunt down dirty money networks
summary: HMT/Home Office announced a news story on a £500 million crackdown to recruit 500 new officers to target money laundering, organised crime and criminal asset recovery under the UK’s Anti-Money Laundering and Asset Recovery Strategy. It describes enforcement and intelligence activity across police, the NCA, CPS and FCA, but does not create new rules or deadlines for firms.

title: Vandemoortele / Délifrance merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has accepted the merger notice for Vandemoortele’s anticipated acquisition of Délifrance and started the initial merger review period. The notice states the phase 2 referral decision deadline is 8 December 2025.

title: Welltower / multiple care homes merger inquiries
summary: The CMA published a merger-related derogation letter and annex for the completed acquisition of HC-One by Welltower. It allows limited disposal activity for five care homes, subject to prior CMA written consent and advance notice. The annex restates penalties for false or misleading information under the Enterprise Act 2002.

title: Co-operative Group / Southern Co-operative merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has made an Initial Order in relation to Co-operative Group’s anticipated acquisition of Southern Co-operative. The order, effective from 2026-07-26, requires CGL and Siena to keep the businesses separate and maintain their independence pending the merger inquiry. It restricts integration, asset transfers, staff moves, IT integration and information sharing.

title: OCS / Mitie merger inquiry
summary: The CMA is inviting comments on OCS Group International Limited’s anticipated acquisition of Mitie Group plc. This is an early merger case page and no formal phase 1 investigation has started yet. Interested parties can submit views by 29 September 2026.

title: Chancellor announces Bank of England appointments
summary: HMT announced three new non-executive director appointments to the Bank of England’s Court, plus two reappointments. The release gives names, backgrounds and start dates, with first Court meetings for the new appointees from September 2026 to February 2027. It is informational only and does not change rules or obligations for firms.

title: Delivering predictable regulation in an unpredictable world
summary: A CMA Chair speech sets out the regulator’s commitment to stable, predictable and transparent regulation, with references to a three-year strategy, merger process improvements and public procurement reports. It is for awareness only and does not itself change rules or create deadlines for firms.

title: UK’s 250th banking hub opens in Chepstow, keeping access to cash and face-to-face banking in the town
summary: HMT announces the opening of the 250th UK banking hub in Chepstow, preserving cash access and face-to-face banking after a branch closure. It reiterates the government’s wider goal of 350 hubs this parliament and notes an independent review into access to banking services will report in October.

title: UK – U.S. Financial Regulatory Working Group Summer 2026: Joint Statement
summary: HM Treasury and the U.S. Treasury published a joint statement recording the 13th UK–U.S. Financial Regulatory Working Group meeting. It summarizes topics discussed and outcomes, but does not set new requirements, deadlines, or formal policy changes.

title: Google search fair ranking conduct requirement
summary: The CMA published interpretative notes for Google’s Fair Ranking Conduct Requirement under the UK digital markets regime. The notes explain how the requirement applies to ranking and presentation of organic search results, search features and search generative AI, and what is out of scope. Google must use the notes in its compliance and reporting, and the CMA may update them while the requirement remains in force.

title: British Sign Language (BSL) 5-year plan: HM Treasury
summary: HM Treasury published its 5-year British Sign Language plan, explaining how it intends to improve BSL use in communications over the next five years. It applies to HM Treasury as a government department and includes annual progress updates during the plan period. No direct financial-services requirements are created for firms.

title: Financial Inclusion Committee
summary: HMT published an informational policy paper on the Financial Inclusion Committee, including its terms of reference, membership and summary notes of meetings from December 2024 to June 2026. It explains the Committee’s role in supporting delivery of the Financial Inclusion Strategy. No new regulatory requirements or deadlines are set.

title: Scottish Income Tax outturn reconciliation for 2024-25
summary: HM Treasury published an explanatory note on the 2024-25 Scottish Income Tax outturn reconciliation. It explains how HMRC and ONS data update Scottish Government funding under the Fiscal Framework, resulting in a net £720 million decrease in funding for 2027-28. It applies to Scotland and does not set requirements for firms.

title: Welsh Rates of Income Tax outturn reconciliation for 2024-25
summary: HM Treasury published an explanatory note on the 2024-25 Welsh Rates of Income Tax reconciliation. It explains how HMRC outturn data updates Welsh Government funding under the fiscal framework, producing a net £146 million increase in funding for 2027-28. No regulatory change or firm obligation is created.

title: Treasury Minutes – August 2026
summary: HM Treasury’s August 2026 Treasury Minutes is a government response to Public Accounts Committee reports on asylum, regulating for growth, MoD follow-up, Access to Work, museums and galleries, and Northern Powerhouse Rail. It is a parliamentary accountability document, not a financial-services rule or supervisory publication. It notes implementation timings including Autumn 2026 and December 2026 for government actions.

title: McCormick / Unilever merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a statutory merger notice for McCormick’s anticipated acquisition of the majority of Unilever’s global food business. The notice starts the initial review period on 17 September 2026 and sets 11 November 2026 as the CMA’s deadline to decide whether to refer the merger for a phase 2 investigation.

title: Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee – 17 September 2026
summary: This is a communiqué from the Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee meeting on 17 September 2026. It is informational only and does not create or change any requirements for firms.

title: Whole of Government Accounts, 2024-25
summary: HM Treasury’s Whole of Government Accounts 2024–25 is a public-sector financial reporting publication for the year ended 31 March 2025. It explains the UK public sector’s consolidated financial position and ongoing audit-quality issues, but does not create new regulatory requirements for financial services firms.

title: Business Rates Review: technical consultation
summary: HM Treasury/DLUHC published the outcome of the Business Rates Review technical consultation for England. It confirms the government’s commitment to reforms from the 2020 review and provides further detail on implementation, including more frequent revaluations, improvement relief, green plant and machinery support, and other administrative changes. The document is an outcome/consultation record rather than a final rule, and no in-force date is stated here.

title: Senior Managers & Certification Regime: a Call for Evidence
summary: HM Treasury has issued a call for evidence on the Senior Managers and Certification Regime, asking for views on how well it is working and whether future reforms are needed. It is not a rule change itself, but may inform later legislative or regulatory action. Responses are invited as part of a joint evidence-gathering exercise with the FCA and PRA.

title: The future of customs declarations
summary: HMT and HMRC published the outcome of a call for evidence on simplifying customs declarations and using technology to support import and export processes. The government says it will reduce information requirements by up to a quarter and will use the feedback to shape wider border transformation. The consultation closed on 8 September 2023.

title: Draft regulations: the Co-ownership Contractual Schemes (Tax) Regulations 2024
summary: Draft statutory regulations for co-ownership contractual schemes and Reserved Investor Funds (Contractual Schemes) would amend multiple tax statutes, including stamp duty, stamp duty land tax, capital gains and reporting provisions. They set out tax treatment, information requirements to HMRC and penalties for failure to notify or provide information. The regulations come into force on a date to be specified in the instrument.

title: Review of Home Credit Market Investigation Order 2007: Final Decision and Notice of Intention to Vary consultation
summary: The CMA has published a consultation tied to its final decision to vary parts of the Home Credit Market Investigation Order 2007. It concerns the cash-loan price comparison website requirements and proposed changes to lender information and website obligations. Stakeholders could respond to the consultation; the notice says the relevant provisions are under review and may be varied.

title: Data protection fee regime: proposed changes
summary: The ICO has published the outcome of a consultation on proposed changes to the data protection fee regime. It proposes increasing fees payable by data controllers by 37.2% across all tiers and reviews fee criteria, the Direct Debit discount and exemptions. The consultation closed on 3 October 2024; this outcome is informational and does not itself change the rules.

title: Pensions Investment Review: Unlocking the UK pensions market for growth
summary: The UK government has published its consultation response on reforms to the defined contribution workplace pensions market. It sets final policy positions on minimum scale and investment capability requirements, approval of new default arrangements, and contractual overrides for bulk transfers, with legislation to follow in the forthcoming Pension Schemes Bill. The consultation on differential pricing is closed and no further reforms will be taken forward.

title: Strengthening the Soft Drinks Industry Levy
summary: HM Treasury and HMRC have issued a consultation outcome changing the Soft Drinks Industry Levy. The lower sugar threshold is reduced, exemptions for milk-based and milk substitute drinks are removed or narrowed, and a lactose allowance will apply to milk-based drinks. A technical consultation on draft legislation is due in 2026, with legislation to follow in a future Finance Bill and take effect on 1 January 2028.

title: Small business access to finance
summary: HM Treasury and the Department for Business and Trade published the outcome of a closed call for evidence on small business access to debt finance in the UK. It summarises responses on lending markets, alternative finance and underserved customers, and sets out the government’s position. No new requirements or deadlines are created.

title: Access to Banking Services Review: Call for Evidence
summary: HM Treasury has launched a Call for Evidence for the Access to Banking Services Review on declining access to in-person banking. It invites evidence from stakeholders across the UK, including financial institutions, consumers, SMEs and trade bodies, and closes for input on 20 July 2026. The review will use responses to assess customer detriment and develop recommendations for the Government.

title: Unlocking business: reform driven by you
summary: HM Treasury publishes a summary of responses to its business questionnaire on regulatory burdens. It reports stakeholder concerns about complexity, delays, duplicated reporting and difficulty challenging regulators, and says the evidence will inform future departmental and sector-specific reform work. No new rules, obligations or deadlines are created.

title: Pennon / Sumisho Osaka Gas Water UK merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has made an Initial Enforcement Order for the Pennon/Sumisho Osaka Gas Water UK merger. It applies to Pennon and the Target from completion of the transaction and restricts integration and other actions pending the CMA’s review. The order requires the businesses to remain separate and maintain operations, staff and information barriers.

title: EasyPark / Flowbird merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a statutory merger notice for the anticipated acquisition of Mobility 1 SAS by EasyPark Group AS. It confirms the merger notice meets the Enterprise Act requirements and sets the phase 1 timetable, with the CMA’s referral decision deadline stated as 8 August 2024.

title: Sale of Oasis concert tickets by Ticketmaster
summary: The CMA has closed a call for evidence about Ticketmaster’s sale of Oasis tickets and opened an investigation into whether it broke the law. The evidence-gathering window ran from 2024-09-05 14:00 to 2024-09-19 17:00. This is an enforcement/investigation notice about alleged misleading pricing and purchase-process issues, not a new rule.

title: CMA wins drug market sharing appeal
summary: The Court of Appeal has overturned part of the CAT’s ruling and reinstated the CMA’s findings in a drug market-sharing case involving hydrocortisone tablets. The CMA’s penalties and anti-competitive findings against pharmaceutical firms were upheld in relation to the 10mg agreement. This is a published judgment/appeal outcome with no new compliance deadline.

title: Review of the Energy Market Investigation (Electricity Transmission Losses) Order 2016
summary: The CMA has completed its review of the Energy Market Investigation (Electricity Transmission Losses) Order 2016 and issued a final decision plus notice of variation. It found changed circumstances due to Energy Act 2023 provisions and the planned new electricity system operator, so parts of the Order are no longer appropriate as drafted and will be varied. The consultation ran from 23 July 2024 to 23 August 2024.

title: Tribunal fines drug firms £69m for excessive pricing after CMA investigation
summary: The Competition Appeal Tribunal has issued a judgment in a competition case against Pfizer and Flynn, finding they abused dominant positions and imposing combined fines of £69 million. This is a court determination and press release about the outcome, not a new rule or supervisory requirement.

title: CMA letter to Somerset Bridge Group about a breach of the Private Motor Insurance Order
summary: The CMA wrote to Somerset Bridge Group about breaches of the Private Motor Insurance Market Investigation Order 2015 on NCB Protection disclosures, affecting PMI products and many customers. The letter says the firm has taken remediation steps and the CMA will monitor compliance, with no formal enforcement action at present.

title: CMA letter to Direct Line Group about a breach of the Private Motor Insurance Order
summary: The CMA wrote to Direct Line Group about a breach of the Private Motor Insurance Market Investigation Order 2015, relating to failure to provide No Claims Bonus Protection information to at least 320 customers. Direct Line has refunded affected customers and fixed systems; the CMA says it will not take formal enforcement action for now but will monitor compliance. The public letter was copied to the FCA.

title: CMA wins appeal in emergency services case
summary: The Court of Appeal refused Motorola permission to appeal the CMA’s findings and price cap in the Airwave/emergency services case. The decision closes the case and leaves the CMA’s charge control order in place. No new requirements are created for firms, but the ruling confirms the existing cap on what Motorola can charge emergency services.

title: Bidvest (phs Group) / Citron Hygiene merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a merger notice under the Enterprise Act for Bidvest Group’s anticipated acquisition of Citron Hygiene. The notice starts the CMA’s initial merger review period on 10 January 2025, with a decision on whether to refer the merger for a phase 2 investigation due by 6 March 2025.

title: Court upholds CMA’s £99m fine on pharma over excessive NHS thyroid drug prices
summary: The Court of Appeal upheld the CMA’s finding that Advanz overcharged the NHS for liothyronine and reinstated Cinven’s full £51.9 million penalty. This is a court judgment on a competition-law appeal, not a new rule or supervisory requirement. It affects pharmaceutical market conduct and may be relevant for legal awareness only.

title: MasterCard / VocaLink merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a notice extending the preliminary assessment period in its merger inquiry into Mastercard’s anticipated acquisition of VocaLink. The extension takes effect on the publication date and remains until Mastercard provides the requested information to the CMA’s satisfaction or the CMA cancels it.

title: Water code modification appeal 2025 (Castle Water)
summary: Castle Water has filed a notice of appeal to the CMA against Ofwat’s decision on code modification CPW132 about credit support and wholesaler credit ratings in the non-household water retail market. It argues the decision was wrong and seeks relief from the appeal tribunal. This is a court/tribunal proceeding, not a rule change, and the document is dated 26 February 2025.

title: Ticketmaster: consumer protection case
summary: The CMA has accepted legally binding undertakings from Ticketmaster under Part 8 of the Enterprise Act 2002 over consumer protection concerns in primary-market ticket sales. Ticketmaster must change its website and ticket-labeling transparency practices and provide reports within the stated timetable, with measures to be taken within 4 weeks and in any event no later than 6 weeks from signature.

title: Provisional redeterminations on water price controls issued
summary: The CMA’s Independent Group has issued provisional redeterminations for five water companies’ price controls, allowing only part of the extra revenue sought and linking funding to outputs and performance. This is a consultation-stage decision, not yet final. It affects Anglian Water, Northumbrian Water, South East Water, Southern Water and Wessex Water, with the CMA now consulting on the provisional decision.

title: Investigation into suspected anti-competitive conduct by housebuilders
summary: The CMA issued a notice of intention to accept commitments in its investigation into suspected anti-competitive conduct by major housebuilders under the Competition Act 1998. It invites comments on the proposed commitments, including compliance, monitoring and reporting measures. This is relevant to firms in the housebuilding sector and to any group with competition-law exposure.

title: Sportradar / IMG Arena merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has issued a notice in a merger inquiry confirming that Sportradar Group AG’s merger notice for the anticipated acquisition of IMG Arena US Parent, LLC meets the statutory filing requirements. The initial period started on 1 September 2025, and the CMA’s phase 2 referral decision deadline is 24 October 2025.

title: Global Payments / WorldPay merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a statutory notice confirming that the merger notice for Global Payments’ proposed acquisition of Worldpay satisfies the Enterprise Act requirements. It also sets the initial period and the CMA’s deadline to decide whether to refer the merger to a phase 2 investigation, with the decision deadline stated as 11 November 2025.

title: Subsea7 / Saipem merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a notice that the merger notice for Subsea7 S.A. and Saipem S.p.A. satisfies the Enterprise Act 2002 requirements, starting the initial review period. The CMA’s deadline to decide whether to refer the merger to a phase 2 investigation is 25 November 2025.

title: Review of SME Banking Undertakings 2002
summary: The CMA has published its final decision on the SME Banking Undertakings 2002, releasing the remaining bundling provisions in full. The review concluded that the provisions are no longer appropriate. This is final and effective from 1 December 2025 for the designated banks covered by the undertakings.

title: Unite / Empiric merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has issued a notice that the merger notice for Unite Group’s proposed acquisition of Empiric Student Property meets the statutory filing requirements. It starts the initial merger period on 24 October 2025, with the CMA’s phase 2 referral decision due by 19 December 2025. This is an M&A competition-law notice, not a financial-services rule change.

title: FIS / TSYS merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a statutory merger notice for the anticipated acquisition of TSYS by FIS under the Enterprise Act 2002. It starts the CMA’s initial review period and sets the deadline for the CMA’s decision on whether to refer the merger to a phase 2 investigation.

title: Procedural complaints: raising procedural issues in CMA cases
summary: The CMA issued a procedural officer decision in Flynn Pharma’s competition case, refusing an extension of time to submit written representations on a Statement of Objections. It also addresses related access-to-file and hearing-timing issues, but does not change substantive competition rules. The decision concerns the parties to the investigation and the procedural timetable already in place.

title: Investigation of the Atlantic Joint Business Agreement
summary: The CMA issued a notice proposing to accept binding commitments from American Airlines and IAG in relation to the Atlantic Joint Business Agreement. It invites third-party comments before any formal acceptance, which would end the investigation without a finding on infringement. No compliance deadline is created for firms outside the case.

title: CMA investigates Adobe over concerns about cancellation fees
summary: The CMA has launched an investigation into Adobe over possible unfair and misleading early cancellation fees on certain membership plans. This is a press release, not a decision or rule change, and the CMA says it has reached no conclusions. It affects consumer-facing subscription pricing and disclosures for Adobe’s products; no compliance deadline is set.

title: Registering with and reporting your fuel prices to Fuel Finder
summary: The CMA has issued an open letter to motor fuel traders reminding them of mandatory Fuel Finder registration and reporting duties under the Motor Fuel Price (Open Data) Regulations 2025. Traders must register all forecourts and submit price updates within 30 minutes, with other details updated within three days. The CMA says it will prioritise enforcement from 1 May 2026.

title: Investigation into suspected anti-competitive conduct by Google in ad tech
summary: The CMA is investigating Google for suspected abuse of dominance in ad tech under Chapter II of the Competition Act 1998. This is an open enforcement investigation, not a rule change, and the CMA has issued a statement of objections and is considering representations. No action date applies to firms generally; the case concerns Google and the ad tech market.

title: Suspected anti-competitive conduct in relation to the supply of roofing and other construction services
summary: The CMA says it is investigating suspected bid-rigging and other anti-competitive conduct in the supply of roofing and construction services, with the scope expanded in January 2026 to include more parties and wider end customers. It names current businesses under investigation and reminds recipients of the duty to preserve relevant documents. No infringement has been found.

title: Private healthcare market investigation
summary: The CMA has brought article 22 of the Private Healthcare Market Investigation Order 2014 into force and published updates on PHIN compliance milestones and hospital action plans. The material concerns private healthcare providers and hospitals required to publish data through PHIN, with milestone updates issued on 4 December 2024, 10 October 2025 and 2 July 2026.

title: Suspected anti-competitive conduct in relation to the supply of Solidworks computer-aided design and computer-aided engineering software and related products and services
summary: The CMA has opened a Chapter I Competition Act 1998 investigation into suspected anti-competitive conduct in the supply of Solidworks software and related products/services in the UK. It names the current businesses under investigation and says the case is at the initial information-gathering stage, with no finding yet. Section 25B document-preservation duties apply to anyone who knows or suspects the investigation is under way.

title: Court upholds CMA findings that firms charged excessive and unfair prices for lifesaving NHS-funded medicine
summary: CMA press release saying the Court of Appeal upheld findings that Auden Mckenzie and Actavis UK broke competition law by charging excessive and unfair prices for hydrocortisone tablets and using anti-competitive conduct. It confirms infringement findings, while penalties will be reheard by the CAT. No new rules or deadlines are created.

title: Macquarie Asset Management / Energy Assets Group merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a notice starting the initial period for its merger inquiry into Macquarie Asset Management’s anticipated acquisition of Energy Assets Group. The notice says the CMA has enough information to begin investigating whether to refer the merger for a phase 2 investigation. The initial period starts on 30 July 2026 and the CMA’s referral decision deadline is 25 September 2026.

title: Emma Group: consumer protection case
summary: The High Court made a consent order in the CMA’s consumer protection case against Emma entities. The order declares past urgency messaging to be a Schedule 13 infringement and requires the defendants to stop repeating it, comply with Appendix B requirements, and ensure relevant group entities follow the order. The order is enforceable immediately and breach may be contempt of court.

title: CMA takes next procedural step in vet services investigation
summary: The CMA has published an issues statement in its market investigation into veterinary services, setting out initial competition concerns, possible remedies and the evidence it will gather. The consultation on the issues statement is open until 30 July 2024. This is an early procedural step only; no findings or remedies have been made.

title: Reviews of three merger undertakings and one market investigation Order
summary: The CMA published final decisions after reviewing three merger undertakings and one market investigation order under the Enterprise Act 2002. The decisions concern Lloyds TSB/Abbey National, Subsea 7/Acergy, Home Retail Group/Focus DIY, and the Energy Market Investigation (ECOES/DES) Order 2016. The consultation on provisional decisions closed on 18 April 2024; this publication records the final outcome.

title: CMA review of Part 3, Article 29, and Part 1 of Schedule 4 of the Home Credit Market Investigation Order 2007: Launch Consultation
summary: The CMA has decided to launch a review of parts of the Home Credit Market Investigation Order 2007 covering the comparison website and related requirements. It seeks stakeholder views on whether changed market conditions mean those provisions should be varied, superseded or revoked. The review follows a January invitation to comment and is aimed at deciding whether the remedies remain appropriate.

title: Directions issued to HSBC about breaches of the Retail Banking Order
summary: The CMA issued directions to HSBC UK Bank plc after finding repeated breaches of the Retail Banking Market Investigation Order 2017. HSBC must correct and keep accurate certain Open Banking API data and SME representative rates, and implement remedial steps including independent assurance and staff training. The document applies to HSBC and concerns breaches already identified; no new market-wide deadline is stated.

title: Leading UK boiler brand is changing marketing practices following CMA action
summary: The CMA has issued consumer law compliance advice for businesses marketing green heating and insulation products, including heat pumps, biomass boilers, solar thermal panels, insulation and solar PV. It sets out principles for headline pricing and product claims, and also applies to businesses marketing hydrogen-ready boilers. The advice is non-binding guidance, but firms should review marketing practices now.

title: Referral of the proposed Net Zero Hydrogen Fund Carbon Capture Use and Storage Scheme by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its report on DESNZ’s proposed Net Zero Hydrogen Fund CCUS Scheme, assessing compliance with the Subsidy Control Act 2022. The scheme concerns capital grant support for CCUS-enabled low carbon hydrogen projects in the UK, especially Track 1 projects. This is an information/reporting exercise rather than a binding rule change for firms.

title: CMA sets out provisional view on Vodafone / Three merger
summary: The CMA has provisionally found Vodafone/Three’s merger could substantially lessen competition in UK retail and wholesale mobile markets. It is consulting on provisional findings and possible remedies, with responses due by 27 September 2024 and 4 October 2024, before a final report due by 7 December 2024. Potential remedies include legally binding investment commitments and customer protections.

title: Vets Market Investigation: CMA updates on ‘behind the scenes’ progress
summary: The CMA has issued a market investigation update on veterinary services for household pets in the UK. It reports site visits, roundtables, teach-ins and information requests, and says a provisional decision is targeted for mid-next year. This is a progress update only, not a rule or enforcement action.

title: Housebuilding market study
summary: The CMA has launched a market study notice on the supply of new homes in England, Scotland and Wales. It invites representations, including on whether to make a market investigation reference, and says it will publish a report with findings and any proposed action by 27 February 2024. The notice is informational for firms in or adjacent to housebuilding.

title: Microsoft / Inflection inquiry
summary: The CMA is inviting comments on whether Microsoft’s hiring of Inflection AI employees and related licensing arrangements amount to a merger situation under the Enterprise Act 2002 and whether they could lessen competition in the UK. Interested parties are asked to submit views by 9 May 2024.

title: CMA publishes provisional findings in Mobile Browsers and Cloud Gaming market investigation
summary: The CMA has published provisional findings in its market investigation into mobile browsers and cloud gaming. It says Apple’s rules may be restricting browser competition, but proposes no further action on cloud gaming. The CMA is inviting comments by 13 December 2024 and expects a final decision in March 2025.

title: Loyalty pricing in the groceries sector
summary: The CMA has published the findings of its review of supermarket loyalty pricing in groceries. It says loyalty schemes generally deliver genuine savings, but warns retailers to review practices to ensure promotions comply with consumer law, especially when alternating loyalty and was/now offers. The review is now closed; no formal new rules or deadlines are set.

title: Administrative Penalties: Statement of Policy on the CMA’s Approach (CMA4)
summary: The CMA has published its Statement of Policy on Administrative Penalties (CMA4), explaining when it may impose penalties for breaches of investigatory and remedy requirements across CA98, EA02 and parts of the DMCCA24. It is a policy statement rather than a new rule, but it sets enforcement expectations now for affected firms and regulated sectors, including concurrent regulators such as the FCA and PSR.

title: Referral of a proposed subsidy to FlyDoncaster Limited by City of Doncaster Council
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit has published its final report on City of Doncaster Council’s proposed subsidy to FlyDoncaster Limited for reopening Doncaster Sheffield Airport. Third parties could submit comments by the stated deadline in the timetable. The publication explains the proposed £105.2m loan package and the SAU’s evaluation of compliance with the Subsidy Control Act 2022.

title: Mobile radio network services
summary: The CMA has opened an ordinary market reference into the supply of land mobile radio (LMR) network services for public safety in Great Britain, including relevant ancillary services. It defines the scope of the investigation but does not create obligations for firms in the publication itself.

title: Infant formula and follow-on formula market study
summary: The CMA has launched an invitation to comment for a market study into the UK supply of infant formula and follow-on formula, including some special medical purpose formulas sold directly to consumers. It seeks views on scope, consumer behaviour, regulation and supply-side features, with no direct obligations yet. Stakeholders should respond to the consultation and next steps set out in the document.

title: Mobile browsers and cloud gaming
summary: The CMA has issued draft terms of reference for a market investigation into mobile browsers, mobile browser engines, and cloud gaming distribution through app stores on mobile devices in the UK. It is an investigative publication, not a rule or enforcement decision, and no compliance date or obligation is set out.

title: Fake reviews
summary: CMA guidance explains the new DMCC Act banned practice on fake reviews and concealed incentivised reviews, plus misleading publication and prevention steps for trader-published consumer reviews. It sets expectations for traders and review publishers on what is unlawful and what reasonable, proportionate steps should be taken. No consultation or deadline is stated in the text provided.

title: Direct consumer enforcement guidance: CMA200
summary: The CMA has published guidance for its new direct consumer enforcement regime under the DMCC Act 2024. It explains the CMA’s enforcement process, information-gathering powers, undertakings, remedies, administrative penalties and monetary penalties for consumer law infringements. It is relevant to businesses covered by the consumer enforcement regime and signals how the CMA will exercise its powers, but it is guidance rather than a new binding rule.

title: Competition law court proceedings: serving documents on the CMA
summary: The CMA has published guidance for parties and advisers involved in competition law private actions on which documents must be served on the CMA in court proceedings. It explains how service should be made for cases raising issues under EU and UK competition laws. No deadline or new binding rule is stated in the notice.

title: Dynamic pricing project
summary: The CMA published an update on its dynamic pricing project, summarising findings and tips for businesses using dynamic pricing across sectors such as travel and leisure. It is not a formal investigation or market study. No direct compliance deadline is set, but businesses should use the guidance to assess pricing practices and consumer/competition impacts.

title: Consultation on proposed commitments in respect of the Atlantic Joint Business Agreement
summary: The CMA has published a notice of intention to accept binding commitments from IAG, American Airlines and Finnair concerning the Atlantic Joint Business Agreement. The consultation covers proposed slot, passenger volume and related commitments on routes such as London–Boston, Chicago, Dallas and Miami. Interested parties should review the proposals and respond within the consultation period; the document does not itself impose new obligations.

title: Cloud services market investigation
summary: The CMA has issued an issues statement for its market investigation into public cloud infrastructure services in the UK. It sets out initial competition hypotheses and potential remedies, and invites evidence during the investigation. The publication is relevant to firms using cloud services, especially where switching, interoperability or licensing practices may affect resilience and outsourcing arrangements.

title: Report on the proposed DRIVE35 Scale-Up Grants scheme by UK Research and Innovation
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit issued a non-binding report on UKRI’s proposed DRIVE35 Scale-Up Grants scheme. It reviews UKRI’s assessment of the scheme under the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and suggests improvements to the analysis, but does not decide whether the scheme can proceed. The scheme is expected to run from September 2025 to March 2030.

title: CMA refers B2B used car auction merger for Phase 2 investigation
summary: The CMA has provisionally found that Constellation’s acquisition of Aston Barclay may substantially lessen competition in B2B used vehicle auction services in Great Britain and has referred the merger for a Phase 2 investigation unless undertakings in lieu are offered by 6 October 2025. This is a competition-law merger review affecting the parties, not a financial-services rule change.

title: Vets market investigation: remedies working paper
summary: The CMA has published a working paper in its veterinary services market investigation setting out potential remedies and design considerations, including information disclosure, comparison tools, care plan cancellation/switching, referral information and other market reforms. It is a consultation-stage document for the vet sector, with no direct rule change yet. Firms in or connected to veterinary services should review the proposed options and likely impacts.

title: Investigation into Google’s ‘Privacy Sandbox’ browser changes
summary: The CMA published a notice of intention to release commitments previously accepted from Google about its Privacy Sandbox browser changes. It explains the competition concerns and invites comment on releasing those commitments; it does not create new rules for banks. No action date is stated in the excerpt, and the notice is mainly for awareness unless the firm has relevant digital advertising or browser-related exposure.

title: Proposed decision: SMS investigation into Apple's mobile platform
summary: The CMA has published a proposed decision in its strategic market status investigation into Apple’s mobile platform. It sets out the CMA’s provisional view on Apple’s market position and related digital activities, including mobile operating systems, app distribution, and browser engines. This is an intermediate competition-market investigation step, not a final binding decision, and no firm compliance deadline is stated in the excerpt.

title: Proposed decision: SMS investigation into Google's mobile platform
summary: The CMA has published a proposed decision in its Strategic Market Status investigation into Google’s mobile platform, setting out its provisional view on market status and competition concerns in Google’s mobile ecosystem. This is a non-binding market study/investigation publication, not a rule or enforcement notice. It is relevant to firms with digital platform, app distribution, browser or mobile ecosystem interests, but it creates no direct compliance deadline.

title: Leniency and no-action applications in cartel cases
summary: The CMA has published updated guidance on leniency and no-action applications in cartel cases, replacing the 2013 version. It explains how firms and individuals can seek immunity or reduced penalties for cartel conduct, including cooperation expectations and conditions for protection from prosecution or director disqualification. This is guidance rather than a new rule, so it mainly affects how cartel cases are handled going forward.

title: Merger notice form
summary: The CMA has updated its merger notice template for notifications under section 96 of the Enterprise Act 2002, reflecting changes from the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024. Firms that notify mergers to the CMA should use the revised form and follow the guidance notes when preparing draft and final notifications.

title: Image deal to move to in-depth investigation
summary: The CMA says Getty’s proposed purchase of Shutterstock will move to a Phase 2 merger investigation after Phase 1 concerns that the deal could raise prices, worsen terms or reduce quality in editorial and stock imagery. It is a press release, not a decision. No compliance deadline is set, but media, content and advertising businesses should monitor the investigation.

title: Understanding the CMA’s provisional decision in its vets market investigation
summary: The CMA sets out its provisional remedies from the veterinary services market investigation, including requirements for veterinary businesses operating FOPs on pricing, complaints handling, prescriptions, switching, and consumer information. It also provisionally recommends a new statutory regime for government to create. This is a consultation-stage market study output, so firms may need to prepare for later changes rather than act immediately.

title: Referral of the proposed Offshore Wind and Related Network Sectors Supply Chain Subsidy Scheme by Great British Energy
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit has published its report on Great British Energy’s proposed £300 million Offshore Wind and Related Network Sectors Supply Chain Subsidy Scheme. The report evaluates the scheme against the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and invites third-party submissions by the deadline in the administrative timetable. This is relevant to firms interested in subsidy control, public funding or supply-chain opportunities.

title: Draft guidance for businesses on price transparency
summary: The CMA has published draft guidance on price transparency under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024. It explains how businesses should present total prices, when charges must be included, and when partitioned pricing may be allowed. This is draft guidance for businesses, legal advisers and enforcers; no new binding rule is created in this publication.

title: Unfair commercial practices
summary: The CMA has published guidance on the DMCC Act’s unfair commercial practices provisions, replacing OFT1008. It explains who the rules apply to, what conduct is prohibited, and how the new regime applies to practices from 6 April 2025. Firms selling to consumers should review marketing, pricing, omissions, aggressive practices and review-related controls.

title: Provisional decision: review of the SME Banking Undertakings 2002
summary: The CMA has issued a provisional decision in its review of the SME Banking Undertakings 2002. It sets out provisional findings on whether the SME banking behavioural undertakings, especially the Limitation on Bundling Provisions, should be released, varied or kept. The document follows a consultation that closed on 7 May 2025 and is part of a market review of SME banking conditions.

title: What businesses need to know about unfair commercial practices
