summary: The CMA published a short guide on unfair commercial practices under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act. It is aimed at businesses and traders selling to consumers, including online sellers and their advisers, and points readers to fuller guidance on fake reviews and price transparency. No new obligations are set out in this short guide.

title: Civil engineering: CMA sets out concerns and options for better outcomes
summary: The CMA has published an interim report in its market study on civil engineering for public roads and railways. It identifies concerns around funding uncertainty, procurement, risk allocation and regulatory barriers, and seeks stakeholder views on possible remedies. Written submissions are due by 2026-01-28, with a final report expected in spring 2026.

title: Report on the proposed modified Network Charging Compensation Scheme by the Department for Business and Trade
summary: CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a non-binding report on DBT’s proposed modified Network Charging Compensation Scheme for energy-intensive industries in Great Britain. The report evaluates DBT’s subsidy-control assessment and suggests improvements, but it does not itself change the scheme or create obligations. No compliance deadline is set in the report.

title: CMA requires Aramark to sell Entier after finding competition concerns
summary: The CMA is consulting on remedies to address competition concerns in Aramark’s completed acquisition of Entier. It proposes options including divestment of a subset of offshore catering contracts, a full divestment of Entier, or an alternative remedy package. Interested parties were invited to comment by 2025-11-18.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy to Agratas Limited by the Department for Business and Trade
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its final report on DBT’s proposed subsidy to Agratas for an EV battery gigafactory in Somerset. It evaluates DBT’s assessment of compliance with the Subsidy Control Act 2022. Third parties were invited to submit comments by the timetable date set in the case materials.

title: Strategic review of merger remedies 2025
summary: The CMA has opened a strategic review of 37 merger remedies and proposes releasing or revoking them, mainly because the remedies are over 10 years old or no longer apply. The review covers 35 divestiture remedies and two rail-franchise remedies that have been brought into public ownership. This is a consultation/publication, not a binding rule change.

title: Will writing and other unregulated legal services
summary: The CMA has refreshed final compliance guidance for unregulated will writing, online divorce and pre-paid probate businesses, reflecting consumer law changes from the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024. It also closed its compliance review and noted some improvements, while reminding firms they must comply with consumer protection law. The guidance was published on 30 January 2026; the underlying law took effect on 6 April 2025.

title: Unregulated legal services: complying with consumer law
summary: The CMA updated guidance for unregulated providers of will writing, online divorce and pre-paid probate services on how to comply with consumer law. It reflects changes from the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024, which took effect on 6 April 2025. This is relevant to firms offering these services and their legal/compliance teams.

title: Consumer experience of private dental services
summary: The CMA closed a call for evidence for its market study into private dental services in the UK. It sought views from consumers and UK dental professionals on service experiences, choice drivers and payment for private treatment. The call ran from 5 March 2026 at 7am to 19 March 2026 at 5pm.

title: Dental professional experience of private dental services
summary: The CMA opened a closed call for evidence as part of a market study into the supply of private dental services in the UK. Dental professionals and consumers were asked for views on the sector, including services provided, challenges faced and how consumers choose treatments. The call for evidence ran from 5 March 2026 to 19 March 2026.

title: CMA launches review of private dentistry
summary: The CMA has launched a market study into private dentistry and published a proposed scope, inviting views and consumer/dental professional input. It will examine access, prices, competition, complaints/redress and sector regulation, and may lead to recommendations or other action. No direct obligations are created for firms, but private dentistry providers should monitor the review and any follow-on measures.

title: Referral of the proposed Post Office Remediation Unit and Horizon IT Inquiry 2026 to 2027 and IR35 liability costs subsidy by the Department for Business and Trade
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its report on DBT’s proposed subsidy for Post Office Limited’s Remediation Unit, Horizon IT Inquiry work, and historic IR35 liability settlement. It is an advisory report under the Subsidy Control Act 2022, with third-party submissions already closed by the time of publication. No direct obligations are created for regulated firms.

title: Vets market investigation: consultation on provisional decision
summary: The CMA has published a consultation on its provisional findings and proposed remedies in the veterinary market investigation. It proposes new requirements on price transparency, written estimates and bills, pet plans, complaints handling, medicine pricing and out-of-hours contracts for veterinary businesses. This is a consultation, so firms in scope should review and respond by the consultation deadline if one is set elsewhere in the publication.

title: Commitments made in respect of aspects of Apple's mobile platform
summary: The CMA publication records Apple commitments for iOS and iPadOS app review, App Store search, third-party data use and interoperability requests. Apple will follow the commitments from 1 April 2026, with multiple reporting schedules and the first annual metrics for UK-based app developers due by 31 May 2026. The commitments set expectations for app review transparency, timing and handling of interoperability requests.

title: Commitments made in respect of aspects of Google’s mobile platform
summary: The CMA published commitments from Google about its mobile platform app review process for UK developers. The commitments include fair, transparent and non-discriminatory review, an annual UK transparency report, developer engagement, better dispute resolution visibility, and reporting to the CMA. They are intended to take effect from 1 April 2026.

title: Report on the proposed Bus Network Support Grant subsidy scheme by West Midlands Combined Authority
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a non-binding report on West Midlands Combined Authority’s proposed Bus Network Support Grant subsidy scheme. It finds the assessment broadly adequate but highlights areas for improvement in the subsidy control analysis under several principles and in the SPEI requirements. No compliance date or binding obligation is set out in the report.

title: Civil engineering market study
summary: The CMA has launched a market study into civil engineering for roads and railways, inviting representations by 17 July 2025. It will publish a market study report no later than 18 June 2026, with potential further consultation if a market investigation reference is proposed. This is relevant for firms exposed to UK infrastructure, transport or construction markets.

title: CMA recommends overhaul of road and rail procurement to cut costs and drive economic growth through infrastructure investment
summary: The CMA published a market study press release on road and rail infrastructure procurement, recommending government-led reforms to improve long-term planning, procurement and delivery. It is not a financial-services rule or supervisory notice, but it may be of general interest to firms involved in public procurement or infrastructure. The UK Government is expected to respond within 90 days.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy to EP Lynemouth Power Limited by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its final report on DESNZ’s proposed subsidy for EP Lynemouth Power Limited under the Subsidy Control Act 2022. It evaluates DESNZ’s assessment of compliance for a proposed 4-year Low Carbon Dispatchable CfD arrangement, with third-party submissions referenced in the timetable. No direct obligations are created for firms in this publication.

title: Digital Regulation Cooperation Forum workplan 2022 to 2023
primary_functions: Compliance; Financial crime; Risk; Product; Operational resilience; Privacy; Regulatory change
summary: The ICO and partner regulators published the DRCF workplan for 2022 to 2023, setting out joint digital-regulation priorities on coherence, collaboration and capability building. It highlights projects on children’s online privacy and safety, online advertising, algorithmic transparency and innovation. This is a planning document with no direct requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: Findings from the DRCF Algorithmic Processing workstream - Spring 2022
summary: The ICO and other DRCF members published two discussion papers on algorithmic processing: the benefits and harms of algorithms, and the current landscape for algorithmic auditing. They also launched a call for input asking stakeholders to respond by 2022-06-08, and later published a summary of responses and next steps. This is an awareness-only publication for firms using or developing algorithmic systems.

title: Request for regulators to publish an update on their strategic approach to AI: Secretary of State letters
summary: The UK government asked a set of regulators, including the ICO and FCA, to publish by 30 April 2024 an update on their strategic approach to AI and how they are applying the AI Regulation White Paper principles. This is a correspondence/announcement rather than a rule, guidance or binding requirement. Banks are only indirectly in scope through the FCA letter and wider AI governance expectations.

title: Cochlear / Oticon merger inquiry
summary: CMA notice that the merger notice for Cochlear Limited’s planned acquisition of Demant A/S’s Oticon Medical business meets the statutory filing requirements under the Enterprise Act. It starts the CMA’s initial period from 12 October 2022 and sets the Phase 2 referral decision deadline as 6 December 2022.

title: Referral of the proposed Sizewell C Devex scheme by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ)
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a report on DESNZ’s proposed Sizewell C Development Expenditure scheme. It evaluates DESNZ’s assessment of compliance with the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and invites third-party submissions on the report process. This is an advisory publication about a government subsidy scheme, not a binding rule or obligation for firms.

title: Referral of the proposed Sizewell C Final Investment Decision (FID) scheme by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ) and UK Infrastructure Bank (UKIB)
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its report on DESNZ and UKIB’s proposed Sizewell C Final Investment Decision scheme. It reviews the proposed subsidy arrangement for the nuclear project and invites any third-party submissions by the timetable date stated in the document. This is an advisory publication, not a rule or enforcement notice.

title: Referral of the proposed Energy Intensive Industry (EII) Businesses Exemption from Nuclear Regulated Asset Base (RAB) Policy Costs subsidy scheme by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ) and the Department for Business and Trade (DBT)
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its final report on DESNZ and DBT’s proposed Energy Intensive Industry exemption from Nuclear RAB policy costs. It explains the scheme and invites third-party submissions on the assessment of compliance, with comments due by the timetable date in the notice. This is an intelligence/publication item, not a rule or enforcement notice.

title: Referral of the proposed Social Housing Decarbonisation Fund Wave 3 by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its report on DESNZ’s proposed Social Housing Decarbonisation Fund Wave 3. It evaluates DESNZ’s assessment of compliance under the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and invited third-party submissions by the timetable date. The scheme concerns grant funding for social housing energy-efficiency and low-carbon heating measures, with delivery expected to run to September 2028.

title: AlphaTheta / Serato merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has issued a merger notice for the anticipated acquisition of Serato by AlphaTheta and says its initial review period starts on 5 March 2024. The CMA’s deadline to announce whether it will refer the merger for a phase 2 investigation is 1 May 2024.

title: Joint Statement on competition in generative AI foundation models and AI products
summary: The UK, EU and US competition authorities issued a joint statement on competition in generative AI foundation models and AI products. It sets out principles to support competition, protect consumers and help businesses innovate, building on the CMA’s earlier AI foundation models work. This is an awareness item for firms developing or using AI products; no deadline or direct rule change is stated.

title: Interim road fuel monitoring update: July 2024
summary: The CMA published its third interim road fuel monitoring update, summarising fuel prices, retail spreads and margins, and progress on the road fuel market study recommendations. It notes the voluntary price data-sharing scheme is insufficient and encourages government to implement the statutory monitoring and open data schemes when legislation is in place. No direct obligations are created for firms.

title: Consumer law court proceedings: notifying the CMA
summary: This CMA guidance explains how parties to private consumer law court proceedings should notify the CMA, especially where the case raises novel or widely applicable legal issues. It is informational only and does not create new obligations.

title: OIM launches study of regulatory restrictions on single-use plastics
summary: The CMA published its 2024/25 Annual Plan, setting out its strategy, priorities and areas of focus for the year ahead, including how it will use its competition and consumer powers and the new responsibilities from the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Bill. It is an informational planning document, not a rule or enforcement notice.

title: Thermo Fisher Scientific / Olink merger inquiry
summary: The CMA issued a notice under the Enterprise Act confirming the merger notice for Thermo Fisher Scientific’s proposed acquisition of Olink meets statutory requirements. It also states the CMA’s initial review period and the deadline for a phase 2 referral decision. This is relevant for firms monitoring UK merger control, but it does not create direct obligations for the bank.

title: Scanpole / C&G merger inquiry
summary: The CMA published a merger notice for the anticipated acquisition of Calders & Grandidge (Boston) Limited by Scanpole Limited. It confirms the initial period starts on 26 June 2024 and says the CMA’s deadline to decide on a phase 2 referral is 20 August 2024.

title: CMA response to airport slot allocation system reform consultation
summary: The CMA published its response to a government consultation on airport slot allocation reform. It supports market-based mechanisms, such as auctions and trading, to improve competition and efficiency in the aviation sector. This is an advisory response only and does not itself create obligations.

title: Investigation into suspected anti-competitive conduct by Google
summary: The CMA announced it has closed its Google Play Billing investigation under the Competition Act 1998 on administrative priority grounds. It said this is not a finding of infringement and that it may still use its new DMCC Act powers or other tools in future. No immediate action or compliance deadline is set out.

title: CMA looks to new digital markets competition regime to resolve app store concerns
summary: The CMA says it has closed its Competition Act cases into Google Play Store and Apple App Store and will instead consider app-store concerns under the new digital markets regime once it comes into force. It also rejects Google’s proposed commitments. The CMA says it expects to launch around 3 to 4 SMS investigations in the first year, but has not named firms or activities yet.

title: Roche / LumiraDx merger inquiry
summary: CMA published a merger notice for Roche Diagnostics’ acquisition of certain LumiraDx assets. It says the initial review period starts on 24 May 2024 and the CMA’s phase 2 reference decision deadline is 19 July 2024. This is a market/competition notice, not a financial-services rule or enforcement action.

title: Referral of the proposed Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) Brownfield Housing scheme
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a report on Greater Manchester Combined Authority’s proposed Brownfield Housing Scheme. It evaluates GMCA’s assessment under the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and invites third-party comments by the deadline in the timetable. The scheme concerns housing and brownfield development in Greater Manchester.

title: Sugar deal cleared by CMA
summary: The CMA announced it has cleared T&L Sugars’ acquisition of Tereos UK & Ireland’s retail sugar business after a Phase 2 investigation. The decision followed a consultation on provisional findings and is a merger-control outcome, not a rule or obligation for firms.

title: CMA launches investigation into Ticketmaster over Oasis concert sales
summary: CMA press release says it has opened an investigation into Ticketmaster over Oasis ticket sales and possible misuse of dynamic pricing, and invites fans to submit evidence by 2024-09-19. It also notes wider work on ticketing and dynamic pricing, but does not itself impose new requirements.

title: Report on the proposed Net Zero Hydrogen Fund (NZHF) Carbon Capture Use and Storage (CCUS) Scheme by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ)
summary: CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a non-binding report on DESNZ’s proposed Strand 4 Net Zero Hydrogen Fund scheme for CCUS-enabled hydrogen projects. It evaluates the subsidy control assessment and describes the selected projects, but does not create obligations for firms. No action deadline is set in the report.

title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company / Juniper Networks, Inc. merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a merger notice for Hewlett Packard Enterprise Company’s anticipated acquisition of Juniper Networks, Inc. The notice starts the initial merger-review period on 20 June 2024 and sets 14 August 2024 as the deadline for the CMA to decide whether to refer the deal to a phase 2 investigation.

title: Greenwashing: CMA issues tailored guide for fashion brands
summary: The CMA published a press release and tailored guide for fashion brands on making accurate green claims under consumer law. It also said it had written to 17 brands and reminded them of forthcoming stronger consumer enforcement powers under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024. This is awareness material rather than a binding rule or notice.

title: Tereos fined for failure to comply with CMA merger procedures
summary: The CMA announced a £25,000 fine on Tereos for failing to provide full information during a merger inquiry under section 109 of the Enterprise Act 2002. It also noted that future maximum fixed penalties for this type of breach will rise to 1% of worldwide turnover when DMCCA amendments come into force. This is a press release, not the enforcement notice itself.

title: Open letter to unregulated legal services providers
summary: The CMA issued an open letter to unregulated providers of will writing, online divorce and pre-paid probate services, reminding them of existing UK consumer law obligations and pointing them to CMA compliance guidance. It is aimed at businesses offering these services and does not itself create new requirements.

title: What to consider when buying will writing services
summary: CMA guidance explains what consumers should consider when buying will writing services, including differences between providers, what to look for, and where to get help if things go wrong. It is informational only and does not impose any new requirements. No deadline or in-force date is stated.

title: Macquarie Asset Management / Last Mile Infrastructure merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a merger notice for Macquarie Asset Management’s anticipated acquisition of a jointly controlling 50% interest in Last Mile Infrastructure Holdings Limited. It starts the CMA’s initial merger period on 22 July 2024 and sets 16 September 2024 as the deadline for the CMA’s phase 2 referral decision.

title: CMA response to Scottish Law Commission report on review of contract law consultation
summary: The CMA published a response to the Scottish Law Commission’s consultation on contract law, updating it on consumer protection developments, especially the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024. It explains how new CMA direct enforcement powers and related changes to consumer law could indirectly affect contract-law enforcement in Scotland. No new obligations are created by this response itself.

title: CMA response to Northern Ireland Department of Education School Uniform Policy Consultation
summary: The CMA published its response to the Northern Ireland Department of Education’s consultation on school uniform policy. It supports statutory guidance to help reduce uniform costs and warns that price controls can create unintended consequences, offering design considerations if such controls are pursued. This is an advisory consultation response, not a binding rule, and no compliance date is set.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy to Plymouth Citybus Limited by Plymouth City Council
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its report on Plymouth City Council’s proposed subsidy to Plymouth Citybus Limited for zero-emission buses and charging infrastructure. The report evaluates the council’s assessment of compliance under the Subsidy Control Act 2022. Third-party submissions were invited by the date in the timetable; this is a market-specific public report, not a rule change.

title: CMA response to the Welsh Government consultation on inspection ratings for care home services and domiciliary support services
summary: The CMA published a response to the Welsh Government’s consultation on inspection ratings for care home services and domiciliary support services. It supports publishing and displaying inspection ratings, but says ratings alone may not be enough for informed care-home choices and points back to its 2017 care homes market study recommendations. No direct obligations are created for firms.

title: T&L Sugars/Tereos merger inquiry
summary: The CMA published a merger-inquiry notice for the anticipated acquisition by T&L Sugars Limited of certain Tereos UK and Ireland assets. It states the initial period starts on 15 January 2024 and the CMA’s deadline to decide on a Phase 2 reference is 8 March 2024. This is informational for firms watching UK merger control.

title: Referral of the proposed Welsh Freeports Subsidy Scheme by the Welsh Government (WG) and the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG)
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a report on the Welsh Government and MHCLG’s proposed Welsh Freeports Subsidy Scheme. It describes the scheme, the SAU’s assessment under the Subsidy Control Act 2022, and invites third-party submissions on the report by the stated timetable date. This is an intelligence/publication item, not a rule or enforcement notice.

title: Logistics deal could raise prices for business customers in the UK
summary: The CMA issued a press release saying its Phase 1 merger review of GXO’s completed acquisition of Wincanton raises competition concerns in UK mainstream contract logistics services. GXO has 5 working days to offer remedies, otherwise the CMA may move to Phase 2. The notice concerns market structure, not a rule or obligation for regulated firms.

title: The SAU referrals process: information for public authorities
summary: CMA guidance explains how public authorities should refer subsidies or subsidy schemes to the Subsidy Advice Unit (SAU), including mandatory and voluntary referrals, pre-referral discussions, and use of the Public Authority Portal. It describes the SAU’s role, acceptance process, and report timings, but does not create new rules for firms.

title: Fast Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG)
summary: The CMA says it has closed its investigation into Unilever UK Limited’s environmental claims on household goods, noting changes made by the company and wider impact of its work on green claims. It also restates that businesses should comply with consumer law and read the Green Claims Code. The publication is a press-release/update, not a new rule or enforcement notice.

title: CMA publishes interim report in corporate travel merger
summary: The CMA published a press release on its interim report in the GBT/CWT corporate travel merger, provisionally finding the deal could substantially lessen competition. Interested parties are invited to respond to the provisional findings by 27 November 2024.

title: Infant formula: CMA sets out concerns and potential solutions
summary: The CMA published an interim report on the infant formula market, highlighting concerns about pricing, branding, labelling and the effects of current regulations. It seeks feedback on provisional findings and potential remedies, with a consultation to inform final recommendations expected in early 2025. This is a press release summarising a market review, not a binding rule or supervisory notice.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy to Cromarty Firth Port Authority by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ)
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a report advising DESNZ on its proposed subsidy to Cromarty Firth Port Authority for a floating offshore wind port facility. It is part of the subsidy control assessment process and invited third-party submissions by the timetable date. No direct obligations are created for regulated firms.

title: CMA tips: How to navigate finding a ‘recommended’ trader online
summary: The CMA published consumer tips and finalised advice for trader recommendation sites on how to comply with consumer law, alongside a short crib sheet. It is aimed at sites and consumers, with no specific compliance deadline stated. The CMA says it will monitor the sector and may take further action if needed.

title: Avoid and report anti-competitive activity
summary: The CMA published general guidance for all businesses on avoiding and reporting anti-competitive activity such as cartels, bid rigging and abuse of dominance. It explains the risks and penalties, and suggests using policies, training and legal advice. No new obligations or deadlines are created in this publication.

title: Theramex/European Rights to Viatris’ Femoston and Duphaston products
summary: The CMA grants consent/derogation under an Initial Enforcement Order in the Theramex/Viatris transaction. The parties may exclude non-UK assets from certain hold-separate obligations, while preserving the UK Femoston business and its supply, approvals, IP and resources until the CMA varies or withdraws the order.

title: Spreadex required to sell Sporting Index
summary: The CMA issued a press release saying Spreadex must sell Sporting Index after a Phase 2 merger investigation found the deal harmed competition in UK licensed online sports spread betting. The CMA said it now has 12 weeks to accept undertakings or make a final order, and it will monitor remedy implementation.

title: Review of loyalty pricing in the groceries sector
summary: The CMA published a research and analysis report on loyalty pricing in the groceries sector. It says its review found loyalty scheme members can usually make genuine savings on usual prices and summarises consumer survey findings. This is an informational publication for supermarkets and shoppers, with no new rules or deadlines.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy to Barking and Dagenham Homes Limited by the London Borough of Barking and Dagenham Council
summary: The CMA Subsidy Advice Unit published a report on a proposed subsidy from Barking and Dagenham Council to Barking and Dagenham Homes Limited for affordable housing. The report evaluates the council’s assessment under the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and invites third-party submissions by the stated deadline in the timetable. This is informational and does not itself create obligations for firms.

title: Interim road fuel monitoring update: November 2024
summary: The CMA published an interim update on road fuel prices, retail spreads and margins, using voluntary data from fuel retailers. It also notes that statutory monitoring powers under the DMCC Act are expected to commence by January 2025, but this publication itself is only an update and does not create obligations.

title: CMA letter to PHIN welcoming achievement of bronze compliance milestone
summary: The CMA published a letter congratulating PHIN and the private healthcare sector on reaching the Bronze Milestone under the Private Healthcare Market Investigation Order 2014. It also notes future milestones in September 2025 and June 2026 and says the CMA will continue enforcement against non-compliant parties.

title: Muller Dairy (UK) Limited / Yew Tree Dairy Holdings Limited merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a merger notice for Müller Dairy UK’s anticipated acquisition of Yew Tree Dairy Holdings under the Enterprise Act 2002. It starts the CMA’s initial review period on 28 August 2024 and states the CMA’s phase 2 referral decision deadline as 22 October 2024. This is a competition-law perimeter notice, not a financial-services rule change.

title: NHS set to benefit from £23 million following CMA pharma probe
summary: The CMA issued a press release saying Vifor Pharma has offered commitments, including a £23 million payment and corrective communications, to resolve competition concerns about misleading claims on iron deficiency treatments. The CMA will consult on the proposed commitments until 17 January 2025 before deciding whether to accept them.

title: XSYS / MGS merger inquiry
summary: The CMA published a merger notice for the anticipated acquisition of MacDermid Graphics Solutions by XSYS, confirming the merger notice meets Enterprise Act requirements. It starts the initial review period on 22 October 2024 and sets 16 December 2024 as the CMA’s deadline to decide whether to refer the merger for a phase 2 investigation.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy to CalMac Ferries Limited by Transport Scotland
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a final report on Transport Scotland’s proposed subsidy to CalMac Ferries Limited for Clyde and Hebrides Ferry Services. It evaluates Transport Scotland’s assessment under the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and notes the request was for a Subsidy of Particular Interest. Third-party submissions were due under the administrative timetable.

title: Report on the Extension Awards over £1 million subsidy scheme by Arts Council England
summary: CMA Subsidy Advice Unit report giving non-binding advice on Arts Council England’s proposed Extension Awards over £1 million subsidy scheme. It comments on ACE’s assessment under the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and suggests improvements, but does not make rules or impose obligations. The scheme is proposed for arts and culture organisations in England; no compliance date is set.

title: Referral of the proposed Extension Awards over £1 million subsidy scheme by Arts Council England
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a report on Arts Council England’s proposed Extension Awards over £1 million subsidy scheme. It assesses ACE’s subsidy-control compliance for this proposed scheme and invites third-party submissions. This is a closed case and does not itself change rules or impose obligations on firms.

title: Referral of the proposed Contracts for Difference Clean Industry Bonus Subsidy by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a report advising DESNZ on its proposed Contracts for Difference Clean Industry Bonus subsidy scheme. It is an intelligence/update item about a subsidy control referral, not a new rule. The scheme is planned for Allocation Round 7, with the first CIB allocation round expected to open for applications in 2025.

title: Quick guide to UK merger assessment: CMA18
summary: The CMA published a quick guide summarising the UK merger control regime, including jurisdiction tests, notification process, review stages and remedies. It is a non-binding overview for businesses considering mergers; no new rules or deadlines are created. It points readers to more detailed CMA guidance for the operative requirements.

title: DBT and CMA memorandum of understanding: international cooperation
summary: The CMA and DBT published a memorandum of understanding on international cooperation for competition and consumer law enforcement. It sets out expectations, roles and responsibilities for information disclosure, investigative assistance to overseas regulators, and other cooperation arrangements under the DMCC Act. No firm action date or direct requirement is set out in this notice.

title: CMA sets out initial plans as new digital markets competition regime comes into force
summary: The CMA issued a press release setting out its initial plans for the new digital markets competition regime, which came into force on 1 January 2025. It says it expects to launch SMS investigations into three areas of digital activity in the first six months and may consult on proposed conduct requirements in parallel. This is an update on implementation and planned enforcement activity, not a binding rule change.

title: CMA response to Northern Ireland Department for the Economy support for low carbon heating in the residential sector consultation
summary: The CMA published a response to a Northern Ireland Department for the Economy consultation on support for low-carbon heating in the residential sector. It argues for consumer protection measures alongside government funding and highlights risks from mis-selling, poor-quality installations and weak redress. It is an intelligence item with no direct obligations or compliance date.

title: Response from CMA Chair and CEO to correspondence from government
summary: CMA Chair and CEO wrote to government setting out the CMA’s draft 2025/26 Annual Plan and medium-term priorities. It says the draft plan is out for consultation and outlines intended work on competition, consumer protection, digital markets and sector investigations over the next 12 months. No direct obligations are created for firms in this letter.

title: CMA to investigate Google’s search services
summary: CMA press release announcing a new investigation into whether Google has strategic market status in UK search and search advertising under the digital markets competition regime. It says the investigation may lead to conduct requirements, and the CMA expects to decide by October 2025. This is an update on regulatory activity, not a binding rule or notice for firms.

title: Public Transport Ticketing Schemes Block Exemption: proposed recommendation
summary: The CMA published a proposed recommendation on whether the Public Transport Ticketing Schemes Block Exemption should continue, be varied, or expire in 2026. It follows an earlier consultation and asks the Secretary of State for Business and Trade to accept a recommendation to keep the exemption without a fixed duration, with some limited changes. No direct obligations are created for firms.

title: Subsidy Advice Unit consultation response regarding the UK subsidy control regime
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a consultation response on the UK subsidy control regime, analysing whether the current mandatory referral threshold for Subsidies of Particular Interest should change and whether streamlined routes should be introduced. It does not create new rules; it informs DBT’s consultation and future policy decisions. No action date is stated in the publication.

title: Data protection
summary: ICO guidance page summarises UK data protection law, the UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018, and the main principles and individual rights around personal data. It is an informational webpage for the public and organisations, with no new rules, dates or deadlines.

title: Undertakings in lieu of reference form
summary: The CMA has published a Remedies Form for merger parties offering undertakings in lieu of reference under the Enterprise Act 2002. It sets out the information the CMA expects on the proposed divestment, the business to be divested and how the remedy addresses the competition concern. It is not a rule change, but it is the template parties use when preparing a UIL submission.

title: Merger enquiry letter template
summary: The CMA has published an updated merger enquiry letter template used when it opens an investigation into an unnotified merger. It reflects changes to the mergers regime under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024. This is a guidance/template publication, not a binding notice, and it does not set a firm deadline for firms.

title: How the UK’s digital markets competition regime works
summary: CMA guidance explains the UK digital markets competition regime, including how firms may be designated with strategic market status, conduct requirements, pro-competition interventions, and merger reporting rules for SMS firms. It is an overview document, not a new rule or decision. No immediate compliance deadline is stated in the publication.

title: CMA to investigate Apple and Google's mobile ecosystems
summary: The CMA has opened press-release announced strategic market status investigations into Apple and Google’s mobile ecosystems, including operating systems, app stores and browsers. The CMA will gather evidence from stakeholders and decide by end of October 2025 whether either firm has SMS and whether conduct requirements should follow. This is informational for firms developing apps or mobile-related services.

title: Carlsberg / Britvic merger inquiry
summary: The CMA published a merger notice for Carlsberg UK Holdings Limited’s anticipated acquisition of Britvic PLC. It confirms the merger notice meets statutory requirements and starts the CMA initial review period on 24 October 2024, with a phase 2 referral deadline of 18 December 2024.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy to Berkeley Homes (East Thames) Limited by Homes England
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its report on Homes England’s proposed £29.4m subsidy to Berkeley Homes (East Thames) Limited for the Lombard Square development. It explains the assessment of compliance, invites third-party submissions by the stated deadline, and notes the subsidy is a Subsidy of Particular Interest under the Subsidy Control Act 2022.

title: Study into regulatory restrictions on single-use plastics in the United Kingdom
summary: The CMA’s Office for the Internal Market published a completed study and final report on the impact of current and future single-use plastic restrictions in the UK. It is an informational market study, not a rule, consultation, or enforcement notice. The report was published on 12 February 2025.

title: Infant formula: CMA outlines clear path forward to help parents save hundreds of pounds a year
summary: CMA issued a press release on its final recommendations after a market study of infant and follow-on formula. It urges UK governments to improve information, labelling, advertising and enforcement to help parents compare products and save money. This is a policy recommendation rather than a binding rule change, and no compliance date is set.

title: CMA provisionally clears poultry feed merger
summary: The CMA issued a press release saying its independent inquiry group has provisionally cleared Boparan’s proposed purchase of ForFarmers’ Burston and Radstock feed mill sites after a Phase 2 merger investigation. It is seeking feedback on the interim report by 11 March 2025, with a final decision due by 13 May 2025.

title: Co-op re-writes anti-competitive land agreements
summary: The CMA issued a press release saying Co-op admitted 107 breaches of the Groceries Market Investigation (Controlled Land) Order 2010 and is resolving the remaining issues. It also says the CMA is continuing targeted enforcement of similar land-agreement breaches across major grocers. This is relevant for firms with competition-law exposure, but it does not itself create new requirements.

title: Open letter to Co-op about land agreements restricting competition
summary: The CMA published an open letter to Co-op saying it had breached the Groceries Market Investigation (Controlled Land) Order 2010 on 107 occasions, with 3 breaches still ongoing. Co-op is expected to fix the outstanding breaches and will now report annually to the CMA on compliance with the Order.

title: Referral of the proposed Affordable Housing Delivery Scheme by the Welsh Government
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a report on the Welsh Government’s proposed Affordable Housing Delivery Scheme. The report assesses the scheme’s compliance with the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and invites third-party submissions, with the scheme due to run from 20 March 2025 to 31 March 2031.

title: Global Business Travel Group, Inc / CWT Holdings, LLC merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a notice confirming that the merger notice for Global Business Travel Group’s anticipated acquisition of CWT Holdings meets statutory requirements. It also states the merger review period starts on 5 June 2024 and that the CMA’s phase 2 referral decision deadline is 30 July 2024.

title: Cérélia / Jus-Rol merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has made an Initial Enforcement Order under the Enterprise Act in the Cérélia/Jus-Rol merger inquiry. It restricts integration, asset transfers, information sharing and management changes while the CMA reviews the transaction. The order applies to Cérélia and took effect on 3 February 2022; breach may lead to penalties.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy to Vivid Housing Limited for Victory Quay, Portsmouth by Homes England
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a report on Homes England’s proposed £19.794 million subsidy to Vivid Housing Limited for the Victory Quay redevelopment in Portsmouth. It assesses compliance with the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and notes the project qualifies as a Subsidy of Particular Interest. Third-party submissions were invited for the report process; no direct obligations are created for banks.

title: Outbrain Inc. / Teads S.A. / Altice Teads S.A. merger inquiry
summary: The CMA issued a merger notice for the anticipated acquisition of Teads S.A. by Outbrain Inc., and for Altice Teads S.A.’s minority shareholding in Outbrain Inc. It starts the CMA’s initial review period on 9 December 2024 and gives a phase 2 referral decision deadline of 5 February 2025. No direct obligations are imposed on financial firms.

title: BlackRock / Preqin merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a merger notice for BlackRock’s anticipated acquisition of Preqin and stated the phase 1 initial period start and referral deadline. This is a competition-law market notice affecting the parties to the transaction, not a regulatory rule change for firms generally.

title: CMA response to the UK government’s consultation on the resale of live events tickets
summary: The CMA published a response to the UK government’s consultation on resale of live events tickets. It gives the CMA’s views on design issues for any resale price cap or licensing regime, and notes the sector still needs legislative change. This is advisory only and does not itself change rules or create deadlines.

title: Referral of the proposed (Remediation Unit and Horizon IT Inquiry) subsidy to Post Office Limited by the Department for Business and Trade
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its report on DBT’s proposed £57.9 million subsidy to Post Office Limited for Horizon redress and inquiry-related costs in FY2025/26. It is a final advisory report, not a rule or obligation for firms. Third-party submissions were part of the process before publication.

title: CMA’s Annual Plan to drive growth by promoting competition, protecting consumers and enhancing business and investor confidence
summary: The CMA published its 2025 to 2026 Annual Plan, setting out its priorities for competition, consumer protection, growth and improved internal processes. It highlights use of new powers under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act and a focus on digital markets, consumer protection, and bid-rigging enforcement. This is an awareness-only plan, not a binding rule or notice.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy to The Auckland Project by Durham County Council
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a report on Durham County Council’s proposed £28m subsidy to The Auckland Project. It evaluates the council’s assessment under the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and invites third-party submissions for the report process. No direct obligations are created for firms.

title: Referral of the modified Capacity Market scheme by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its final report on the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero’s proposed amended Capacity Market scheme. It explains the scheme and the SAU’s evaluation of DESNZ’s subsidy-control assessment, with a public submissions process already closed. This is an advisory publication about an energy subsidy scheme, not a regulatory rule for financial firms.

title: Informal guidance on Builders Merchants Federation’s supply chain initiative
summary: The CMA published informal guidance on the Builders Merchants Federation’s proposed supply chain assurance initiative, explaining how the CMA’s Green Agreements Guidance applies to the proposal. It is guidance only and does not itself change the law or impose new requirements. The CMA also notes firms should consider the Green Claims Code if they make environmental claims.

title: Road fuel quarterly update report: March 2025
summary: The CMA published its first quarterly road fuel monitoring update under the DMCC Act framework. It summarises recent petrol and diesel prices, spreads and margins, notes the statutory monitoring function started in January 2025, and says the next monitoring report is expected in June 2025. It also updates progress on Fuel Finder, which the government aims to launch by end-2025.

title: IBM / HashiCorp merger inquiry
summary: The CMA issued a merger notice for IBM’s anticipated acquisition of HashiCorp and confirmed the initial review period under the Enterprise Act 2002 starts on 31 December 2024. The CMA’s phase 2 referral deadline is 25 February 2025. This is a competition-law market notice, not a financial-services rule change.

title: William Grant & Sons / The Famous Grouse merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a merger notice for William Grant & Sons’ anticipated acquisition of The Famous Grouse, Naked Malt and related brands. It starts the initial merger review period on 30 January 2025 and states the CMA’s phase 2 referral decision deadline as 27 March 2025. This is a competition-law process notice, not a financial-services rule change.

title: CMA to boost consumer and business confidence as new consumer protection regime comes into force
summary: The CMA has issued a press release on the new consumer protection regime under the DMCCA 2024, which came into force on 6 April 2025. It says it will take a proportionate approach, publish guidance, and begin enforcement on the most serious practices such as fake reviews, drip pricing, hidden fees and unfair terms. This is informational rather than a rule-making or enforcement notice.

title: DBT-CMA joint statement on consumer protection
summary: The CMA and DBT published a joint policy statement on consumer protection after provisions in the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act commenced. It explains the CMA’s planned approach to using its new consumer-protection powers and how this aligns with government priorities. No action date or firm-specific requirement is set out.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy to First Hampshire & Dorset Limited by Portsmouth City Council
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its final report on Portsmouth City Council’s proposed subsidy to First Hampshire & Dorset Limited for zero-emission buses and charging infrastructure. The report evaluates the council’s assessment of compliance with the Subsidy Control Act 2022. Third parties could submit comments during the timetable set out in the notice.

title: Microsoft / OpenAI partnership merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has issued an invitation to comment on Microsoft’s partnership with OpenAI, asking interested parties to submit views and evidence on whether the arrangement creates a relevant merger situation and affects UK competition. This is an initial information-gathering step ahead of any possible phase 1 investigation, with comments invited by 3 January 2024.

title: Referral of the proposed West Midlands Bus Network Support Grant scheme by West Midlands Combined Authority
summary: The CMA Subsidy Advice Unit published a report on West Midlands Combined Authority’s proposed bus network support grant. It evaluates the authority’s assessment of compliance with the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and invites third-party submissions. The scheme is due to run from 1 May 2025 to 31 December 2025, with a possible extension to April 2026.

title: Report on the proposed West Midlands Bus Network Support Grant scheme
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a non-binding report on West Midlands Combined Authority’s proposed Bus Network Support Grant scheme. It evaluates the authority’s assessment against the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and identifies areas for improvement in the scheme’s evidence and analysis. There are no direct obligations on firms, only advisory findings for the public authority.

title: Chancellor unveils plans to maintain level playing field for British business
summary: HMT issued a press release announcing support for British business through stronger action on unfair trade practices, improved trade monitoring, and a planned review of the customs treatment of low-value imports. It also says the TRA will increase resources and speed up responses to unfair import surges. No immediate regulatory obligation is created for firms.

title: Referral of the proposed Post Office (Future Technology Portfolio 2025 to 2026) subsidy by the Department for Business and Trade
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its final report on DBT’s proposed Post Office Future Technology Portfolio 2025-2026 subsidy. It assesses DBT’s compliance with the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and concerns a proposed £136 million grant for Post Office IT replacement and transformation through to the end of 2025-26. Third-party submissions were invited during the reporting process.

title: Valuation Office Agency scrapped in government drive to slash inefficiencies
summary: HMT announced that the Valuation Office Agency will be brought into HMRC by April 2026, alongside a wider tax simplification package. The package also includes planned legislation to change the VAT Capital Goods Scheme, a consultation on VAT relief for donated goods, and a new flat fee for spirit drink verification from 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2031.

title: Referral of the proposed network subsidy to Post Office Limited by the Department for Business and Trade
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a report on 28 April 2025 advising the Department for Business and Trade on its proposed Network Subsidy to Post Office Limited. The report evaluates the government’s assessment of compliance with the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and invites any third-party submissions by the timetable in the publication. It is an advisory publication, not a rule or decision.

title: Report on the proposed network subsidy to Post Office Limited by the Department for Business and Trade
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a non-binding report on a proposed network subsidy from the Department for Business and Trade to Post Office Limited. It evaluates the subsidy against the Subsidy Control Act principles and highlights areas for improvement in the assessment, but it does not decide whether the subsidy may be given.

title: The CMA's approach to the new consumer enforcement regime
summary: The CMA published an update explaining how it prioritises its work under its principles, including strategy alignment, impact, alternative bodies, resources and risk. It is general guidance on internal decision-making rather than a rule or sector-specific requirement, and it does not set a compliance deadline for firms.

title: Iberdrola / NWEN merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has made an Initial Order in the Iberdrola/NWEN merger inquiry under the Enterprise Act 2002. It restricts integration and requires the businesses to remain separate, preserve assets, staff, IT and information flows, pending the CMA’s final determination. It applies from completion of the merger and continues during the specified period.

title: Report on the Subsidy to Kishorn Port Limited by Highlands and Islands Enterprise
summary: CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a non-binding report on Highlands and Islands Enterprise’s proposed subsidy to Kishorn Port Limited. It evaluates HIE’s assessment under the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and suggests improvements, but does not decide whether the subsidy may be granted. The report was published on 2025-05-09 and has no direct obligations for firms.

title: Pension schemes back British growth
summary: HMT announces the Mansion House Accord, under which 17 workplace pension providers will voluntarily aim to invest 10% of workplace portfolios in productive assets by 2030, including 5% in the UK. The press release says this could unlock up to £50 billion for UK businesses and infrastructure and will be followed by measures in the Pensions Investment Review final report.

title: CMA response to the Independent Water Commission's call for evidence
summary: The CMA published its response to the Independent Water Commission’s call for evidence, recommending reform of regulatory appeals and redeterminations, including moving appeals from redeterminations and potentially transferring appeal hearings to a judicial body. It is an intelligence/public consultation response from the CMA, not a binding rule or supervisory notice. No direct obligations are created for firms.

title: Consumer protection in green heating and insulation sector
summary: The CMA has launched a call for information on consumer protection in the green heating and insulation sector, covering products such as heat pumps, solar, insulation, biomass boilers and hydrogen-ready boilers. It seeks evidence from consumers, businesses and stakeholders about consumer experiences, business practices and any barriers or harms. This is an information-gathering exercise, not a binding rule or enforcement action.

title: Pension plan to double £25 billion+ megafunds, boost investment and improve returns for savers
summary: HMT issued a press release announcing planned pensions reforms to create larger DC megafunds, require LGPS pooling by March 2026, and enable new investment and transfer powers through the forthcoming Pension Schemes Bill. It also says local investment targets will be set for LGPS authorities and references a reserve power for binding asset allocation targets.

title: Hunter Douglas N.V. / 247 Home Furnishings Ltd merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has made an Initial Enforcement Order in the Hunter Douglas/247 Home Furnishings merger inquiry. It restricts integration and requires the two businesses to remain separate, preserve assets, staff, contracts, IT and confidential information, pending the CMA’s final determination. It applies to Hunter Douglas and Buismetaal during the specified period.

title: Barratt / Redrow merger inquiry
summary: The CMA published a merger notice for Barratt’s anticipated acquisition of Redrow under the Enterprise Act 2002. It states the initial merger review period starts on 14 June 2024 and the CMA’s phase 2 referral decision deadline is 8 August 2024. This is a competition-law market notice, not a financial-services rule change.

title: Hitachi / Thales merger inquiry
summary: CMA notice that Hitachi Rail’s merger notice for the anticipated acquisition of Thales SA’s Ground Transportation Systems Business meets the Enterprise Act filing requirements. It starts the initial merger review period and states the Phase 2 referral decision deadline as 9 December 2022.

title: Cellnex / CK Hutchison UK towers merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a notice confirming that the merger notice for Cellnex UK Limited’s planned acquisition of CK Hutchison’s UK passive telecoms infrastructure assets satisfies the statutory requirements. It starts the CMA’s initial merger-review period on 18 May 2021, with the Phase 2 referral deadline set for 13 July 2021.

title: Biggest ever investment in city region local transport as Chancellor vows the 'Renewal of Britain'
summary: HMT issued a press release announcing £15.6 billion of funding for local transport projects in England’s city regions, ahead of next week’s Spending Review and a Green Book review publication on 11 June 2025. It is an investment announcement, not a rule, consultation or supervisory notice. Banks may be indirectly interested as regional employers and infrastructure users, but no direct obligations are created.

title: viagogo / StubHub merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has made an Initial Enforcement Order in the viagogo/StubHub merger inquiry under the Enterprise Act 2002. It restricts integration and other pre-emptive actions by viagogo, PUG and eBay while the CMA considers the merger, and requires the businesses to remain separate until the CMA gives written clearance or the inquiry is otherwise determined.

title: Report on the proposed subsidy to Great British Energy by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a non-binding report on DESNZ’s proposed subsidy to Great British Energy for operationalisation and early commercial activity. It comments on the subsidy control assessment under the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and suggests areas for improvement, but does not itself approve or require any action. No firm-specific deadlines or obligations are set out.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy to Great British Energy by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its report on DESNZ’s proposed subsidy to Great British Energy. It is an advisory publication about a subsidy-control assessment, with a request for third-party submissions already part of the process and no new obligations for firms.

title: Merging your business
summary: CMA guidance page explaining how businesses should engage in merger investigations, notify mergers, respond to information requests and propose remedies. It is aimed at firms considering or undergoing a CMA merger review, with no fixed deadline or new rule change stated.

title: Guidance for businesses
summary: The CMA published a general guidance page for businesses covering mergers, selling goods and services, collaboration with other businesses, cartel leniency, and how to report issues or suspicious activity to the CMA. It is informational only and does not create new requirements or deadlines.

title: Dynamic pricing: tips for businesses
summary: The CMA published guidance tips for businesses using dynamic pricing, explaining how firms can stay on the right side of the law and treat customers fairly. It is informational and reflects research from the CMA’s dynamic pricing project. No deadline or binding rule is set out.

title: Powering Britain's future: Electricity bills to be slashed for over 7,000 businesses in major industry shake-up
summary: HMT and other departments announced a ten-year Industrial Strategy to cut electricity costs, improve grid access and reduce regulatory burdens for businesses. It says a consultation will follow on eligibility for the new electricity support scheme, with some measures intended from 2026 and 2027 and a new connections service expected by end-2025. No direct obligations are created in this press release.

title: Tell the CMA about a merger that might affect you
summary: CMA guidance explains how customers, competitors and other parties can give views or information about a merger under CMA review, including invitations to comment and requests for information. It describes response expectations, confidentiality treatment and the CMA’s information-gathering powers. No new obligations are created for firms, but relevant businesses may be contacted during merger cases.

title: Submit a case team request form for your merger
summary: The CMA has published a case team request form for businesses that want to notify an anticipated or completed merger. It is an administrative form to help the CMA allocate a merger investigation case team and does not itself change merger rules or deadlines.

title: Referral of the proposed Automotive Transformation Grants scheme by the Department for Business and Trade
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its report on the Department for Business and Trade’s proposed Automotive Transformation Grants scheme. The report evaluates DBT’s assessment of the scheme under the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and notes third-party submissions could be provided for the report process. No direct obligations are created for regulated firms.

title: CMA takes first steps to improve competition in search services in the UK
summary: The CMA issued a press release proposing to designate Google with strategic market status in UK search and search advertising, and published a roadmap of possible future interventions such as choice screens, fair ranking, publisher controls and data portability. It invites views on the proposal before a final designation decision expected in October. The release is for awareness only and does not itself impose obligations on firms.

title: Referral of the proposed Automotive Innovation Grants scheme by UK Research and Innovation
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its final report on UKRI’s proposed Automotive Innovation Grants scheme under the Subsidy Control Act 2022. The report evaluates UKRI’s assessment of compliance and invites third-party comments on the scheme. Submissions were due by the timetable in the notice; no new binding requirements for firms are created.

title: G7 reach agreement on global minimum tax
summary: HM Treasury announced that G7 countries have reached an understanding on the future of global minimum tax rules under Pillar 2, and that this helped secure removal of proposed US retaliatory tax measure Section 899. It is a press release about ongoing international talks, not a new rule. The publication names no direct compliance deadline for firms.

title: New targeted support regime to enable more people to make the most of their money
summary: The FCA has published draft rules for a new targeted support regime, alongside a consultation open until 2025-08-29. The government will also publish a policy note and draft statutory instrument on 2025-07-15 to propose legislative changes needed to implement the regime. It affects authorised firms that may provide support on pensions and investments.

title: Road fuel quarterly update report: June 2025
summary: CMA published its June 2025 quarterly update on the road fuel market. It reports latest UK pump prices, retail spreads and retailer margins, and notes progress toward a statutory Fuel Finder scheme and the CMA’s monitoring function. The publication is informational only and does not create new requirements for firms.

title: 'Innovator passports’ set to accelerate cutting-edge NHS care
summary: HMT/DHSC published a press release announcing an NHS ‘innovator passport’ and MedTech Compass to speed rollout of proven medical technologies across the NHS over the next 2 years. It is aimed at reducing duplicate assessments and helping suppliers get innovations adopted more quickly, but it does not create regulatory obligations for financial services firms.

title: Affordable housing set to benefit from £100 million following CMA probe
summary: CMA press release says seven housebuilders have offered commitments following a competition investigation, including a combined £100 million payment to affordable housing and limits on sharing sensitive information. The CMA will consult on the package until 24 July 2025 before deciding whether to accept it. If accepted, the commitments become legally binding.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy to Besson Street LLP by Lewisham London Borough Council
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a report on Lewisham Council’s proposed subsidy to Besson Street LLP for affordable housing, as part of a closed SAU referral. Third parties could submit comments by the timetable date, and the SAU said it would evaluate the council’s assessment under the Subsidy Control Act 2022.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy to Drax Power Limited by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its final report on DESNZ’s proposed subsidy for Drax Power Limited. It evaluates DESNZ’s assessment of compliance with the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and invites third-party submissions by the timetable in the report. The proposed support would run from 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2031, but no direct obligations are imposed on firms by this publication.

title: Referral of the proposed Transformation and Network Investment subsidy to Post Office Limited by the Department for Business and Trade
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a final report advising the Department for Business and Trade on a proposed subsidy to Post Office Limited. It is an assessment of compliance under the Subsidy Control Act 2022, with third-party submissions already closed and the report published on 15 July 2025.

title: UK tightens Oil Price Cap in blow to Putin's war machine
summary: The UK and EU announced a lower crude oil price cap for Russian oil, reducing it from $60 to $47.60 per barrel. The new cap takes effect at 23:01 BST on 2025-09-02, with a 45-day wind-down for qualifying pre-existing trades ending at 23:01 BST on 2025-10-17. Firms involved in shipping, insurance or servicing Russian oil must apply the new cap and wind-down rules.

title: CMA letter to Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Patient Safety, Women's Health and Mental Health
summary: The CMA wrote to the Minister updating its fertility-sector work and publishing its view that current fertility regulation should be reformed to better protect patients. It also said its programme on consumer protection and voluntary pricing is ending, though future enforcement remains possible if consumer law breaches emerge. The letter highlights issues with price transparency and treatment add-ons.

title: CMA proposes action to drive more competition on mobile platforms
summary: The CMA has issued a press release proposing to designate Apple and Google with strategic market status in mobile platforms and setting out roadmaps for possible future interventions on app stores, interoperability, steering, and consumer choice. It invites views on the proposals; final designation decisions are due by 2025-10-22.

title: Chancellor pledges to unlock growth in Cornwall
summary: HMT issued a press release about the Chancellor’s visit to Cornwall, highlighting a £28.6 million National Wealth Fund investment in South Crofty tin mine and announcing proposed licensing deregulation for hospitality. It says a consultation on the licensing proposals will be launched later this year, but this publication itself is informational only.

title: Kpler / Spire Global merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has issued an Initial Enforcement Order in relation to Kpler’s acquisition of Spire Global’s maritime data business. The order requires the parties to keep the target business separate and preserve its independent operation until the CMA’s merger review is completed. It applies from completion of the transaction and carries financial-penalty consequences for breach.

title: Penalty issued for breach of Russia Sanctions
summary: OFSI has imposed a £300,000 monetary penalty on Markom Management Limited for breaching Russia sanctions by facilitating a payment to a designated person. The release also reminds firms to maintain adequate sanctions controls and report suspected breaches promptly. It notes OFSI has launched a consultation on enforcement-process changes, but this press release itself is the penalty notice.

title: Personal information charter
summary: The CMA has published a personal information charter explaining how it handles data portability requests, identity checks, response times, fees, and complaint routes to the ICO. It applies to individuals making requests under data protection law and does not set new firm-wide regulatory obligations for the bank.

title: North Sea catering merger set for in-depth investigation
summary: The CMA announced that Aramark’s completed purchase of Entier will move to a Phase 2 merger investigation after a Phase 1 review found potential competition concerns in offshore catering and facilities management in the UK North Sea. This is a news update on a merger case, not a rule or obligation. No action date is set in the publication.

title: Funerals market: insight gathering
summary: The CMA published a summary of anonymous responses from its third annual insight-gathering exercise on the funerals sector. It reports perceived changes in costs, prices, service quality, consumer awareness and sector relationships, but does not impose new requirements. The document is informational only.

title: Annual review of funerals sector 2025
summary: The CMA published its third annual review of market outcomes in the funerals sector. It summarises how the sector has changed since the 2020 market investigation, including the impact of the existing funerals order and whether the CMA Board should consider a further market investigation reference. It is an informational review, not a new rule or enforcement action.

title: Kingspan / Coverworld merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has issued a merger notice acceptance for Kingspan’s anticipated acquisition of Coverworld under the Enterprise Act 2002. This starts the initial review period on 3 July 2025 and sets 1 September 2025 as the deadline for the CMA to decide whether to refer the deal for a phase 2 investigation.

title: Referral of the proposed Welsh Investment Zones subsidy scheme by Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a report on MHCLG’s proposed Welsh Investment Zones subsidy scheme under the Subsidy Control Act 2022. The report evaluates MHCLG’s assessment of compliance and invites third-party submissions for the report process. The scheme is expected to come into effect from autumn 2025 and run to 2035, but this publication itself is not a rule or binding notice.

title: Referral of the proposed Scottish Investment Zones subsidy scheme by Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its report on MHCLG’s proposed Scottish Investment Zones subsidy scheme. The report evaluates MHCLG’s assessment under the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and notes the scheme is expected to run from autumn 2025 to 2035. This is an informational publication and does not itself impose obligations on firms.

title: Reviews and endorsements: principles for social media platforms
summary: The CMA published principles for social media platforms on how to comply with consumer protection law on reviews and endorsements, including preventing hidden advertising and fake reviews. It is guidance only and does not itself create new rules or deadlines.

title: How the CMA gathers information to enforce consumer law
summary: The CMA published a guidance page explaining how it gathers information when investigating suspected consumer law breaches, including before or after opening a case. It is aimed at businesses under investigation or people asked to provide information about them, with no new deadline or rule change.

title: CMA’s response to DBT’s statutory review consultation on the Groceries Code Adjudicator 2025
summary: The CMA published its response to DBT’s statutory review consultation on the Groceries Code Adjudicator. It says the GCA still has sufficient powers and has been effective in enforcing the Groceries Code. This is an awareness item for grocery retailers and suppliers; it does not itself change rules or impose deadlines.

title: How the CMA uses its direct consumer enforcement powers
summary: The CMA published a guidance summary explaining how it uses its direct consumer enforcement powers to investigate suspected consumer law breaches, gather information, decide cases, and handle settlements or undertakings. It is informational only and points readers to the full guidance CMA200. No new obligations or deadlines are set out in this publication.

title: Safran / Collins merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a merger notice confirming that the initial period for its review of Safran’s proposed acquisition of part of Collins Aerospace’s actuation and flight control business starts on 19 February 2025. The CMA’s deadline to decide whether to refer the merger for a phase 2 investigation is 16 April 2025.

title: Social media endorsements: guidance for content creators
summary: The CMA published guidance for content creators and influencers on how to label gifted, discounted and promotional social media content so it is clear when posts are ads or otherwise commercially connected. It explains the guidance applies where creators receive free or discounted products, payment or commission, and even when posting about their own brand. No deadline or new mandatory rule is stated in the publication itself.

title: Budget to address economy that’s “not working well enough for working people”
summary: HM Treasury announced that the UK Budget will be on 26 November 2025 and launched a Budget representation portal for comments on existing policy. The portal closes at 23:59 on 15 October 2025. This is an informational government press release, not a rule or requirement.

title: Rubix UK/Eriks UK merger inquiry
summary: The CMA is inviting comments on the Rubix UK/Eriks UK merger inquiry by 25 July 2025. This is a market intelligence call for interested parties, not a binding rule or enforcement action. It also includes a privacy notice about how the CMA will process personal data.

title: Investment and competition over the business lifecycle
summary: The CMA published a research report on how competition affects investment across the business lifecycle, including start-ups, scale-ups, innovation, trade, private equity, IPOs and mergers. It is an intelligence publication and does not create rules or obligations. The CMA says it will continue stakeholder engagement through 2025 and expects a further report in early 2026.

title: Covid repayment window opens
summary: HMT announced a voluntary repayment window for Covid-era scheme money, open until December 2025, for individuals and businesses to repay money they were not entitled to or did not need. It says tougher sanctions and additional investigatory powers may follow next year, and has launched a website for reporting suspected Covid fraud.

title: CMA response to the Cabinet Office's public procurement consultation
summary: The CMA published its response to the Cabinet Office’s public procurement consultation. It is an advocacy and commentary document explaining how procurement can support growth, competition and anti-collusion objectives, and encouraging market-shaping and better data collection. It does not create rules or obligations for firms.

title: Road fuel quarterly update report: September 2025
summary: The CMA published its September 2025 quarterly road fuel monitoring update. It reports on fuel prices, retail spreads and margins, and notes the government’s Fuel Finder plans and the CMA’s monitoring role under the DMCC Act. No new obligations are created for firms in this publication.

title: How best to make a competition or consumer law complaint and what happens next
summary: The CMA published guidance explaining how to make a competition or consumer law complaint, what evidence to include, and what happens next. It also explains the CMA’s acknowledgement and update process, including a possible 6-week contact point if the complaint may be investigated. No new legal obligations are created.

title: Major reforms would require vet businesses to make fundamental changes to the way they support pet owners
summary: The CMA has published a provisional market-investigation decision on veterinary services, proposing 21 remedies to improve price transparency, prescriptions, treatment quotes, cremation pricing and pet care plans. It also recommends government reform of veterinary regulation. The final decision is due by March 2026, and any binding CMA Order could bring some measures into force before end-2026, with extra time for small vet businesses.

title: Review of merger remedies approach
summary: This is a law firm response to the CMA’s call for evidence on merger remedies. It comments on the CMA’s current approach and suggests changes to its guidance, but it does not itself change any rules or create obligations. It is relevant mainly as market intelligence for teams monitoring competition-law developments.

title: Report on DESNZ’s proposed Contracts for Difference for Renewables Allocation Round 7 scheme
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its final report on DESNZ’s proposed Contracts for Difference Allocation Round 7 scheme. It evaluates DESNZ’s assessment of compliance with the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and describes changes to AR7, including contract length, eligibility and budget process. This is an advisory publication, not a rule or enforcement notice.

title: CMA response to DBT call for evidence on the opt-out collective actions regime
summary: The CMA published its response to the DBT call for evidence on the opt-out collective actions regime.
