It argues that private and public competition enforcement both matter, and discusses case-management stays and possible protection for businesses that cooperate with the CMA’s leniency policy. This is an advisory response only; it does not itself change rules or obligations.

title: Cartels: come forward and apply for leniency
summary: The CMA published guidance on its leniency programme for cartel participants. It explains who can apply, what cooperation is required, and the possible protections from fines, disqualification, criminal prosecution and public contract exclusion. It also notes Scotland-specific treatment and points readers to further guidance and a helpline.

title: CMA’s mergers intelligence function
summary: The CMA published guidance on how its mergers intelligence function works, including how it gathers merger intelligence, decides whether to investigate, and how it treats publicity and timing for completed mergers. It also notes the new digital markets regime and that SMS firms have separate merger reporting duties, but those duties are covered in other guidance.

title: Study into proposed regulatory changes to bovine electronic identification in the United Kingdom
summary: The CMA’s Office for the Internal Market published the final report from its study of proposed regulatory changes to bovine electronic identification in the UK. It is an informational market study, not a rule, consultation, or enforcement notice. No action date or compliance deadline is set for firms.

title: Accent Wire / DR Baling Wire merger inquiry
summary: The CMA published a merger notice for the anticipated acquisition of DR Baling Wire Holdings Limited by Accent Wire Limited. It starts the CMA’s initial merger review period on 17 September 2025 and sets a decision deadline of 11 November 2025. This is a market/operational notice, not a financial-services rule change.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy to TBG Open Door Homes Ltd by the London Borough of Barnet
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a final report on Barnet Council’s proposed subsidy to TBG Open Door Homes Ltd for affordable housing. It evaluates the council’s assessment under the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and invites third-party submissions as part of the reporting process. No direct compliance obligation is created for banks.

title: Major banks give helping hand to people experiencing homelessness as new Financial Inclusion Strategy launches
summary: HMT has launched a Financial Inclusion Strategy and announced a pilot with Shelter and five major UK banks to help people without a fixed address open bank accounts. The strategy also covers credit repair for domestic abuse survivors, payroll savings schemes, financial education in schools, and banking hubs. It is a press release with no direct new requirements for firms.

title: New IRA and suspected terror facilitator sanctioned
summary: HMT has designated the New IRA and Kieran Gallagher under the Counter-Terrorism (Sanctions) (EU Exit) Regulations 2019 from 6 November 2025. The measures impose an asset freeze, prohibit making funds or economic resources available, and add director disqualification sanctions for Gallagher. UK persons and firms must comply immediately.

title: CMA proposes to accept remedies in supermarket supplier deal
summary: The CMA issued a press release saying it proposes to accept remedies in Greencore’s planned acquisition of Bakkavor after a Phase 1 competition review. The parties have offered to divest Greencore’s chilled sauces and soups plant in Bristol, and the CMA will consult further on the remedies package and purchaser in due course.

title: S&P Global / ORBCOMM AIS merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published notice that S&P Global Market Intelligence’s merger notice for its anticipated acquisition of Orbcomm AIS meets the Enterprise Act requirements. The CMA’s initial review period started on 1 October 2025, and the deadline to decide whether to refer the merger to phase 2 is 25 November 2025.

title: CMA launches major consumer protection drive focused on online pricing practices
summary: The CMA announced a consumer-protection campaign on online pricing, opening investigations into eight businesses, sending advisory letters to 100 firms, and publishing guidance on price transparency under the DMCCA. It is a press release about enforcement and guidance, not the underlying rule or notice. Businesses named or operating in the affected sectors should review pricing, fees, time-limited offers and opt-in practices now.

title: Getting consent for additional charges when selling online
summary: The CMA published guidance for businesses that sell goods and services online, explaining that customers must give express consent before being charged for optional extras such as insurance or faster delivery. It also points to separate pricing transparency guidance and a pricing check tool. No new deadline or rule change is stated.

title: Referral of the proposed Heat Pump Investment Accelerator Competition subsidy scheme – Round 2 by the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ)
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its report on DESNZ’s proposed Heat Pump Investment Accelerator Competition subsidy scheme. The report evaluates DESNZ’s assessment under the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and invites any third-party comments in line with the timetable. This is informational rather than a rule or obligation for firms.

title: Report on the proposed Heat Pump Investment Accelerator Competition subsidy scheme – Round 2
summary: CMA Subsidy Advice Unit published non-binding advice on DESNZ’s proposed Heat Pump Investment Accelerator Competition Round 2 subsidy scheme. It comments on the scheme assessment and suggests improvements, but does not create rules or obligations. The report is relevant mainly to public subsidy control policy rather than bank compliance, and no action date is set.

title: SMFLH / MRL merger inquiry
summary: The CMA published a revocation order lifting an initial enforcement order made in connection with SMFL LCI Helicopters’ acquisition of Macquarie Rotorcraft. The order applies to the parties named and revokes the earlier hold-separate order; it is effective from 15 May 2025. This is a merger-control case notice rather than a general rule change.

title: Soft drinks levy extended to protect children and improve health
summary: HM Treasury/HMRC has issued the final policy response extending the Soft Drinks Industry Levy to more high-sugar drinks, including certain pre-packaged milk-based and milk-alternative drinks. The sugar threshold is lowered from 5g to 4.5g per 100ml, and manufacturers/importers have until 1 January 2028 to reduce sugar or face the charge. This is a final policy change with an implementation date.

title: Reeves tackles cost-of-living and backs Welsh industry at Budget
summary: HMT issued a press release on the 2025 Budget highlighting cost-of-living measures, tax reform, Welsh public spending and major investment commitments. It is informational only and does not create or change compliance obligations for firms. The publication mentions changes such as minimum wage increases and fuel duty freeze, but as a press release it is not the operative rule or notice.

title: Budget 2025 fact sheet: Tax support for businesses
summary: HM Treasury published a Budget fact sheet setting out business tax support measures, including business rates relief, fuel duty changes, investment allowances, EV support, and a UK listing relief from April 2026. It is an informational news item aimed at businesses and investors, with signposts to GOV.UK for eligibility and further details.

title: Small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) banking undertakings
summary: CMA undertakings set out binding conditions for named UK clearing banks on SME banking services, including account definitions and obligations around switching, credit history and business loan information. The document reflects ongoing commitments under the Fair Trading Act framework for SMEs rather than a new consultation or rule. No new date-driven action is stated in the excerpt.

title: Chancellor announces increase to the National Living Wage and National Minimum Wage
summary: HMT announced the government will increase the National Living Wage and National Minimum Wage from 1 April 2026. The release gives the proposed new hourly rates for adult, youth and apprentice workers and notes a full impact assessment will follow in early 2026.

title: Rogue insiders and dirty money targeted in corruption crackdown
summary: HMT and the Home Office published a news story on the government’s anti-corruption strategy 2025. It announces planned measures including stronger vetting, expanded enforcement, AML supervisory reform, sanctions use and a review of beneficial ownership. No direct firm obligations or implementation dates are set out in the news story itself.

title: New crypto rules to unlock growth and protect customers
summary: HMT announced plans for a new UK cryptoassets regulatory regime, with FCA regulation and similar consumer-protection rules to other financial products. The news says the rules are expected to come into force from 2027, but this is a government announcement rather than the rule text itself.

title: Greencore / Bakkavor merger inquiry
summary: The CMA published a notice saying it has enough information to start the initial period in its merger investigation into Greencore Group plc’s anticipated acquisition of Bakkavor Group plc. It says the initial period started on 2 September 2025 and the CMA’s phase 2 referral decision deadline is 27 October 2025.

title: Referral of the proposed modified Network Charging Compensation Scheme by the Department for Business and Trade
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its report on DBT’s proposed modification to the Network Charging Compensation Scheme, evaluating DBT’s assessment under the Subsidy Control Act 2022. Third parties could submit comments by the timetable deadline, and the report notes the proposed uplift of NCC relief from 60% to 90% from 1 April 2026.

title: Road fuel annual monitoring report: December 2025
summary: CMA’s annual road fuel monitoring report says competition in UK road fuel remains weak and operating margins have not fallen. It explains progress on Fuel Finder, which the government expects motorists to start benefiting from during 2026, and notes the CMA’s monitoring role backed by information-gathering powers. This is an intelligence update rather than a new rule or notice.

title: Fuel margins remain “persistently high” and this is not explained by operating costs, CMA finds
summary: The CMA published a press release and analysis on road fuel margins, saying they remain high and are not explained by operating costs. It also notes the upcoming fuel finder scheme and says the CMA has issued enforcement guidance for the new fuel finder regulations, with a support-first approach to enforcement until at least May 2026.

title: What are the changes to agricultural property relief?
summary: HMT published a news story explaining changes to agricultural property relief and business property relief for inheritance tax from 6 April 2026. It says the 100% relief will be limited to the first £2.5 million of combined qualifying assets, with 50% relief above that, and describes examples and spousal transfer treatment. This is informational and does not itself create obligations.

title: Inheritance tax reliefs threshold to rise to £2.5m for farmers and businesses
summary: HM Treasury and DEFRA announced a press release saying the Agricultural Property Relief and Business Property Relief threshold will rise from £1m to £2.5m from April 2026, to be delivered through an amendment to the Finance Bill 2025. It is a tax-policy announcement for farmers and business owners, not a rule or notice for regulated firms.

title: Business investment boosted with new tax relief taking effect today
summary: HM Treasury announced that a new permanent 40% first-year capital allowance for main-rate plant and machinery takes effect on 1 January 2026. The measure extends upfront tax relief to assets bought for leasing and to unincorporated businesses, while the main rate writing-down allowance will reduce from 18% to 14% from April 2026.

title: Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) between the Information Commissioner’s Office and HM Government
summary: The ICO and HM Government have published a non-binding memorandum of understanding setting out how they will work together on data protection, privacy, security and breach handling. It commits government to regular information-sharing, annual assurance statements and improved internal processes, but does not create enforceable obligations for firms. No action is directly required of banks.

title: CMA launches review of its approach to merger efficiencies
summary: The CMA has launched a call for evidence on how it assesses merger efficiencies, including the evidence it requires and how it engages with merging businesses. It is seeking stakeholder views now, with proposals for consultation in spring and possible implementation by summer 2026. This is a competition-policy review, not a financial-services regulatory rule change.

title: Beacon / Eversholt merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a merger notice for Beacon Rail Lux’s anticipated acquisition of Eversholt UK Rails Limited and stated that the phase 1 initial period began on 2 December 2025. The CMA’s deadline to decide whether to refer the merger for a phase 2 investigation is 30 January 2026.

title: Retail banking market investigation
summary: CMA publishes an updates page on the retail banking market investigation and open banking remedy. It includes letters, decisions and status updates on roadmap items such as variable recurring payments, sweeping and trustee appointments. The page is informational and points to past and current correspondence rather than creating new requirements.

title: Collaborating with other higher education providers
summary: The CMA published guidance for senior managers at higher education providers on how to collaborate with other providers while complying with competition law. It covers informal collaboration, contractual partnerships, mergers, and working with non-HE providers. No new obligations or deadlines are created.

title: Informal guidance on the Landscape Enterprise Networks scheme
summary: The CMA published informal guidance on how its Green Agreements Guidance applies to 3Keel’s Landscape Enterprise Networks (LENs) 2.0 scheme. It explains the CMA’s enforcement expectations for the scheme and is effective from the date of issue, subject to the stated conditions. This is guidance only and does not itself create new legal requirements.

title: Pubs and Live Music Venues Relief
summary: HMT announced that in 2026-27 pubs and live music venues will receive a 15% business rates relief, with rates then frozen in real terms for 2027-28 and 2028-29. The note explains eligibility criteria for pubs and live music venues and gives worked examples. It is an informational news story rather than a binding rule or consultation.

title: SAU Report on the proposed UK SHORE subsidy scheme by Innovate UK
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a non-binding report on Innovate UK’s proposed UK SHORE subsidy scheme, assessing the scheme’s design against subsidy control principles. It is advice to Innovate UK, not a rule, supervision notice, or enforcement action. The scheme would fund maritime decarbonisation R&D, but this publication itself creates no obligations for banks.

title: Referral of the proposed London Social and Affordable Homes Programme 2026-36 by the Greater London Authority
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a report on the Greater London Authority’s proposed London Social and Affordable Homes Programme 2026-36. It evaluates the scheme’s compliance assessment under the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and describes the scheme’s scope, budget and bidding timetable. This is an advisory/publication notice, not a rule or enforcement action.

title: Report on the proposed London Social and Affordable Homes Programme 2026-36 by the Greater London Authority
summary: The CMA Subsidy Advice Unit issued a non-binding report on the Greater London Authority’s proposed London Social and Affordable Homes Programme 2026-36. It reviews the GLA’s subsidy control assessment, highlights areas for improvement, and discusses how the scheme should be finalised. No direct obligations are created for firms.

title: New Green Book to ensure that investment in all parts of the UK given a "fair hearing"
summary: HM Treasury issued a press release announcing a revised Green Book for public spending decisions. The guidance says investment appraisals should take a broader view of regional impacts and not rely only on single metrics such as benefit-cost ratios. It affects government capital spending assessment and is intended to support fairer investment decisions across the UK.

title: Government publishes Budget Information Security Review
summary: HMT published a review on protecting Budget information security ahead of Budget 2026. It sets out recommended controls such as mandatory IT protections, a new market-sensitive label, reduced access lists, and publishing the March 2026 EFO via GOV.UK. The changes are to be implemented in full, but this is a press release/review rather than a binding rule.

title: CMA secures commitments from Apple and Google to improve fairness in app store processes and enhance iOS interoperability
summary: CMA press release seeking views on proposed commitments from Apple and Google to improve app store review, ranking, data use and iOS interoperability. Views are invited by 3 March 2026, and the CMA says the commitments would take effect from 1 April 2026 if adopted.

title: CMA fines Euro Car Parks £473k for failure to comply with legal information notice
summary: The CMA issued a press release saying it fined Euro Car Parks £473,000 for failing to comply with a legal information notice. It says this is the first use of the CMA’s new fining powers under the DMCCA 2024 and that no consumer enforcement case is currently open against the firm.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy for capitalisation of the National Housing Bank by Homes England
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a final report on Homes England’s proposed subsidy to capitalise the National Housing Bank. It evaluates Homes England’s assessment under the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and invites no further regulatory action from firms, though third parties could submit comments during the reporting process. The report was published on 19 February 2026.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy to 2020 Developments (Luton) Limited by Homes England
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a report on Homes England’s proposed £29.5 million subsidy to 2020 Developments (Luton) Limited for the Power Court redevelopment. The report evaluates Homes England’s assessment under the Subsidy Control Act 2022. Third parties could make submissions within the timetable stated in the report; the subsidy is a Subsidy of Particular Interest.

title: Referral of the proposed Great British Energy Multi-Year Capitalisation Scheme by the Department for Energy, Security and Net Zero
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a final report on DESNZ’s proposed Great British Energy Multi-Year Capitalisation Scheme. The report evaluates DESNZ’s assessment of the scheme under the Subsidy Control Act 2022. It concerns a proposed £5.3 billion subsidy scheme running from 2026/27 to 2029/30 and invites third-party comments as part of the process.

title: Using AI agents: complying with consumer law
summary: The CMA published guidance on using agentic AI while complying with consumer protection law. It says businesses remain responsible if an AI agent acts illegally and should train agents properly. No specific deadline or new binding requirement is stated.

title: Final decision on disputed price controls for 5 water companies
summary: CMA press release announcing the final decision in the redetermination of price controls for five water companies. It confirms limited extra revenue and bill increases for those firms, with some funding tied to outputs and performance. This is a market/public announcement about an external sector decision, not a new regulatory obligation for FS firms.

title: CMA steps up monitoring of petrol and diesel prices
summary: The CMA says it will step up monitoring of petrol and diesel prices and publish an update on pricing as soon as possible. It is also bringing forward formal data requests from firms running fuel stations, to review fuel margins and possible ‘rocket and feather’ pricing. The notice is aimed at fuel retailers and station operators, not financial firms.

title: Over £50 million to help families struggling with soaring heating oil costs
summary: HMT announced over £50 million of targeted support for low-income households facing high heating oil costs, with allocations across the UK and local authority delivery in England from 1 April. The statement also says government intends to explore stronger consumer protections and possible future regulation of the heating oil market, but no new binding rules are set out here.

title: CRH / Gibson merger inquiry
summary: The CMA published a notice confirming that the merger notice for CRH’s anticipated acquisition of Gibson meets statutory requirements. This starts the initial merger review period on 6 February 2026 and sets the CMA’s phase 2 referral deadline at 7 April 2026.

title: Referral of the proposed network subsidy to Post Office Limited for 2026 to 2029 by the Department for Business and Trade
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its final report on the Department for Business and Trade’s proposed 2026–2029 subsidy for Post Office Limited. It evaluates the subsidy’s compliance with the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and invites third-party submissions on competition issues. This is an awareness notice for the subsidy case, with no direct obligations on firms.

title: Government to Improve Support for Affordable Debt Repayments
summary: HM Treasury published a press release announcing the 2026–2030 Government Debt Management Strategy. It says government departments will use data and earlier engagement to prevent avoidable debt, improve repayment plans, and support people who can afford to repay, while taking a tougher approach to fraud and deliberate non-payment. No direct obligations are created for financial firms.

title: Referral of the proposed 'Retail, hospitality and leisure business rates multipliers and pubs and live music venues relief' subsidy scheme by HM Treasury
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its final report on HM Treasury’s proposed retail, hospitality and leisure business rates multipliers and pubs and live music venues relief scheme. It is advice on subsidy control compliance, not a new rule or obligation. The scheme is described as starting from 1 April 2026, but this publication itself creates no direct requirements for firms.

title: CMA draft Annual Plan 2026 to 2027
summary: The CMA has published its 2026 to 2027 Annual Plan after a consultation on the draft has closed. It sets out the authority’s priorities and how it will work under its 2026 to 2029 Strategy. No direct obligations for regulated firms are created by this publication.

title: Report on the proposed Electric Car Grant subsidy scheme by the Office for Zero Emission Vehicles
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a non-binding report on the proposed Electric Car Grant subsidy scheme referred by OZEV. It evaluates OZEV’s assessment against the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and guidance, and highlights areas for improvement, but does not decide whether the scheme should proceed.

title: CMA concludes market investigation with major reforms to veterinary sector
summary: The CMA says it has concluded a market investigation into the veterinary sector and set out a timetable for remedies due to come into effect from September 2026 through September 2028. The publication lists planned reforms for vets and the RCVS, including written policies, complaint handling, mediation, estimates, itemised bills, prescription-related measures and publication of complaint insights.

title: Report on the Zero Emission Truck Grant (ZETG) and Zero Emission Van Grant (ZEVG) Scheme
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a non-binding report evaluating OZEV’s Zero Emission Truck Grant and Zero Emission Van Grant subsidy scheme under the Subsidy Control Act 2022. It identifies areas where OZEV should strengthen its assessment of market failure, beneficiary identification, evidence, counterfactual analysis, subsidy design, competition impacts and balancing exercise. This is advisory only and does not itself change rules or create obligations.

title: Referral of the proposed Electric Car Grant subsidy scheme by the Office for Zero Emission Vehicles
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its report on OZEV’s proposed Electric Car Grant subsidy scheme. The report evaluates OZEV’s assessment under the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and invites third-party submissions for the report process. It is an intelligence/publication item about a government subsidy scheme, not a binding financial-services rule.

title: OIM Annual Report 2025 to 2026
summary: The CMA’s Office for the Internal Market published its 2025 to 2026 annual report on the UK internal market and updated its regulatory developments dashboard. It is an informational publication that reviews intra-UK trade and regulatory developments, and notes it fulfils a statutory reporting duty under the UK Internal Market Act 2020. No action date or new requirement is set out for firms.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy to Belfast City Council by the Department for the Economy
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a report on a proposed subsidy from the Department for the Economy to Belfast City Council for the Belfast Stories Project. It evaluates DfE’s assessment under the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and invites third-party submissions within the timetable set out in the report. This is informational and does not itself create obligations for firms.

title: Dignity: consumer protection enforcement case
summary: The CMA published a press release saying it has opened an investigation into Dignity Group Holdings Limited over possible unfair commercial practices linked to consumer reviews about crematoria services. It is an early-stage consumer enforcement case under the DMCC Act, with evidence gathering through September 2026 and no finding yet made.

title: Online consumer reviews
summary: The CMA published an update on its work on online consumer reviews, including open consumer enforcement cases against five businesses and the results of website compliance reviews. It says businesses should have clear policies and measures to prevent fake and misleading reviews and asks firms that receive letters to respond on any changes made.

title: Fake and misleading reviews: 5 businesses under CMA investigation
summary: CMA press release says it has opened five consumer-law investigations into businesses over fake or misleading online reviews and star ratings. It explains the types of practices under review, notes that some review practices became banned under the DMCC Act in April 2025, and says the cases could lead to findings of unlawful conduct and fines. No conclusions have been reached.

title: CMA announces package of actions on business software and cloud services
summary: The CMA issued a press release announcing a planned strategic market status investigation into Microsoft’s business software ecosystem and noting ongoing engagement with Microsoft and Amazon on cloud egress fees and interoperability. It says further steps may follow and that progress will be reviewed in 6 months. This is a market update, not a rule or enforcement notice.

title: Suspected anti-competitive conduct in relation to fragrances and fragrance ingredients (51257)
summary: The CMA published an update on its ongoing investigation into suspected anti-competitive conduct in the fragrances and fragrance ingredients market. It confirms the case remains open, names the businesses under investigation, and notes a closure decision for one party on administrative priority grounds. No compliance deadline or new obligation is created by this publication.

title: Britain’s innovators backed with around £100m of new investment
summary: HM Treasury announces a news package from 6 April 2026 expanding EMI, EIS and VCT tax incentives, introducing UK Listing Relief, and outlining British Business Bank support for scale-ups. It is an information release about policy already brought into force, with no direct action for firms stated in the notice.

title: Referral of the proposed Post Office Transformation Subsidy Scheme by the Department for Business and Trade
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a report advising the Department for Business and Trade on the proposed Post Office Transformation Subsidy Scheme. It evaluates DBT’s assessment of compliance with the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and invites third-party submissions. The scheme covers FY2026/27 to FY2028/29 and funds Post Office transformation and technology changes.

title: CMA orders the AA and BSM driving schools to refund learner drivers over drip pricing
summary: CMA publication presenting research on the prevalence and impact of online drip pricing across sectors, including consumer harm estimates and case studies. It is an analytical report and does not create new requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: AkzoNobel / Axalta merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a merger notice confirming that the initial review period for the anticipated Akzo Nobel/Axalta merger starts on 17 September 2026. The CMA’s deadline to decide whether to refer the merger to a phase 2 investigation is 11 November 2026.

title: Our governance
summary: The CMA published an overview of its governance arrangements, including the board’s responsibilities, panel structure, committees, authorisations, and standing counsel panel. It describes internal decision-making and appointments rather than new rules or obligations for regulated firms.

title: Government cuts electricity bill for 10,000 manufacturers in boost for UK competitiveness
summary: HMT announced a press release saying the British Industrial Competitiveness Scheme will cut electricity bills for over 10,000 manufacturers from April 2027, with backdated support and expanded eligibility. It also says a new consultation on regulatory changes and scheme delivery has been linked. The announcement is for energy-intensive manufacturers, not banks.

title: Daily Mail and General Trust plc / Telegraph Media Group merger inquiry
summary: The Secretary of State is minded to issue a Public Interest Intervention Notice to the CMA on DMGT’s proposed acquisition of Telegraph Media Group. The letter says the deal may create a relevant merger situation and raises public-interest concerns about plurality in UK news media. It is not a final decision and no compliance deadline is set.

title: Chancellor rallies retail banks behind her economic plan
summary: HMT issued a press release on the Chancellor’s meeting with retail banks and wider growth strategy messages. It also mentions Treasury’s response to SM&CR reforms and related FCA/PRA policy statements, but this publication itself is only a news release and creates no new obligations.

title: CMA advice to Defra on reform of the Veterinary Surgeons Act 1966
summary: The CMA gives advice to Defra on reform of the Veterinary Surgeons Act 1966 and related veterinary regulation. It discusses competition, consumer protection, monitoring, enforcement and redress for veterinary services, but it is advice rather than a rule, consultation or enforcement notice. No direct obligations are created for firms in this publication.

title: Referral of the proposed Mayoral Revolving Growth Fund Subsidy Scheme by the Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its report on MHCLG’s proposed Mayoral Revolving Growth Fund subsidy scheme. It evaluates MHCLG’s assessment of compliance with the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and invites third-party submissions on the report process. The scheme is described as coming into effect in 2026 and running to 2056, but this publication itself is an advisory report, not a rule or requirement.

title: Report on the proposed subsidy to Center Parcs Scotland Limited by South of Scotland Enterprise
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a non-binding report on a proposed subsidy from South of Scotland Enterprise to Center Parcs Scotland Limited for a holiday village project. It assesses SoSE’s subsidy-control analysis and suggests areas for improvement before SoSE finalises its assessment. The report is advisory only and does not decide whether the subsidy can be given.

title: Referral of the proposed Bus Network Support Grant subsidy scheme by West Midlands Combined Authority
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a final report on West Midlands Combined Authority’s proposed Bus Network Support Grant subsidy scheme. It assesses the authority’s compliance with the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and describes the scheme’s proposed eligibility and data/reporting conditions for bus operators. This is informational only and does not itself create obligations for banks.

title: Government reviews access to face to face banking services
summary: HMT announces an independent Access to Banking Review, led by Richard Lloyd, to examine the impact of branch closures and identify where further action may be needed to protect face-to-face banking. The government says findings may inform new legislation and broader powers, with a report due by October 2026. It also notes planned credit union common bond reforms in the Bill.

title: Banking reforms to boost investment by billions for British businesses
summary: HMT has announced proposed reforms to the bank ring-fencing regime, including a new Growth Allowance and wider product range to support lending to UK businesses. The changes will be delivered through forthcoming legislation and later rules, with a consultation to follow on detail and ongoing review of thresholds and reporting requirements.

title: Competition Act 1998 cases in the sectors regulated by UKCN members
summary: The CMA has published a guidance page listing public Competition Act 1998 cases handled by UKCN regulators in regulated sectors since 2014. It is an informational register of cases, not a new rule, consultation or enforcement notice affecting firms directly.

title: Fairer taxes for high-value homes
summary: HM Treasury has launched an eight-week consultation on the design of a new High Value Council Tax Surcharge for residential properties in England worth £2 million and above. It covers valuation, billing, appeals, deferral and enforcement, and says the charge is expected to start from April 2028. Taxpayers, local government, tax experts, legal professionals and the property industry are invited to respond.

title: Chancellor commits to new anti-profiteering powers and fights back on rising bills
summary: HMT issued a press release saying it will bring forward new powers for the CMA and other regulators to tackle unfair price rises during crises, including possible naming and shaming and targeted enforcement powers. It is an announcement of intended future action, not a rule, consultation, or binding requirement.

title: Referral of the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero’s Proposed Subsidy to ITM Power UK Ltd
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a report on DESNZ’s proposed subsidy to ITM Power UK Ltd. It evaluates DESNZ’s assessment under the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and invites third-party submissions as part of the process. This is a case-specific report on a proposed subsidy, not a rule, guidance or enforcement action.

title: Boost for Britain’s financial services and greater protections for consumers as new legislation is introduced
summary: HM Treasury issued a press release on a new Financial Services and Markets Bill introduced to Parliament. The Bill aims to simplify regulation, transfer Payment Systems Regulator responsibilities to the FCA, reduce the SMCR burden, modernise consumer redress, expand credit unions, protect access to face-to-face banking, and update ring-fencing rules. No immediate compliance date is stated.

title: CMA proposes to accept remedies in care home deal
summary: CMA press release says it is proposing to accept remedies for Welltower’s purchase of more than 600 UK care homes after finding competition concerns in 30 local areas. The remedies would involve selling some properties and reassigning operations at certain homes, with consultation on the package to follow.

title: Great British Summer Savings 2026: Family activities VAT relief fact sheet
summary: HM Treasury announced a temporary summer 2026 VAT reduction from 20% to 5% for eligible children’s meals and family leisure activities, plus free bus travel for children aged 5–15 in England in August. It applies from 25 June to 1 September 2026 across the UK for specified admissions and meals. Businesses are expected to pass the saving through to customers, but this is a news/fact-sheet announcement rather than a rulemaking text.

title: Millions to benefit from lower travel and food costs
summary: HM Treasury says it has launched a consultation on suspending tariffs on 125 everyday essentials, and is also seeking views on possible tariff suspensions for some fertilisers. The story also announces changes to mileage rates, fuel duty and other cost-of-living measures, with some relief backdated to April 2026 and a road tax holiday for hauliers from 1 July.

title: Trader recommendation platforms: complying with consumer law
summary: The CMA has published compliance advice for trader recommendation platforms on how to comply with consumer law. It sets out six principles covering representations, vetting, complaints, monitoring, investigations and sanctions, and consumer reviews. It is guidance only, aimed at TRPs operating on websites, apps, social media, ads and brochures, with no new legal deadline.

title: Court endorses CMA action as Emma Sleep agrees to change sales practices
summary: CMA press release says Emma Sleep agreed court-endorsed, legally binding undertakings to stop misleading urgency and discount practices and to strengthen compliance controls. The company must monitor compliance, report to the CMA and act quickly on breaches. The remaining reference-pricing issue will go to trial in early June 2026.

title: Hays / Polka Dot and Hays / Millington merger inquiries
summary: The CMA has made an initial enforcement order under the Enterprise Act 2002 in relation to the Hays/Polka Dot Travel merger inquiry. Hays and Polka Dot Travel must keep the businesses separate and avoid pre-emptive action while the CMA considers the merger, starting from 2025-12-16. The order applies to Hays and PDT.

title: CMA secures fairer deal for publishers and improves Google search services in UK
summary: CMA press release announcing a new conduct requirement for Google search under the UK digital markets regime. It says publishers can opt out of certain AI uses of their content, Google must improve attribution and submit compliance reports, and the CMA may take further action as the changes roll out. Google has nine months to implement all changes, with some controls expected sooner.

title: LB Group / Venator UK (TiO2 assets) merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has issued a notice confirming that the merger notice for LB Group’s proposed acquisition of Venator UK TiO2-related assets meets the Enterprise Act requirements. The initial merger review period starts on 18 March 2026, and the CMA’s deadline to decide on a phase 2 referral is 15 May 2026. This is relevant to legal and competition-law monitoring, not to financial-services conduct obligations.

title: Review into access to banking services begins
summary: HM Treasury has launched a Call for Evidence for its Access to Banking Review, asking individuals, businesses and organisations to share views on in-person banking access. Responses are due by 20 July 2026, and the review will make recommendations to government in October 2026. The news item also notes possible future legislation if evidence shows intervention is needed.

title: Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) market orders and calculator
summary: The CMA has published updated LPG market orders, an annual tank transfer calculator, and guidance for suppliers covered by the domestic bulk LPG market investigation remedies. Suppliers must follow the order requirements, including annual switching data submissions by the first working day of July for data covering 1 June 2025 to 31 May 2026.

title: CMA investigates Ryanair over charging parents to sit with children
summary: The CMA has announced an investigation into Ryanair’s mandatory family seat charges and booking-price presentation, to assess possible unfair contract terms and drip pricing under consumer law. This is an early-stage press release, not a decision or new rule. No immediate action date is stated, and the CMA says it has reached no conclusions.

title: Next steps for veterinary services for household pets: what the CMA's remedies mean in practice
summary: CMA speech explaining next steps on remedies for household pet veterinary services. It describes planned binding Orders, funding measures and phased implementation, including quicker contract obligations for out-of-hours providers and an 18-month period for complaints information. The speech also previews future consultation on levy funding and notes the remedies are aimed at veterinary businesses.

title: Spreadex / Sporting Index merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has made an Initial Enforcement Order in the Spreadex/Sporting Index merger inquiry. Spreadex TopCo and Spreadex must keep the businesses separate, preserve assets and staff, and avoid integration or information sharing unless the CMA consents. The order starts on 2024-01-15 and applies until the merger reference is finally determined.

title: Competition law: guide for public authorities
summary: The CMA published a guidance note for officials in public authorities explaining how competition law may apply to their day-to-day work. It is informational only and does not create new obligations for firms.

title: Government publishes Terms of Reference for Wholesale Digital Markets Champion
summary: HM Treasury announces the Terms of Reference for the Wholesale Digital Markets Champion, who will convene industry on tokenisation, DLT adoption and interoperability in UK wholesale markets. The Champion must produce an initial forward look by July 2026 and a report to the Chancellor by July 2027. The role runs for 18 months and is ongoing for strategy promotion and coordination with AST and DEMAT.

title: ABF / Hovis merger inquiry
summary: The CMA published a notice that the merger notice for ABF’s anticipated acquisition of Hovis meets the statutory requirements under the Enterprise Act 2002. It states the CMA’s initial review period starts on 22 December 2025 and the deadline to announce a phase 2 referral decision is 19 February 2026.

title: UK issues largest penalty for financial sanctions breaches since Russia’s 2022 illegal invasion of Ukraine
summary: HM Treasury/OFSI has imposed a £1,000,920.59 penalty on Sabre Global Technologies Limited for breaches and circumvention of UK Russia sanctions, the largest such penalty since 2022. The case highlights failures in senior oversight, payment controls and sanctions risk management, and is the third penalty under OFSI’s new settlement policy introduced in February 2026.

title: Referral of the proposed Business Rates Relief for Electric Vehicle (EV) chargepoints and EV-only forecourts by HM Treasury
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its final report on HM Treasury’s proposed business rates relief scheme for EV chargepoints and EV-only forecourts. The report evaluates HMT’s assessment under the Subsidy Control Act 2022. It is informational for firms; the document does not itself change requirements or set a compliance deadline.

title: Further CMA action to secure a fairer deal for businesses and improve Google search services in UK
summary: CMA press release announcing two new conduct requirements for Google’s UK general search services: fair ranking and data portability. Google has 6 months to implement the fair ranking requirement and 3 months for data portability. The release says the CMA will monitor compliance and may add further measures, but it is not itself the legal instrument.

title: Google's general search and search advertising services
summary: The CMA has started an SMS investigation into Google’s general search and search advertising services under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024. It sets the scope of the investigation, identifies Google entities in scope, and says the CMA must issue its decision by 13 October 2025 unless the period is extended. This is an investigation notice, not a rule or enforcement action.

title: Ambition to end era of ‘outsourcing by default’ as government looks to bring cleaners and security staff in-house
summary: The UK government announced new procurement guidance and a Public Interest Test to support bringing some outsourced public services back in-house, including cleaning, security and building management. It applies to central government departments with over £100 million in annual contract spend and to contracts over £1 million. The move is to be applied as current contracts end, with some services targeted from 2028.

title: CMA orders Marks Electrical to refund customers over pre-selected extra charges
summary: CMA press release says Marks Electrical must refund about 40,000 customers and pay a £720,000 fine after automatically opting shoppers into paid extras without express agreement. The conduct was investigated under the CMA’s strengthened consumer powers for activity from April 2025 to November 2025. This is an enforcement announcement, not the notice itself.

title: Government procurement to prioritise national security
summary: HMT announced news about new procurement guidance that will prioritise national security and supply chain resilience in public spending, alongside letters to accounting officers and sector leads. It is a government news item, not the guidance itself, and it does not impose direct obligations on firms. The publication highlights future procurement approaches and awards to British firms.

title: Suzano / Kimberly-Clark JV merger inquiry
summary: The CMA published a merger notice for the anticipated joint venture between Suzano SA and Kimberly-Clark Corporation. It confirms the merger notice meets the statutory requirements and states the phase 1 initial period starts on 30 March 2026, with the CMA’s referral decision deadline on 28 May 2026.

title: Government fraud squad hunts down Covid loan scams
summary: HM Treasury says a new government fraud squad has started investigating Covid loan fraud and will use expanded powers, including search, seizure, information-gathering and direct recovery from bank accounts and wages. The post is a press release and says the new powers will become available this autumn, with the limitation period for civil claims extended to 12 years under the PAFER Act 2025.

title: Microsoft’s business software ecosystem
summary: The CMA has opened an initial Strategic Market Status investigation into Microsoft’s business software ecosystem under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024. It covers Microsoft’s productivity suite, PC and server operating systems, RDBMS and security software, and may include Copilot/AI features. No firm action is required yet, but the scope could change during the investigation.

title: Getting money back if the CMA orders refunds or compensation
summary: CMA guidance page explaining that, where it has found consumer law breaches, it has ordered named businesses to refund or compensate customers directly. It lists the AA/BSM, Marks Electrical and StubHub UK cases, the affected customer groups, and refund processing deadlines extending to December 2026 and June/April 2027.

title: Great British Summer Savings: Tax cut on kids’ meals and days out goes live
summary: HMT issued a press release announcing a temporary VAT cut on eligible children’s meals and family days out, effective from 25 June 2026, alongside free bus travel for children in England in August. It is aimed at families and participating leisure, hospitality and transport businesses, not at regulated financial firms.

title: Review of the effectiveness of the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and its impact on competition and investment in the UK
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its first statutory report on the effectiveness of the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and its impact on competition and investment in the UK. It is an information and advice to government publication, with no direct requirements for firms. The report was published on 25 June 2026 and relates to the subsidy control regime’s first reporting period ending 31 March 2026.

title: Referral of the proposed subsidy to Athletic Ventures LLP by UK Sport and the Greater London Authority
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its report on a proposed subsidy from UK Sport and the Greater London Authority to Athletic Ventures LLP. It is an evaluation of the authorities’ assessment of compliance under the Subsidy Control Act 2022, with third-party submissions invited by the deadline in the timetable. No direct obligations are created for financial services firms.

title: CMA letter to PHIN welcoming achievement of gold compliance milestone
summary: CMA congratulates PHIN on reaching the Gold milestone under the Private Healthcare Market Investigation Order 2014, noting private hospitals and consultants are complying with transparency requirements. It says compliance with the Order remains a priority, but this is a supervisory-style update and not a new rule or obligation.

title: Getty Images / Shutterstock merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has issued a procedural notice on the anticipated Getty Images/Shutterstock merger under the Enterprise Act 2002, stating the initial period starts on 26 August 2025 and the CMA’s phase 2 referral deadline is 20 October 2025. This is a competition-law market notice, not a financial-services rule or supervisory publication.

title: UK financial system strengthened with new safeguards for major technology providers
primary_functions: Operational resilience; Compliance; Risk; InfoSec; Board
summary: HMT has designated four major cloud/technology providers as Critical Third Parties for UK financial services, bringing them under joint oversight by the Bank, PRA and FCA. The regime starts from 13 July 2026 and is aimed at improving resilience of critical outsourced services used by banks, insurers and financial market infrastructures.

title: Chancellor to unlock billions in finance for small businesses
summary: HMT issued a press release announcing expanded support for small business lending, including a larger British Business Bank Growth Guarantee Scheme, £500 million for innovative SMEs, and additional support for community lenders and exporters. It also says the government will remove legislative barriers for building societies that want to lend to SMEs and accelerate Open Finance development. No direct rule change is made in this press release.

title: UK’s heating oil households need stronger protections, says CMA
summary: CMA press release on its heating oil market study. It says households need stronger protections and recommends governments consider a new regulatory regime for heating oil suppliers, plus possible compensation for affected customers. The CMA says it will keep engaging with suppliers and may take court-based enforcement action where compensation is not paid voluntarily.

title: Government delivers fairer deal for shoppers as Buy-Now, Pay-Later rules come into force
summary: HMT announces that new Buy-Now, Pay-Later consumer protections have come into force, including affordability checks, clearer refund rights and access to FCA/FOS protections. The measures apply from 15 July 2026 and are aimed at BNPL providers such as Klarna, PayPal and Clearpay. This is a government press release about the change, not the rulemaking instrument itself.

title: Referral of the proposed Low Carbon Fuels Fund subsidy scheme by the Department for Transport
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published a final report on the Department for Transport’s proposed Low Carbon Fuels Fund subsidy scheme. It evaluates DfT’s assessment under the Subsidy Control Act 2022 and invites any third-party submissions on the scheme. No direct obligations are created for firms; the document is informational and consultative.

title: Care workers to be represented in fair pay agreements
summary: The government announced a press release on plans for a new Adult Social Care Negotiating Body and a first fair pay agreement for care workers in England, backed by £500 million. Negotiations are due to start in April 2027, with the first settlement expected by April 2028. This is a policy announcement, not a binding rule for financial firms.

title: Parking charges: CMA takes action to drive improvements for motorists
summary: The CMA announced a press release on private parking charges, launching an investigation into Euro Car Parks, writing to other operators, and publishing tips for motorists. It also made recommendations to government on a new Code of Practice and urged the sector to improve appeals handling and additional charges. No binding requirements are created by the press release itself.

title: Open letter to the private parking sector
summary: The CMA has published an open letter to private parking operators setting out concerns about consumer law compliance and asking operators to review their practices, terms and appeals processes now. It also references related CMA actions, including advisory letters, an investigation, and a letter to government. The letter is not itself a rule or binding requirement.

title: CMA letter to government in relation to private parking
summary: The CMA wrote to government with recommendations for possible changes to the private parking code and said it may consider enforcement action against some parking operators. It is not a rule, consultation or enforcement notice; it is an intelligence/advice publication aimed at informing policy development in the private parking sector.

title: eBay / Depop merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has published a merger notice for eBay’s proposed acquisition of Depop and says the initial merger review period starts on 9 June 2026. The CMA’s deadline to decide whether to refer the merger for a phase 2 investigation is 6 August 2026.

title: Writing a fair contract for customers
summary: The CMA has published guidance on unfair contract terms and consumer notices under the Consumer Rights Act 2015. It explains how businesses should draft fair, transparent terms, what may be unfair or exempt, and examples of prohibited wording. It applies to trader-consumer contracts and notices, including standard terms and EULAs; no new deadline or binding rule is introduced.

title: Referral of the proposed British Industrial Competitiveness Scheme by the Department for Business and Trade
summary: The CMA’s Subsidy Advice Unit published its final report on the Department for Business and Trade’s proposed British Industrial Competitiveness Scheme. The report evaluates DBT’s assessment of compliance with the Subsidy Control Act 2022. The scheme is proposed to launch in April 2027, but this publication itself is an advisory report, not a rule or requirement for firms.

title: Collaborating with other businesses
summary: The CMA has published a short guidance note for businesses that want to collaborate with other firms without breaching competition law. It explains the CMA’s role in supporting legitimate collaboration and points readers to further contact information and sustainability-specific material. No new obligations or deadlines are set out.

title: Budget to move “power and money out of Westminster, and into every postcode around Britain”.
summary: HM Treasury announces that the Chancellor’s first Budget will be on Wednesday 28 October 2026. It also opens a Budget Representation Portal for comments on existing policy, closing at 23:59 on Wednesday 9 September 2026, which will be shared with Treasury policy officials.

title: Healthcare Ireland / Hutchinson Homes merger inquiry
summary: The CMA has made an Initial Order in a completed merger inquiry involving Healthcare Ireland Limited and Hutchinson Homes Limited. It restricts integration and certain changes to the businesses, and requires the parties to keep them separate pending the CMA’s determination. The order applies from 2 June 2026 and is addressed to the Acquirer Group and Hutchinson Homes.

title: Vodafone / CK Hutchison JV merger inquiry
summary: The CMA is inviting comments on the proposed Vodafone/CK Hutchison joint venture merger and asking interested parties to submit views by 1 November 2023. This is an initial information-gathering notice ahead of a formal merger investigation, not a decision or binding rule.

title: Charter for Budget Responsibility: autumn 2021 update
summary: HMT presents an updated Charter for Budget Responsibility for parliamentary approval. It restates the government’s fiscal objectives, debt management framework and guidance to the OBR under the Budget Responsibility and National Audit Act 2011. It applies to fiscal policy and public debt management rather than bank conduct rules, and is relevant for monitoring macro/prudential impacts.

title: Treasury Minutes – December 2021
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes respond to the Public Accounts Committee on several topics, including the COVID-19 cost tracker, with updates on actions already taken and intended follow-up letters. It is a government response document, not a rule, consultation, or supervisory notice, and it does not create new requirements for firms.

title: Summary of Financial Inclusion Policy Forum meeting December 2021
summary: HMT published a summary of the December 2021 Financial Inclusion Policy Forum meeting. It is a policy paper describing discussions between government, regulators, industry and the third sector on financial inclusion, with no new rules, deadlines or obligations.

title: Treasury Minutes – January 2022
summary: HM Treasury’s January 2022 Treasury Minutes set out the government’s responses to Public Accounts Committee reports across defence, test and trace, Crossrail, DWP fraud and error, and Greensill-related issues. It is a parliamentary/government response document, not a rule, guidance or notice. No direct obligations are created for firms, though it references ongoing and planned government reviews and implementation dates in the public sector.

title: Public service pensions increase: 2022
summary: HM Treasury published the 2022 public service pensions increase multiplier tables. Public service pensions, preserved pensions and lump sums will increase by 3.1% from 11 April 2022, with the related Pensions Increase (Review) Order expected to be laid in March 2022.

title: Basic bank accounts: July 2020 to June 2021
summary: HM Treasury published its annual statistical update on basic bank accounts for July 2020 to June 2021. It reports account numbers and market distribution for the nine designated providers under the Payment Accounts Regulations 2015, but does not itself change rules or set new deadlines.

title: Minutes of the Trade Specialised Committee on VAT Administrative Cooperation and Recovery of Taxes: 15 December 2021
summary: Minutes of the first UK-EU Trade Specialised Committee meeting on VAT administrative cooperation and recovery of taxes under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement. It records discussion only and does not create new rules or deadlines for firms.

title: Review of the UK funds regime: a call for input
summary: HM Treasury published a call for input summary on the UK funds regime review, setting out respondent feedback and the government’s intended next steps. It signals possible future changes to fund taxation, authorised fund structures and the authorisation process, but does not itself change rules or impose deadlines.

title: Treasury Minutes – February 2022
summary: HM Treasury’s February 2022 Treasury Minute is a government response to Public Accounts Committee reports on several departments’ programmes, including Green Homes Grant, efficiency in government, policing data, digital change, and environmental land management. It sets out whether the government accepts recommendations and its intended next steps, including some target implementation timing such as Summer 2022. It does not create financial-services obligations.

title: Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes Minutes: 21 December 2021
summary: Minutes of the first meeting of the UK-EU Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes, held on 21 December 2021 and published on 25 February 2022. It records discussion of participation in Union programmes under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement, with no new rules, deadlines, or obligations for firms.

title: Joint Exchequer Committee (Scotland) – 3 February 2022
summary: This is a short HMT policy paper noting that the UK and Scottish finance ministers held talks on 3 February about the upcoming review of the Scottish Government’s Fiscal Framework. It does not announce any rule, deadline, or requirement for firms.

title: HM Treasury’s review of Pool Reinsurance Company Limited 2020-2022
summary: HM Treasury published its final review of Pool Re for 2020-2022, setting out agreed strategic changes for the terrorism reinsurance scheme over the next five years. The report supports moving to a treaty reinsurance system, developing proposals to return more risk to the market, and encouraging wider SME uptake of terrorism insurance. It is a policy review and does not itself create new binding obligations for banks.

title: HM Treasury and Financial Conduct Authority Regulatory Perimeter Meeting - December 2021
summary: HM Treasury published a record of a December 2021 meeting between the Economic Secretary and the FCA CEO discussing the FCA’s annual Perimeter Report and the financial services regulatory perimeter. It is an informational record only and does not change perimeter rules or impose deadlines.

title: Removing the impact of changes in inflation from the welfare cap
summary: HMT publishes a policy note explaining how it will strip out the effect of inflation changes when assessing spending against the welfare cap. It sets out the intended treatment, bottom-up methodology and assumptions used in the accompanying spreadsheet; no bank-specific obligations are created.

title: Spring Statement 2022: documents
summary: This is HM Treasury’s Spring Statement 2022, a government fiscal and economic statement setting out tax, spending and cost-of-living measures, including changes to National Insurance thresholds and fuel duty. It is a policy document and not a regulatory rule, consultation, supervisory notice or enforcement action. Any impacts on firms are indirect and depend on the measures announced becoming law.

title: Government response to the 2021 Fiscal Risks Report
summary: HM Treasury’s response to the OBR’s 2021 Fiscal Risks Report explains how the government will manage public-finance risks from debt, COVID-19 and climate change. It reiterates the new fiscal rules, the move to an annual sustainability report, and wider use of OBR analysis. No firm-specific obligations or compliance dates are set for regulated firms.

title: Temporary Cut to Fuel Duty
summary: The UK government announced a temporary 5 pence per litre cut to fuel duty for petrol and diesel across the UK for 12 months, effective from 6pm on 23 March 2022. This is a fiscal measure affecting consumers and fuel users, not a financial-services rule change, but it may have indirect cost impacts for firms with transport or fuel exposure.

title: Spring Statement 2022: Business support factsheet
summary: HMT published a factsheet listing Spring Statement 2021 measures intended to support UK businesses. It is an informational policy paper and does not itself set new requirements or deadlines.

title: Debt management report 2022 to 2023
summary: HM Treasury’s annual debt management report sets out the government’s borrowing plans, debt management framework and the DMO/NS&I/exchequer cash management remits for 2022-23. It is informational and policy-setting rather than a firm-specific rule. The publication was issued in March 2022 and does not create direct obligations for banks.

title: Spring Statement 2022: Factsheet on Personal Tax
summary: HM Treasury announced changes to National Insurance and income tax thresholds and rates, including raising the NIC Primary Threshold and Lower Profits Limit from July 2022 and cutting the basic rate of income tax from April 2024. The factsheet explains transitional timing for employees and the self-employed and impacts on payroll and tax treatment.

title: Explanatory memorandum on EU directive 2006/112 (6158/22, COM(2022)39)
summary: HM Treasury explains an EU proposal to extend VAT Directive Articles 199a and 199b, keeping the optional reverse charge mechanism and quick reaction mechanism in place until 31 December 2025. It is relevant to UK/Northern Ireland VAT alignment and was published on 24 March 2022. The document itself is explanatory and does not create new UK obligations.

title: National Insurance Contributions (Increase of Thresholds) Bill
summary: Draft legislation proposes to raise National Insurance contribution thresholds for Class 1, Class 2 and Class 4 contributions, with some changes applying from 6 April 2022, 6 July 2022 and 6 April 2023. It also requires Treasury regulations to align Class 2 thresholds with Class 4. This is relevant to employers and self-employed payroll/tax arrangements.

title: Joint statement by HM Treasury, the CMA, the FCA and the PSR on the future of Open Banking
summary: HM Treasury, the FCA, the PSR and the CMA issued a joint statement on plans for future oversight of Open Banking and a new entity to succeed the OBIE. It outlines intended governance, funding and oversight arrangements, but does not create new binding requirements or set an implementation date.

title: Sovereign Grant Act 2011: report of the Royal Trustees on the Sovereign Grant for 2022-23
summary: This is an HMT report to Parliament explaining how the Sovereign Grant for 2022-23 was calculated under the Sovereign Grant Act 2011. It is informational and sets out the statutory methodology and background, but it does not create new requirements for regulated firms.

title: Centre for Finance, Innovation and Technology - Steering Committee
summary: HM Treasury published a policy paper announcing the Centre for Finance, Innovation and Technology steering committee and its terms of reference. The committee is meeting through spring and summer 2022 to develop non-binding recommendations for a future private-sector-led body to support UK fintech innovation. No firm obligations, dates for compliance, or rules are created for regulated firms.

title: User and Preparer Advisory Group Minutes: October 2021
summary: HM Treasury published minutes and agenda for the Government Financial Reporting User and Preparer Advisory Group meeting held on 4 October 2021. The paper records discussion topics including central government reporting, thematic reviews, sustainability reporting, Whole of Government Accounts, BEIS consultation and performance framework updates. It does not create new rules or deadlines.

title: Government financial reporting review: Best practice examples from 2020-21
summary: HM Treasury publishes examples of best-practice narrative and accountability reporting for 2020-21 government annual reports and accounts. It highlights how central government entities should present performance, risk, governance, financial information, COVID-19 and EU exit impacts, and diversity data. The note is for reference by preparers across government and does not create new obligations.

title: Treasury Minutes –  7 April 2022
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes is the government’s response to Committee of Public Accounts reports on a range of public-sector issues, including gigabit broadband, state pension underpayments, local government finance and NHS payment schemes. It records agreed actions and target implementation dates for those departments, but it does not create obligations for FCA/PRA-regulated firms.

title: User and Preparer Advisory Group Minutes: April 2022
summary: Minutes and agenda for a HMT Government Financial Reporting User and Preparer Advisory Group meeting held on 7 April 2022. The paper records updates on government financial reporting topics, including WGA, central and local government reporting, sustainability reporting and a thematic review. It is informational only and does not create obligations.

title: World Bank Spring Meetings 2022: UK Governor’s statement
summary: The UK Governor’s statement for the World Bank Spring Meetings urges the World Bank, IMF and international community to provide more support for Ukraine, its neighbours and developing countries. It is a political/international policy statement, not a regulatory rule or supervisory requirement, and it sets no firm-specific deadline or obligation.

title: Protecting UK wholesale cash infrastructure
summary: HM Treasury sets out plans to protect UK wholesale cash infrastructure as cash use declines. It explains the case for future legislation and possible Bank of England oversight and prudential powers over wholesale cash entities, but does not itself create new requirements. The regime would be designated and brought forward when parliamentary time allows.

title: Treasury Minutes – 26 April 2022
summary: Treasury Minutes is the government’s response to the Committee of Public Accounts on several 2021-22 reports. It sets out how departments will implement recommendations, including updates on border planning, HMRC performance, spending data and other public sector issues, with some target implementation dates in 2022 and 2023. It is informational and does not itself create new rules for firms.

title: Potential Reforms to UK’s Capital Allowance Regime – Inviting views
summary: HMT published a policy paper inviting views on potential reforms to the UK capital allowances regime. It asks businesses to respond by 1 July 2022 and says the government is considering options ahead of a later Budget. This is a consultation-style invitation for evidence, not a final change.

title: Government approach to authorised push payment scam reimbursement
summary: The government sets out its approach to reimbursing victims of authorised push payment scams and says it intends to legislate in the Financial Services and Markets Bill to enable the Payment Systems Regulator to require reimbursement by banks and other payment service providers. This is a policy paper, not the legislation or a final rule.

title: Terms of engagement between HM Treasury and Pool Reinsurance Limited (Pool Re)
summary: HM Treasury published an updated Framework Agreement with Pool Re setting out governance, accountability, reporting, audit and information-sharing arrangements. It applies to Pool Re and any ONS-classified subsidiaries or joint ventures, and should be reviewed periodically by HM Treasury and Pool Re. The document describes existing operating arrangements rather than creating new regulatory rules.

title: Treasury Minutes – May 2022
summary: HM Treasury published the May 2022 Treasury Minutes, which is the Government’s response to the Committee of Public Accounts on several departments’ reports from Session 2021-22. It records departmental responses and target implementation dates for recommendations, including action on criminal courts backlog, NHS backlogs, trade negotiations, COVID-19 preparedness, academies and tax debt.

title: Overall government support for the cost of living: factsheet
summary: HM Treasury published a factsheet summarising government support for households with the cost of living in 2022-23. It is an informational policy paper only and does not set out regulatory requirements, deadlines or obligations for firms.

title: Treasury Minutes progress report – June 2022
summary: This is a Treasury progress report to Parliament tracking implementation of previously accepted Public Accounts Committee recommendations across many government sessions. It does not set new rules or obligations for firms, but provides status updates on public sector recommendations and revised target dates where relevant.

title: Inaugural UK-Japan Financial Regulatory Forum
summary: HM Treasury published a policy paper on the inaugural UK-Japan Financial Regulatory Forum and the Exchange of Letters signed with Japan’s Financial Services Agency. The document describes a cooperation framework under the UK-Japan trade agreement, including information exchange, consultation, deference, technical mediation and working groups on topics such as sustainable finance, diversity and financial innovation. No direct obligations or compliance deadline are set out for firms.

title: Cost of Living Support
summary: HM Treasury’s Cost of Living Support package includes a new Energy Profits Levy technical note and factsheets. It announces a new tax on the profits of oil and gas companies operating in the UK and UK Continental Shelf, with application timing and next steps explained from 26 May 2022. The publication is aimed at affected oil and gas companies and supporting tax policy context, not new FCA/PRA rules.

title: United Kingdom Debt Management Office Annual Business Plan 2022-23
summary: HM Treasury’s Debt Management Office sets out its 2022-23 business plan, including planned gilt issuance, cash management, green gilt issuance, stakeholder engagement and operational resilience objectives. It also reviews 2021-22 performance and governance. This is an informational annual plan for government debt-management operations, not a rule, consultation or supervisory notice.

title: Review of the UK’s AML/CFT regulatory and supervisory regime
summary: HM Treasury published a review of the UK’s AML/CFT regulatory and supervisory regime, covering effectiveness of the Money Laundering Regulations, supervisory gaps and possible reform areas. It is an informational policy paper, not a rule or consultation, and does not itself change obligations. It is aimed at firms subject to AML/CFT controls, especially banks and other regulated businesses.

title: Summary of Financial Inclusion Policy Forum meeting May 2022
summary: HMT published a summary of the ninth Financial Inclusion Policy Forum meeting, held on 10 May 2022. It is an informational policy paper about collaboration on financial inclusion across government and the sector, with no new rules, deadlines or obligations.

title: Independent Report preceding the Fiscal Framework review: terms of reference
summary: HM Treasury published terms of reference for an independent report preceding the Fiscal Framework review. It is a policy paper setting out the remit of the report, not a rule, consultation, or binding requirement for firms.

title: Joint Statement on the U.S.-UK Financial Innovation Partnership Meeting 29th June 2022
summary: HMT published a joint UK-U.S. statement on the Financial Innovation Partnership meeting held on 29 June 2022. It is an informational update on discussions about crypto and digital asset ecosystems and cooperation between financial authorities, with no new rules, deadlines or obligations.

title: Financial Reporting Advisory Board annual report: 2021 to 2022
summary: HMT’s Financial Reporting Advisory Board annual report for 2021-22 summarises the board’s advisory work on public sector financial reporting, including monitoring the reporting cycle, accounting standards and sustainability reporting. It is an informational annual report with no direct obligations or deadlines for firms.

title: Scottish Income Tax outturn reconciliation for 2020-21
summary: HMT explains how published 2020-21 Income Tax outturn data will be used to reconcile Scottish Government funding. It says the reconciliation reduces Scottish self-funding by £417m, increases the block grant by £468m, and leaves a net £50m increase for 2023-24. This is informational for Scotland and does not create obligations for firms.

title: Welsh Rates of Income Tax outturn reconciliation for 2020-21
summary: HMT published an explanatory policy paper on the 2020-21 Welsh Rates of Income Tax outturn reconciliation. It explains how HMRC’s actual 2020-21 income tax data is used to update Welsh Government funding, with a net £48 million increase in overall funding for 2023-24. Applies to Wales.

title: National Insurance Fund Investment Account Report & Accounts 2021 to 2022
summary: HMT/CRND published the National Insurance Fund Investment Account report and accounts for the year ended 31 March 2022. It is an annual government accounts publication describing investment performance, balances and audit information; it does not impose new rules or obligations on firms.

title: Global Anti-Corruption Programme
summary: HMT/FCDO published a policy paper on the Global Anti-Corruption Programme, describing UK support for anti-corruption projects delivered through March 2022 in Colombia, Indonesia, Malaysia, Mexico and South Africa. It explains the programme’s aims around transparency, beneficial ownership, procurement, stolen assets and good practice, but does not set new requirements for firms.

title: Levelling Up Fund Round 2: prospectus
summary: HMT/DLUHC and DfT published a prospectus giving guidance on how local areas can bid for Round 2 of the Levelling Up Fund. It explains who can apply across the UK and says the fund will run until 2024/25. This is informational guidance for local authorities and other local applicants, not a binding rule for firms.

title: Treasury Minutes – July 2022
summary: Treasury Minutes is HMT’s government response to Public Accounts Committee reports across several departments. It includes commentary and intended reforms such as the renters’ property portal, abolition of section 21 evictions, and a new ombudsman for private landlords, with some rollout milestones through Summer 2026. It does not itself create binding obligations for firms.

title: Joint Exchequer Committee (Scotland) – 27 June 2022
summary: HM Treasury published a communique from the Joint Exchequer Committee (Scotland) covering talks on 27 June 2022 about the upcoming review of the Scottish Government’s Fiscal Framework. It is a policy paper and does not set rules, deadlines, or obligations for firms.

title: Finance Bill 2021-2022: Report Stage
