summary: This Finance Bill report stage sets out technical amendments to Schedule 2 creating the qualifying asset holding company regime. The changes clarify definitions, cross-references, control tests and fund-related rules for asset holding companies used in investment structures. As primary legislation, it is binding once enacted; the publication itself does not give a separate compliance deadline.

title: Departmental Minute from HM Treasury: UK Infrastructure Bank Guarantees
summary: HM Treasury published a departmental minute notifying Parliament of a proposed contingent liability for up to £10 billion of UK Infrastructure Bank guarantees. It is an informational policy paper about intended government support for infrastructure investment and does not impose requirements on firms.

title: UK-U.S. Financial Regulatory Working Group
summary: HM Treasury and the U.S. Treasury published a joint statement on the sixth meeting of the UK-U.S. Financial Regulatory Working Group. It summarises the main themes and topics discussed at the 21 July 2022 meeting and does not announce new rules, deadlines or obligations.

title: Treasury minutes - August 2022
summary: Treasury Minutes records the government’s responses to Public Accounts Committee reports across several departments, including IR35 implementation by HMRC. It sets out departmental reactions and target implementation dates for some follow-up actions, but does not itself create new regulatory requirements for firms. Relevant only as background and intelligence.

title: Government response to the National Infrastructure Commission report Infrastructure, Towns and Regeneration
summary: HMT published a policy paper giving the government’s response to the National Infrastructure Commission’s report on infrastructure, towns and regeneration. It is a commentary on recommendations about transport and digital infrastructure in England, not a rule, consultation, or binding requirement.

title: Memorandum of understanding between the Scottish Fiscal Commission and HMT
summary: HM Treasury published a memorandum of understanding with the Scottish Fiscal Commission setting out how the two bodies will co-operate so the Commission can obtain the information it needs for independent forecasts and evaluation of Scottish Government devolved income revenue and social security expenditure. It is an informational policy paper rather than a financial-services rule or supervisory notice.

title: The Growth Plan 2022: documents
summary: HM Treasury’s Growth Plan 2022 is a policy paper and government announcement setting out tax cuts, energy support, investment zones and wider growth measures. It is a high-level policy statement rather than binding financial-services regulation. Some measures were intended to take effect from 23 September 2022 or later, but the document itself is not a rule or supervisory notice.

title: The Growth Plan 2022: Factsheet on Stamp Duty Land Tax
summary: The Chancellor announced changes to Stamp Duty Land Tax for England and Northern Ireland in the 23 September 2022 Growth Plan. This factsheet explains the measure and is relevant to firms and customers involved in affected property transactions. The announcement indicates an immediate tax-policy change rather than a consultation.

title: The Growth Plan: Factsheet on cancellation of National Insurance rise and Health and Social Care Levy
summary: HMT published a factsheet explaining the cancellation of the April 2022 National Insurance rise and the April 2023 Health and Social Care Levy, following legislation introduced to Parliament on 23 September 2022. The change affects employers and payroll administration and is part of the Growth Plan measures.

title: The Growth Plan 2022: Factsheet on Investment Zones
summary: HMT published a factsheet describing proposed Investment Zones and noting early discussions with 38 local authorities in England, plus plans to work with devolved administrations. It is an informational policy paper about intended tax and planning changes to encourage development and investment, with no direct obligations or deadlines for firms.

title: The Growth Plan 2022: Factsheet on Corporation Tax
summary: HM Treasury published a factsheet explaining the Chancellor’s announcement that the planned Corporation Tax rate rise would be cancelled. This is a policy paper and informational summary only; it does not itself change tax law or set an implementation date.

title: The Growth Plan 2022: Factsheet on Income Tax
summary: HM Treasury published a factsheet explaining the Chancellor’s announced changes to the Basic and Additional Rates of Income Tax in the Growth Plan 2022. It is an informational policy paper, not the legal measure itself, and it does not set any firm-specific obligations or deadlines.

title: Treasury Minutes – September 2022
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes responds to Committee of Public Accounts reports on child maintenance, secure training centres, British Steel Pension Scheme, the Police Uplift Programme and cross-border travel. It sets out the Government’s position and intended follow-up actions, including some target implementation dates in the responses, but it does not create financial-services regulatory requirements.

title: Advisory Committee
summary: HM Treasury published a policy paper describing the Advisory Committee’s role and membership. The committee provides advisory support on government credit risk and bespoke financial intervention cases, including under the Energy Markets Financing Scheme. This is informational only and does not create firm obligations.

title: Economic Advisory Council – Terms of Reference
summary: HMT published the terms of reference for an Economic Advisory Council announced by the Chancellor. It is an informational policy paper setting out the council’s purpose and membership concept; it does not create regulatory requirements for firms.

title: User and Preparer Advisory Group Minutes: October 2022
summary: Minutes of an HMT advisory group meeting on government financial reporting, including updates on central and local government reporting, the Whole of Government Accounts timetable, thematic reviews, sustainability reporting, IPSASB/ICAEW matters and IFRS 17. It is an informational meeting record only and does not set requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: Joint Statement: UK – U.S. Covered Agreement. Second meeting on the Joint Committee
summary: HM Treasury, the US Treasury and the U.S. Trade Representative issued a joint statement on the second meeting of the UK–U.S. covered agreement Joint Committee. It summarises discussion areas on the bilateral prudential agreement for insurance and reinsurance; it does not set new requirements or dates.

title: Treasury Minutes – November 2022
summary: HMT published its November 2022 Treasury Minutes, a government response to Public Accounts Committee reports on NHS England COVID-19 vaccination, PPE contracts, and Randox contracts. It sets out the government’s responses and commentary, but does not create regulatory requirements for firms. No action date or compliance deadline is stated.

title: Autumn Statement 2022: documents
summary: HMT’s Autumn Statement 2022 sets out the government’s fiscal and tax plans, including changes to income tax thresholds, dividend and capital gains allowances, National Insurance thresholds, energy profits taxation and business rates support. It is a policy and budget announcement, not a regulatory rule or supervisory notice. No direct compliance deadline is created by this publication itself.

title: Autumn Statement 2022: Energy Taxes Factsheet
summary: HM Treasury’s Autumn Statement 2022 factsheet announces changes to the Energy Profits Levy and the introduction of a new Electricity Generator Tax. This is a government tax-policy publication, relevant to affected energy companies, with the policy changes described on 17 November 2022.

title: Autumn Statement 2022: Business Rates Factsheet
summary: This HMT factsheet announces the Autumn Statement 2022 business rates package worth £13.6 billion, including support for ratepayers facing higher bills from 1 April 2023 valuations. It is a policy paper explaining government measures, not a binding rule or guidance for firms.

title: Terms of Reference: Review of the Energy Bill Relief Scheme
summary: HM Treasury published terms of reference for a review of the Energy Bill Relief Scheme, setting out the review’s context, scope, governance and timetable for reporting. It is an information document about the review process, not a rule change or binding requirement.

title: Autumn Statement 2022: Cost of living support Factsheet
summary: HMT published a factsheet explaining the Autumn Statement 2022 cost of living support package for households. It describes income support, energy bill help, benefits uprating, tax changes and the National Living Wage, plus winter support examples. It is informational and does not create obligations for firms.

title: Minutes of the Trade Specialised Committee on VAT Administrative Cooperation and Recovery of Taxes: 6 October 2022
summary: HMT published minutes of the second UK-EU Trade Specialised Committee on VAT Administrative Cooperation and Recovery of Taxes, held on 6 October 2022. The paper describes the committee’s forum under the TCA for VAT cooperation, anti-fraud coordination and mutual assistance on tax recovery. It does not create new requirements or deadlines.

title: Memorandum of Understanding on the United Kingdom-Singapore FinTech Bridge
summary: HM Treasury and the Monetary Authority of Singapore signed a non-binding Memorandum of Understanding to strengthen UK-Singapore FinTech cooperation, including regular policy discussions, joint innovation work and support for firms exploring both markets. It takes effect on signature and has no direct regulatory requirements for firms.

title: EM on EU regulation 389/2012 (13979/22, COM(2022)539)
summary: HM Treasury issued an explanatory memorandum on an EU proposal to amend Regulation 389/2012 on excise-duty administrative cooperation and electronic registers. It says the change extends information exchange for duty-paid movements in the EU and in Northern Ireland, but creates no new business obligations and is not expected to have UK business impact.

title: Environmental Impacts of Spending Review 2021
summary: HM Treasury published an analytical policy paper on the environmental impacts of Spending Review 2021, including environmental ratings and supporting narrative on its assessment approach. It is an informational publication responding to a Public Accounts Committee recommendation, with no new requirements or compliance deadline for firms.

title: Treasury Minutes progress report – December 2022
summary: This is a Treasury progress report to Parliament on how the Government is implementing previously accepted Public Accounts Committee recommendations across many past reports. It is an update document only, with no new regulatory requirements or compliance deadlines for firms.

title: Ring-fencing reforms
summary: HM Treasury published a policy paper responding to the independent review of ring-fencing and proprietary trading. It says the government intends to consult in mid-2023 on near-term reforms and issue a public call for evidence in Q1 2023 on aligning the ring-fencing and resolution regimes.

title: Building a smarter financial services framework for the UK
summary: HM Treasury sets out its implementation plan for replacing retained EU law in UK financial services and moving to a fuller FSMA-based framework. It explains the phased approach, use of the Financial Services and Markets Bill powers, and early focus areas such as wholesale markets, prospectus, securitisation, Solvency II, payments and e-money, and PRIIPs. No direct firm obligations are created in this paper.

title: Treasury Minutes – December 2022
summary: HM Treasury’s December 2022 Treasury Minutes sets out the government’s responses to Committee of Public Accounts reports, including waste crime, regulation after EU exit, whole-of-government accounts, electronic monitoring services and local air quality breaches. It is a response document and progress update, not a rule, guidance or enforcement notice. It contains some target implementation dates and policy intentions, but no direct new obligations for firms.

title: Response to the remit and recommendations for the Financial Policy Committee: December 2022
summary: HMT and the Bank of England publish the FPC’s response to the Chancellor’s remit and recommendations letter. It explains the Committee’s current assessment of financial stability risks, bank resilience, CCyB settings, market-based finance vulnerabilities, and work on LDI funds and energy market financing. It is informational and does not itself create new requirements.

title: Memorandum of Understanding between the UK and the Republic of Chile
summary: HM Treasury published a memorandum of understanding with the Republic of Chile on financial services collaboration. It records both governments’ intent to share best practices and policy developments to support financial stability, consumer protection and growth. It is a policy statement of international cooperation, not a binding rule, and no action date or compliance deadline is set.

title: Joint statement by HM Treasury, the CMA, the FCA and the PSR to update on the future of Open Banking
summary: HM Treasury, the FCA, the PSR and the CMA issued a joint statement updating their plans for the future of UK Open Banking and a successor entity to OBIE. It outlines three priorities—payments, a scalable model and sustainable funding—and describes desired features of the future governance framework, but it does not set binding requirements or dates.

title: Terms of reference for the review of regulation for emerging technologies
summary: HMT publishes terms of reference for Sir Patrick Vallance’s review of how the UK can better regulate emerging technologies. It sets the scope for work on pro-innovation regulation across sectors such as digital technology, life sciences and green industries, with further work to follow on advanced manufacturing and creative industries. This is an information-setting document only.

title: Financial Inclusion Report 2021/22
summary: HMT’s 2021/22 Financial Inclusion Report summarises government work on access to cash, banking, credit, insurance, technology, vulnerable customers, savings and debt support. It is an informational policy report, not a rule change or consultation, though it references the Financial Services and Markets Bill and other ongoing initiatives. No direct obligations are created by the report itself.

title: Women in Finance Charter: Treasury Progress Update
summary: HM Treasury publishes a progress update on its own commitments under the Women in Finance Charter, including that senior female representation rose to 50% by March 2022. It is an informational update on Treasury’s internal progress and future priorities, not a new rule or requirement for firms.

title: Electricity generator levy technical note
summary: HMT’s technical note sets out the proposed design and scope of the Electricity Generator Levy, a new tax on extraordinary returns from UK electricity generation. It is intended to help generators prepare ahead of the levy’s introduction from 1 January 2023 and to inform the legislation. The note is relevant to affected corporate groups and generation activities, including nuclear and renewables.

title: Economic Evidence to the Pay Review Bodies: January 2023
summary: HMT publishes an economic evidence paper for the 2023-24 public sector pay round. It discusses inflation, GDP, labour market conditions and fiscal context to inform Pay Review Bodies’ recommendations, but does not create obligations for firms. No compliance date or regulatory change is set for banks or other FS firms.

title: UK - US financial services co-operation – statement on the seventh meeting of the Financial Regulatory Working Group
summary: HM Treasury and the U.S. Treasury published a joint statement summarising the seventh UK-US Financial Regulatory Working Group meeting in December 2022. It describes discussion themes and future cooperation points; it does not set new rules, deadlines, or obligations for firms.

title: EM on EU regulation 282/2011 (COM(2022)704)
summary: HM Treasury explains EU proposals for VAT in the Digital Age, including changes to marketplace VAT liability, One Stop Shop and e-invoicing, and a new EU data system. It is an explanatory memorandum on draft EU measures, not a UK rule, and the proposals may change before any future implementation. The document notes possible impacts on Northern Ireland and a staged timeline from 2024 to 2030.

title: Treasury Minutes – January 2023
summary: HM Treasury’s January 2023 Treasury Minutes is a government response to Committee of Public Accounts reports. It records ministerial responses and target implementation dates for several cross-government issues, including public sector decarbonisation, animal health infrastructure, energy supplier regulation and fraud/error in benefits. It is informational only and does not itself create new regulatory obligations for firms.

title: Charter for Budget Responsibility: Autumn 2022 update
summary: HMT lays before Parliament the updated Charter for Budget Responsibility under the Budget Responsibility and National Audit Act 2011. It sets out the government’s fiscal mandate, debt management objectives and guidance to the OBR, including welfare cap-related reporting and publication requirements. The document is part of the statutory fiscal framework and applies immediately on publication, with some provisions requiring future Treasury publication or Parliamentary laying.

title: G7 Fundamental Elements for Threat-LED Penetration Testing
summary: The G7 published non-binding fundamental elements for threat-led penetration testing (TLPT) to help authorities and entities design, run and share results of cyber resilience tests. It is guidance for financial-sector entities, TLPT providers and authorities, with emphasis on scoping, multi-stakeholder coordination, information sharing and data protection. No compliance date or mandatory rule is created.

title: G7 Fundamental Elements of ransomware resilience for the financial sector
summary: HMT has published the G7’s non-binding ransomware resilience principles for financial entities and their critical third-party providers. The paper sets out high-level cyber, governance, business continuity and sanctions-risk considerations, but does not create new requirements or deadlines. Firms can use it as reference material to strengthen ransomware preparedness and incident planning.

title: G7 Fundamental Elements for third party cyber risk management in the financial sector
summary: HMT publishes the G7’s revised, non-binding fundamental elements for third-party cyber risk management in the financial sector. The paper updates the 2018 material to cover ICT supply-chain risk, governance, due diligence, monitoring, incident response, contingency planning and cross-sector coordination. Firms and third parties are encouraged to use it as a toolkit; no compliance date or binding rule is created.

title: G7 Fundamental Elements for Effective Assessment of Cybersecurity in the financial sector
summary: HMT publishes non-binding G7 fundamental elements for assessing cybersecurity in the financial sector. The paper sets out desired outcomes and assessment components to help entities, supervisors and assessors evaluate cyber maturity and board oversight. It is guidance for discussion and review, not a rule or deadline-driven requirement.

title: G7 Fundamental Elements for third party cyber risk management in the financial sector 24.10.2018
summary: This G7 policy paper sets out non-binding fundamental elements for managing third-party cyber risk in the financial sector. It covers governance, risk assessment, monitoring, incident response, contingency planning and cross-sector coordination. It is guidance for entities and authorities to use as a reference, with no specific compliance date or legal obligation created by the document itself.

title: Chancellor and Minister for Local Government and Building Safety commission new study on infrastructure planning
summary: The Chancellor commissions the National Infrastructure Commission to study infrastructure planning and the role of National Policy Statements. This is a policy paper setting out terms of reference, with a final report due by Spring 2023. It does not create or change obligations for firms.

title: Public service pensions increase: 2023
summary: HM Treasury sets the 2023 increase for public service pensions in payment: 10.1% from 10 April 2023, with proportionate increases for pensions paid for less than a year. The note and multiplier tables are for scheme administrators to apply the annual uprating correctly.

title: Autumn Budget and Spending Review 2021: documents
summary: This is HM Treasury’s Autumn Budget and Spending Review 2021 documents, setting out the government’s fiscal and spending plans, tax and public expenditure priorities, and economic context. It is a policy document rather than a rule, supervisory notice, or consultation. No direct compliance action or firm-specific deadline is created in the text provided.

title: Treasury Minutes – February 2023
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes publishes the Government’s responses to PAC reports on a range of public-sector topics, including children’s social care, accounting officer assessments, housing, workforce skills and central government property. It sets out responses and target implementation dates for government departments, but does not create requirements for financial firms.

title: Basic bank accounts: July 2021 to June 2022
summary: HM Treasury published annual statistics on basic bank accounts for July 2021 to June 2022. It reports account stocks, openings, closures, upgrades and refusals across the nine designated PCA providers under the Payment Account Regulations, and notes FCA is responsible for compliance. The paper is informational only and does not change rules or deadlines.

title: Terms of reference for the independent review of university spin-outs
summary: HMT published terms of reference for an independent review of university spin-outs. The review will consult universities, investors and founders to identify best practice and compare the UK approach with other regimes. It is an information-setting policy paper, with no direct regulatory obligations or dates for firms.

title: Spring Budget 2023 customs measures
summary: HMRC/HMT published a policy paper on the Spring Budget 2023 customs package, explaining measures to simplify customs import and export processes for businesses and proposing further reform areas informed by a prior call for evidence. It is informational and does not itself set new requirements or deadlines.

title: Investment Zones
summary: HM Treasury’s March 2023 Investment Zones policy paper sets out the government’s intended policy model and next steps for selected English areas to develop proposals for zone status. It outlines priority sectors, possible incentives and delivery approach, but it is not itself a binding rule or obligation on firms.

title: Spring Budget 2023 – Disability White Paper Factsheet
summary: HM Treasury published a factsheet summarising disability reforms announced in the Health and Disability White Paper. It is a policy paper and high-level government communication, with no financial-services requirements or deadlines stated.

title: Enterprise Management Incentives Call for Evidence: Summary of Responses
summary: HM Treasury publishes a summary of responses to the Enterprise Management Incentives call for evidence. It reflects stakeholder views on how EMI is used, its impact on recruitment and retention, and whether eligibility should be widened. It does not itself change the scheme or set a new deadline, but signals possible future policy changes.

title: Government response to the 2022 Fiscal Risks and Sustainability Report
summary: HMT publishes a government response to the OBR’s 2022 Fiscal Risks and Sustainability Report, explaining the government’s fiscal strategy, public finance position and measures taken on energy support, debt and long-term sustainability. It is an informational policy paper and does not impose new requirements on firms.

title: Spring Budget 2023 Factsheet: Cutting & Simplifying Tax for Businesses to Invest and Grow
summary: HM Treasury published a Spring Budget 2023 factsheet describing planned tax measures on capital allowances, R&D support and tax simplification for businesses. It is an informational policy paper and does not itself create or change requirements.

title: Spring Budget 2023 – Labour Market Factsheet
summary: HM Treasury published a Spring Budget 2023 factsheet describing labour market measures aimed at helping people enter work, increase hours and extend working lives. It is an informational policy paper and does not set out direct obligations for firms or a compliance deadline.

title: Pro-innovation Regulation of Technologies Review: Digital Technologies
summary: HM Government’s March 2023 review sets out recommendations for a pro-innovation regulatory approach to digital technologies, including AI, public data access, autonomous vehicles, drones, cyber security, and space/satellite tech. It is a policy review and not itself binding. Some recommendations may lead to future legislation, consultations or regulator action.

title: Spring Budget 2023
summary: This is the UK Government’s Spring Budget 2023 policy paper, setting out fiscal and policy announcements made by the Chancellor. It is an information publication, not a regulatory rule or supervisory notice. The correction slip updates wording in the published document, including a clarification to the Train and Progress measure. No direct compliance action is created by the publication itself.

title: Joint HM Treasury and FCA statement on the Criminal Market Abuse Regime
summary: HM Treasury and the FCA have published a joint policy statement confirming completion of their review of the criminal market abuse regime. It says the government sees scope to update criminal sanctions for insider dealing and market manipulation, but it does not itself change the law or set any deadlines.

title: Sovereign Grant Act 2011: report of the Royal Trustees on the Sovereign Grant for 2023-24
summary: HMT has published the Royal Trustees’ statutory report under the Sovereign Grant Act 2011 setting out the Sovereign Grant for 2023-24 and how it was calculated. It is a point-in-time parliamentary report explaining the determination process for the coming financial year, not a consultation or rule change. No action is imposed on regulated firms.

title: Treasury Minutes – March 2023
summary: This is a Treasury Minutes government response to Public Accounts Committee reports on several non-financial topics, including sport participation, HMRC performance, the UK Infrastructure Bank, integrated care systems and defence digital strategy. It is informational and records the government’s responses; it does not create new regulatory requirements for firms.

title: HM Treasury Evaluation Strategy
summary: HM Treasury published its Evaluation Strategy, setting out its approach to using evaluation in policy-making and supporting evaluation across government. It is an internal government strategy and does not create new rules or obligations for firms.

title: Terms of reference for the review of foreign direct investment
summary: HMT published terms of reference for a review led by Lord Harrington of Watford on how the UK can better attract foreign direct investment into key growth sectors, including digital technology, creative industries, life sciences, advanced manufacturing and green industries. It is a policy paper setting the review scope only, with no new obligations or deadlines stated.

title: Pro-innovation Regulation of Technologies Review: Green Industries
summary: HM Government publishes its response to the Vallance review on green industries, accepting all recommendations and outlining plans to review regulator capacity, improve grid connections and support net zero growth. It says some follow-on actions will be developed by autumn and this summer, but it does not create direct obligations for firms.

title: Green finance strategy
summary: HMT publishes the 2023 Green Finance Strategy, setting out the government’s policy blueprint for mobilising green investment, transition planning, the UK Green Taxonomy, nature markets and support for green finance internationally. It is a strategic policy paper and does not itself impose firm obligations or immediate compliance dates.

title: Spring Finance Bill 2023: Committee of the Whole House
summary: This Finance Bill amendment changes the calculation of covered taxes for the multinational top-up tax by removing an unnecessary step in clause 174. It is part of the new tax regime and applies to the entities and tax calculations covered by the Bill once enacted.

title: Recommendations for the next phase of open banking in the UK
summary: HMT’s Joint Regulatory Oversight Committee sets out recommendations and a 29-action roadmap for the next phase of UK open banking over the next two years. It focuses on making the ecosystem more sustainable, expanding open banking payments, and creating a scalable future data-sharing model. The document is strategic and directional, not a binding rule or consultation.

title: Economic Advisory Council – Terms of Reference – April 2023
summary: HM Treasury updated the Terms of Reference for the Economic Advisory Council in April 2023. It is an advisory paper describing the council’s role in providing independent economic advice to the Chancellor; it does not create obligations for firms.

title: India-UK 2nd Financial Markets Dialogue: Joint Statement
summary: HM Treasury published a joint statement on the second India-UK Financial Markets Dialogue. It records discussions between UK and Indian government and regulatory officials on deepening financial services ties, including sustainable finance, insurance, asset management, capital markets, payments and cryptoassets. It is informational only and does not impose actions or deadlines.

title: Government financial reporting review: Best practice examples from 2021-22
summary: HM Treasury publishes examples of good practice in annual report and accounts for government entities, based on 2021-22 reports. It is guidance-style material aimed at improving narrative, accountability and financial reporting presentation, with no new requirements or deadlines for banks or other FS-regulated firms.

title: Joint Statement from the Specialised Committee on Financial Provisions, 10 May 2023
summary: HMT published a joint statement with the European Commission noting progress on work streams for invoices the EU sends to the UK under the Financial Settlement. It is an informational policy paper only, with no new requirements, dates or actions for firms.

title: Spring Finance Bill 2023: Public Bill Committee
summary: This Spring Finance Bill amendment excludes certain pension funds from a trust income tax relief calculation in ITA 2007. It changes the conditions for when the reduced de minimis estates amount applies to trustees, including where trust property is held for registered or occupational pension schemes. It is part of the Finance (No. 2) Bill process and affects trustees and pension-related arrangements.

title: Treasury Minutes – May 2023
summary: HM Treasury’s May 2023 Treasury Minutes respond to Public Accounts Committee reports on several government topics, including vulnerable adolescents, NHS backlogs, excess votes, COVID employment support schemes, and DVLA backlogs. It is a government response and progress update, not a rule, supervisory notice, or enforcement action. Some actions are mentioned with target dates such as December 2023, but no direct obligations are created for firms.

title: Conflict, Stability and Security Fund: Counter Terrorism Programme Fund programme summaries 2021 to 2022
summary: HMT and other government departments published annual programme summaries for the Conflict, Stability and Security Fund Counter Terrorism Programme Fund for 2021 to 2022. The paper explains the programmes’ aims, budgets, delivery partners and where they operate, but it does not impose any requirements on firms or set deadlines.

title: Pro-innovation Regulation of Technologies Review: Life Sciences and the government response
summary: HMT published a review and government response on pro-innovation regulation for life sciences, covering medicines, medical devices, biotechnology and related areas. It sets out recommendations and background on regulation, skills, capacity, data and routes to market, but it does not itself impose new rules or deadlines.

title: Financial Services & Markets Bill – Overseas Central Counterparties
summary: HM Treasury published a policy paper on technical amendments to the Financial Services and Markets Bill to help UK firms continue using certain non-UK central counterparties under the run-off regime. The note says the amendments would take effect only if approved by Parliament and are intended to avoid exit of some CCPs from the regime on 1 July 2023.

title: Treasury Minutes progress report – June 2023
summary: HM Treasury published a Treasury Minutes progress report updating Parliament on implementation of Public Accounts Committee recommendations across multiple sessions. It is a status report on government progress, not a regulatory rule, consultation, or supervisory notice. No direct obligations are created for firms.

title: Review of the Oil and Gas Fiscal Regime: Terms of Reference
summary: HM Treasury has published terms of reference for a review of the oil and gas fiscal regime announced in the 2022 Autumn Statement. It sets out the review’s context, objectives and scope, but does not set a consultation deadline, final rule, or compliance date. Relevant firms in the sector may wish to monitor the review.

title: Spring Finance Bill 2023: Report Stage
summary: HM Treasury’s Spring Finance Bill 2023 report stage paper sets out government amendments and explanatory notes to tax legislation, including a domestic top-up tax applying from 31 December 2023 and changes to temporary full expensing, energy profits levy allowances, HMRC data powers and deposit schemes. It is relevant to firms affected by these tax measures and any related reporting or operational changes.

title: Pro-innovation Regulation of Technologies Review: Creative Industries
summary: HMT published a pro-innovation review on regulation in the creative industries. It sets out recommendations for possible regulatory reforms over the next 6-18 months across sub-sectors such as video games, advertising, live performance and fashion. It is a policy/research style report only and does not itself change rules or create obligations.

title: Thematic Review of Non-investment Asset Valuation
summary: HM Treasury published the results of a thematic review of non-investment asset valuation in the public sector. It says there may be merit in exploring changes to the current valuation regime and that further work, including a formal consultation, may follow. No new requirements are created in this paper.

title: Treasury Minutes - June 2023
summary: This is a Treasury Minutes government response to Public Accounts Committee reports. It summarises how departments responded to recommendations on topics including fraud, digital services tax, business support, BBC digital and passport services, with some implementation updates and future publication plans. It does not create new regulatory requirements for firms.

title: UK-EU Memorandum of Understanding on Financial Services Cooperation
summary: HMT and the European Commission published a UK-EU Memorandum of Understanding creating a framework for financial services regulatory cooperation and the Joint EU-UK Financial Regulatory Forum. It sets out how the parties will exchange views, share information and discuss regulatory developments, but it does not itself change UK firm obligations or set a compliance deadline.

title: Economic crime plan 2023 to 2026
summary: HMT published the Economic Crime Plan 2023-2026, setting out government and public-private priorities to reduce money laundering, sanctions evasion, fraud and other economic crime. It is a strategic policy document rather than a binding rule or supervisory notice, and it does not itself create firm obligations. It is relevant to firms exposed to AML, sanctions and fraud risk.

title: Scottish Income Tax outturn reconciliation for 2021-22
summary: HMT explains how 2021-22 Scottish Income Tax outturn data is used to reconcile Scottish Government funding, increasing self-funding but reducing the block grant, with a net funding reduction for 2024-25. It is an explanatory policy paper for Scotland and does not create firm obligations.

title: Data Reporting Services Regulations 2023 - Draft SI and Policy Note
summary: HM Treasury publishes a near-final draft statutory instrument and policy note for the Data Reporting Services Regulations 2023, replacing retained EU law for data reporting service providers and helping enable a UK consolidated tape. It is a technical consultation on the draft SI, and comments are requested by 21 August 2023. The instrument affects DRSPs, investment firms and market data arrangements.

title: Summary of Financial Inclusion Policy Forum meeting February 2023
summary: HMT published a summary of the February 2023 Financial Inclusion Policy Forum meeting. It is an informational policy paper about collaboration on financial inclusion, not a rule, consultation or supervisory requirement. No obligations or deadlines are created for firms.

title: Building a Smarter Financial Services Regulatory Framework: Delivery Plan
summary: HM Treasury sets out its delivery plan for replacing retained EU law in financial services under FSMA 2023. It explains the phased programme, the role of regulators, and the use of the Regulatory Initiatives Grid to signal future changes. This is a strategic forward look and does not itself change rules or impose deadlines on firms.

title: Investment Research Review
summary: HMT published the final outcome of the independent Investment Research Review. The report makes recommendations to government, the FCA and industry on improving the UK investment research market, including a research platform, wider retail access, issuer-sponsored research code of conduct, and possible regulatory changes. It is an awareness item rather than a binding rule or consultation.

title: Securitisation Regulations 2023 - Draft SI and Policy Note
summary: HM Treasury has published a near-final draft Statutory Instrument and policy note on securitisation reform. It is a technical-check publication, not the final rules, and seeks comments by 21 August 2023. FCA and PRA rule changes to replace most firm-facing securitisation requirements are expected in Q3 2023.

title: Public Offers and Admissions to Trading Regulations 2023 – Draft SI and Policy Note
summary: HM Treasury has published a near-final draft statutory instrument and policy note for the new Public Offers and Admissions to Trading regime. It explains how the current prospectus regime will be replaced and invites technical comments by 21 August 2023. Firms involved in capital raising, public offers or admissions to trading should review the changes and assess impacts.

title: Digitisation Taskforce
summary: HMT has published a policy paper on the Digitisation Taskforce, which is considering reforms to the UK shareholding framework, including ending paper share certificates for traded companies and exploring options for private companies. The interim report invites industry feedback by 25 September 2023, and the taskforce will continue open engagement for six months before its final report.

title: National Insurance Fund Investment Account Report & Accounts 2022 to 2023
summary: HMT published the National Insurance Fund Investment Account Report & Accounts 2022-23, setting out the account’s performance, governance and audit for the year ended 31 March 2023. It is an annual report and parliamentary account under the Social Security Administration Act 1992, not a new rule or requirement. No action or compliance date is created for firms.

title: Treasury Minutes - July 2023
summary: Treasury Minutes July 2023 sets out the government’s responses to Public Accounts Committee recommendations across several departments, including defence, HMRC, the Cabinet Office, Defra and health. It is a parliamentary response document and does not create financial-services obligations or set regulatory deadlines for firms.

title: Memorandum of Understanding on Royal Taxation 2023
summary: HM Treasury published a memorandum explaining the voluntary tax arrangements for The King and The Prince of Wales, including how income tax, capital gains tax and inheritance tax are treated. It is an information document presented to Parliament under the Sovereign Grant Act, not a regulatory rule for firms. No action dates or obligations for regulated firms are set out.

title: Report of the Royal Trustees on the Sovereign Grant Review 2023
summary: This is a government report on the 2023 Sovereign Grant review under the Sovereign Grant Act 2011. It concludes the grant percentage should be reduced from 25% to 12% and notes future legislation may later reset the level once Buckingham Palace reservicing is complete, expected in 2026-27.

title: Treasury Minutes – August 2023
summary: HM Treasury’s August 2023 Treasury Minutes is a government response to PAC reports, including education recovery, investment into the UK, pension cases, energy bills support, decarbonising the power sector and local auditor reporting. It records the government’s replies and positions, but does not itself set new FCA/PRA rules or obligations for banks.

title: Block Grant Transparency: July 2023
summary: HM Treasury published an explanatory policy paper and spreadsheet setting out how block grants for the Scottish Government, Welsh Government and Northern Ireland Executive are calculated. It is informational only and does not create or change requirements for firms.

title: Cash Access Policy Statement
summary: HMT has published a Cash Access Policy Statement setting out government policy on access to cash deposit and withdrawal services for relevant personal and business current accounts across the UK. It is published under FSMA 2000 as amended by the Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 and is intended to inform the FCA’s approach to reasonable provision of cash access services. No action date is stated in the text.

title: Public service pensions: 2020 valuations
summary: The Treasury has made the Public Service Pensions (Valuations and Employer Cost Cap) Directions 2023. They set the actuarial valuation and employer cost cap methodology for public service pension schemes, replacing the 2014 directions. The directions come into force the day after they are signed and apply to relevant public service pension schemes, including local government workers where specified.

title: UK-India 12th Economic and Financial Dialogue: Joint Statement
summary: HMT published a joint statement on the 12th UK-India Economic and Financial Dialogue. It sets out high-level outcomes and commitments on investment, financial market access, resilience, climate, infrastructure and technology, but does not create new UK regulatory requirements or deadlines.

title: Treasury Minutes - September 2023
summary: Treasury Minutes responding to Committee of Public Accounts reports across several departments, including a section on HMCTS court and tribunals reform. It records government responses and progress updates; it does not itself create or amend financial-services obligations.

title: Terms of Reference for the Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee
summary: HM Treasury publishes the terms of reference for the Finance Interministerial Standing Committee, describing its purpose and membership across the UK Government and devolved administrations. It is an informational policy paper only and does not set regulatory requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: EM on a UK/EU TCA Specialised Committee decision (COM(2023)527)
summary: HM Treasury explains a proposed EU Council Decision on the UK/EU TCA Specialised Committee decision that would bring into force UK association to Horizon Europe and Copernicus from 1 January 2024. UK researchers and businesses could access 2024 programme funding, while 2021-2023 commitments remain excluded except via the UK guarantee scheme. This is an explanatory memorandum, not a rule or obligation notice.

title: UK Government Green Financing: 2021 to 2023 reports
summary: HM Treasury published its 2023 UK Green Financing Allocation and Impact Report, updating investors and the public on the government’s green gilts and Green Savings Bonds programme. It reports 2022-23 allocations, first-year impact estimates, and progress against the Green Financing Framework’s transparency commitments. No new requirements are created for firms.

title: Joint statement on the UK-U.S. Financial Regulatory Working Group meeting
summary: HM Treasury and US Treasury issued a joint statement summarising the eighth UK-US Financial Regulatory Working Group meeting and the main topics discussed and outcomes. It is informational only and does not set new rules, deadlines or obligations for firms.

title: Payment service contract termination rule changes: implementation, timings, and next steps
summary: HM Treasury sets out how planned changes to payment service contract termination rules will be implemented, including extending notice from two months to 90 days and requiring clear, tailored reasons for termination, subject to limited exceptions. It confirms the intended scope for payment service providers and payment accounts, including certain carve-outs for corporate users. The paper is guidance on forthcoming legislation, with government expecting firms to prepare now.

title: EM on a TCA Specialised Committee decision (12523/23, COM(23)504)
summary: HM Treasury explains the UK position for an EU/UK Trade Specialised Committee decision on VAT administrative cooperation and tax recovery under the TCA. It describes technical implementing decisions on electronic forms, recovery assistance, service levels and UK financial contributions. The memorandum notes the decisions would be binding under international law and that payments would be due within 60 days of adoption.

title: World Bank 108th Development Committee Meeting: UK Governor's statement
summary: The UK Governor’s statement to the World Bank Development Committee calls for international cooperation on reforming the global finance system and increasing financing and ambition. It is a policy speech/statement, not a rule, supervisory notice, or enforcement action, and creates no direct obligations for firms.

title: Fairness Group Joint Public Statement
summary: HMT published a joint public statement on government debt collection fairness with the debt advice sector. It describes voluntary Fairness Principles, aligned to FCA Treating Customers Fairly, and outlines ongoing collaborative work to improve treatment of people in debt and vulnerability. No new obligations or deadlines are created.

title: EM on Windsor Framework customs arrangements
summary: This explanatory memorandum describes the Windsor Framework customs changes for goods and parcels moving between Great Britain and Northern Ireland, including the UK Internal Market Scheme and reduced customs formalities. Some measures are already in force, and the full green-lane arrangements are due from 30 September 2024. It is relevant to firms involved in trade, logistics and cross-border parcel movement.

title: Joint Statement: EU-UK Financial Regulatory Forum, October 2023
summary: HM Treasury and the European Commission published a joint statement recording discussions at the first EU-UK Financial Regulatory Forum on 19 October 2023. It is a public record of topics covered under the UK-EU financial services cooperation memorandum, with no rule change, consultation, or deadline.

title: Economic Crime (Transparency and Enforcement) Bill 2022: overarching documents
summary: HMT has published overarching documents for the Economic Crime (Transparency and Enforcement) Bill, which became the Economic Crime (Transparency and Enforcement) Act 2022 after Royal Assent on 14 March 2022. The pack includes the draft bill and fact sheets on the Register of Overseas Entities, unexplained wealth orders and sanctions. This is background/codified legislation material rather than a new rule or consultation.

title: Joint statement from the Specialised Committee on Financial Provisions, 26 October 2023
summary: HMT published a joint statement with the European Commission noting progress at the eighth meeting of the Specialised Committee on Financial Provisions. It is an informational policy paper about workstreams on invoices the EU sends to the UK under the Financial Settlement; it does not create new requirements.

title: Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023: ECHR memoranda
summary: This is an HMT policy paper publishing ECHR memoranda for the Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023. It explains the human-rights compatibility statements for the Act and notes the Bill received Royal Assent on 26 October 2023. It does not itself create new operational requirements.

title: HM Treasury and Financial Conduct Authority Regulatory Perimeter Meeting – July 2023
summary: Record of a July 2023 meeting between HM Treasury and the FCA on the FCA’s Perimeter Report and the financial services regulatory perimeter. It is a discussion record only and does not create new rules, deadlines or obligations for firms.

title: Update on plans for the regulation of fiat-backed stablecoins
summary: HM Treasury sets out its planned approach to regulate fiat-backed stablecoins used in UK payment chains. It says secondary legislation is expected as soon as possible and by early 2024, to bring issuance, custody and payment-chain activities into the UK regulatory perimeter and enable FCA regulation, with separate powers for systemic payment systems.

title: Extending the transitional period for third country benchmarks in the UK
summary: HM Treasury has laid a statutory instrument extending the UK Benchmarks Regulation transitional period for third-country benchmarks from 31 December 2025 to 31 December 2030. The change comes into force on 1 January 2024 and affects firms using or referencing third-country benchmarks.

title: International Joint Statement on the Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework
summary: HMT published a joint policy statement saying the UK and other jurisdictions intend to implement the OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework and related CRS amendments, with exchanges expected to begin by 2027. It is an announcement of future implementation intentions, not the rules themselves.

title: Treasury Minutes – November 2023
summary: HM Treasury issued its November 2023 Treasury Minutes, responding to Public Accounts Committee reports on COVID support schemes, fraud and corruption, digital transformation, and resetting government programmes. It explains the government’s position on controls, accountability and spending frameworks, but does not create new requirements for regulated firms.

title: Pro-innovation Regulation of Technologies Review: Advanced Manufacturing
summary: HMT published an intelligence report on pro-innovation regulation for advanced manufacturing. It discusses regulatory and standards opportunities across robotics, automation, clean transport, hydrogen, recycling and building materials, and makes recommendations for government and regulators. It is not a binding rule or supervisory notice, and no firm-specific deadline is created.

title: UK Retail Disclosure Framework – Draft SI and Policy Note
summary: HM Treasury has published a near-final draft statutory instrument and policy note for a new UK retail disclosure framework for Consumer Composite Investments, replacing retained EU PRIIPs law. It invites technical comments by 2024-01-10. The draft sets the scope, key definitions and FCA rule-making powers, and is part of the wider Smarter Regulatory Framework under FSMA 2023.

title: Short Selling Regulations 2024
summary: HM Treasury has laid draft Short Selling Regulations 2024 before Parliament. The draft designates short selling activities and sets the framework for FCA rules on settlement arrangements and notifications of significant net short positions, including a 0.2% threshold. It applies to shares and related instruments admitted to trading on UK trading venues. The regulations are a draft statutory instrument and will take effect only once made and brought into force.

title: Government response to the 2023 Fiscal Risks and Sustainability Report
summary: HM Treasury’s response to the OBR’s 2023 Fiscal Risks and Sustainability Report explains the government’s fiscal risk management approach and related policy actions. It discusses public finances, labour inactivity, energy resilience and debt sustainability, but does not create or change requirements for firms. Published on 2023-11-22.

title: Shared Outcomes Fund Round Three
summary: HMT published a Shared Outcomes Fund Round 3 paper summarising pilot projects funded across government for 2023-24 and 2024-25. It describes the aims, partner departments and funding for each pilot, including a net zero blended finance project, but it does not set rules or obligations for firms.

title: Pro-innovation Regulation of Technologies Review: Cross-Cutting
summary: HM Treasury’s review sets out recommendations for government and regulators to support pro-innovation regulation of emerging technologies. It is a policy paper and review, not a binding rule or supervisory notice. It may be of interest to firms involved in technology, innovation or regulated products, but it does not itself create new obligations or deadlines.

title: Government response to the National Infrastructure Commission report on improving nationally significant infrastructure planning
summary: The government publishes a policy paper responding to the National Infrastructure Commission’s recommendations on improving nationally significant infrastructure planning in England. It sets out the government’s position on six recommendations and future reform direction over the next five years. No direct compliance action or binding requirement is created by this document.

title: Autumn Statement 2023: National Insurance Factsheet
summary: HM Treasury published a factsheet on Autumn Statement 2023 changes cutting the main rates of National Insurance for employees and the self-employed and abolishing Class 2 NICs. It is an informational policy paper, not a rule, and does not set firm-specific compliance actions or deadlines.

title: The mortgage guarantee scheme
summary: HMT publishes an outline of the mortgage guarantee scheme, explaining its policy intent and high-level design to support high loan-to-value mortgage lending and home ownership. It is informational and does not itself impose requirements on lenders. The document is dated March 2021, though the publication metadata shows 2023-11-23.

title: The Harrington Review of Foreign Direct Investment
summary: HMT published the Harrington Review of Foreign Direct Investment, an independent review setting out recommendations to improve the UK’s FDI offer and government machinery. It is an intelligence/reporting document, not a rule, guidance, or enforcement notice. No direct obligations are created for firms.

title: UK-Japan Financial Dialogue and Financial Regulatory Forum joint statement
summary: HMT published a UK-Japan Financial Dialogue and Financial Regulatory Forum joint statement recording discussions held in Tokyo on 27 November 2023. It is a public record of bilateral regulatory dialogue, with no new rules, obligations, or deadlines for firms.

title: Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes Provisional Agenda: 21 December 2021
summary: This is a provisional agenda for the first meeting of the EU-UK Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes. It is an informational meeting notice only, with no rule changes, obligations, or deadlines for firms.

title: Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes Provisional Agenda: 22 September 2022
summary: This is a provisional agenda for a UK-EU committee meeting under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement. It lists discussion items, including a UK request about association to EU programmes, but it does not set rules, deadlines, or obligations.

title: Autumn Statement 2023
summary: HMT’s Autumn Statement 2023 is a budget-style policy paper summarising the Chancellor’s fiscal and economic measures, including tax, spending, business and energy announcements. It is a government publication rather than a binding financial-services rule or supervisory notice. It is mainly for awareness, with some measures potentially relevant to firms once implemented through later legislation or rules.

title: Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes Provisional Agenda: 4 December 2023
summary: HMT published a provisional agenda for the 4 December 2023 meeting of the UK-EU Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement. It is a meeting agenda only and does not itself change rules or create obligations for firms.

title: Further detail on HMT analysis of borrowing and interest rates
summary: HM Treasury published a policy paper giving extra methodological detail and supporting data on how it estimates the impact of additional government borrowing on interest rates. It is background analysis only and does not create requirements for firms.

title: Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes Minutes: 22 September 2022
summary: Minutes of the second meeting of the UK-EU Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes, held on 22 September 2022. It is an informational record of discussions under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement and does not introduce any new rules or deadlines.

title: Treasury Minutes progress report – December 2023
summary: This Treasury Minutes progress report updates Parliament on the Government’s progress implementing accepted Public Accounts Committee recommendations across many past reports and sessions. It is a status update, not a new rule, consultation, or supervisory requirement. No direct obligations are created for firms.

title: The Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (The Ombudsman Scheme) Regulations 2024 – Draft SI and Policy Note
summary: HM Treasury has published a draft statutory instrument and policy note on changing who the Financial Ombudsman Service can charge case fees to. It would let the FOS charge claims management companies and other relevant professional representatives, alongside a consultation on FOS Plans and Budget 2024-25. Responses to the FOS consultation close on 30 January 2024; HM Treasury says it expects FOS to start charging by end-September 2024.

title: Decision No 1/2023 of the Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement adopting Protocols I and II and amending Annex 47 to the Trade and Cooperation Agreement
summary: This Decision under the UK-EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement adopts Protocols I and II and amends Annex 47 on UK participation in certain EU programmes. It takes effect on adoption and applies from 1 January 2024. The text sets the framework for UK entities’ participation and contributions to named Union programmes, including Horizon Europe-related arrangements.

title: Money Market Funds – Draft SI and Policy Note
summary: HMT has published a near-final draft statutory instrument and policy note that will replace retained EU law on money market funds with a new UK framework. It deletes certain passporting provisions, keeps the requirement for MMFs to be authorised or approved, and leaves detailed firm-facing rules to the FCA. Technical comments are invited by 2024-01-24.

title: Welsh Rates of Income Tax outturn reconciliation for 2021-22
summary: HM Treasury published an explanatory policy paper on the 2021-22 Welsh Rates of Income Tax outturn reconciliation. It explains how HMRC outturn data and revised ONS population estimates update the Welsh Government’s funding, with effects on 2024-25 funding. This is informational only and creates no direct obligations for firms.

title: Customs simplification measures: December 2023
summary: HMRC/HMT published a policy paper summarising next steps for measures to simplify customs import and export processes for traders. It is informational only and does not create new obligations or set a compliance date.

title: EM about an amendment to EU decision 2021/512 (COM(2023)704)
summary: HM Treasury explains a proposal to extend the UK’s Northern Ireland VAT fuel derogation under the VAT Directive until 31 December 2026. It would let businesses continue using a flat-rate charge for private fuel use instead of detailed mileage records, reducing admin burdens. This is an EU/UK legislative step rather than a UK banking rule change.

title: Thematic review of performance reporting
summary: HMT’s thematic review of performance reporting proposes changes to the Financial Reporting Manual (FReM) and related Annual Report and Accounts guidance for central government bodies. It recommends removing some paragraphs, encouraging signposting to other sources, improving balanced reporting, and publishing training and best-practice materials. No fixed compliance date is stated, but departments and preparers are expected to adapt once the guidance is updated.

title: Women in Finance Charter: Treasury Progress Update 2023
summary: HM Treasury published a progress update on its Women in Finance Charter commitments, including that female representation in senior management rose to 50% by March 2023. It is an informational update on the Treasury’s own internal progress and future priorities, with no new obligations for firms.

title: Response to the VRP Working Group’s Blueprint for non-sweeping VRPs
summary: HMT, via the JROC, published its response to the VRP Working Group’s blueprint for phased rollout of non-sweeping variable recurring payments. It supports progressing initial use cases such as regulated utilities, regulated financial services, and payments to government, with a target third-quarter 2024 rollout discussed in the paper. This is an update on policy direction and industry planning, not a rule change.

title: Joint Regulatory Oversight Committee update on actions to enable the next phase of open banking in the UK
summary: The Joint Regulatory Oversight Committee gives a progress update on work to move UK open banking to its next phase, including the future entity, governance, funding and rollout of new services. It is an update on ongoing ecosystem work, not a new rule or consultation. The document says the Committee will publish a decision on the future entity early next year and mentions further work on open banking in Q1 next year.

title: Technical note: Electricity Generator Levy – new investment exemption
summary: HMT published a technical note on the Electricity Generator Levy new investment exemption. It explains that from 22 November 2023, receipts from qualifying new generating stations or capacity expansions decided after that date will not be subject to EGL. The note is informational only and says formal HMRC guidance will follow. The levy itself remains in force until 31 March 2028.

title: Group of Creditors to Ukraine: Statement on extending the debt deferral for Ukraine
summary: The UK, as part of Ukraine’s bilateral creditor group, issued a statement extending debt deferral for Ukraine. This is an informational government announcement with no direct requirements for firms. No action or deadline is imposed on regulated entities.

title: Policy Design Document
summary: HM Treasury sets out the design of the new UK Infrastructure Bank, including its mission, operating principles, capital structure, headquarters in Leeds, and intended UK-wide scope. It also says legislation will be brought forward later to put the bank on a statutory footing and that a framework document will follow ahead of launch. This is policy design and planning, not a rule or obligation for firms.

title: Keepwell Agreement
summary: HMT and UK Infrastructure Bank have amended and restated a keep well agreement. The deed confirms HMT’s funding support arrangements for UKIB, including a £22 billion funding cap, and replaces the prior agreement. It is a published agreement rather than a new rule or consultation.

title: User and Preparer Advisory Group Minutes: March 2023
summary: Minutes of the HMT User and Preparer Advisory Group meeting held on 8 March 2023, covering updates on performance reporting, local government, Whole of Government Accounts and sustainability reporting. This is a record of discussion only and does not set new requirements or deadlines.

title: UKIB Framework Document
summary: HMT published the UK Infrastructure Bank Framework Document, which sets the governance, accountability and operating framework between HMT, UKGI and UKIB. It explains the bank’s mission, investment principles, legal powers and board/governance arrangements, but it does not itself create regulatory requirements for regulated firms. The document may be updated and is to be reviewed within 12 months of launch.

title: Central Counterparties Special Resolution Regime Code of Practice
summary: HM Treasury has published a Code of Practice for the Central Counterparties Special Resolution Regime under FSMA 2023 Schedule 11. It explains how the Bank of England and Treasury may use CCP resolution powers and what they must have regard to. The code is issued now and will be updated periodically after consultation with the Bank, PRA and FCA.

title: Third Trade Specialised Committee on Customs Cooperation and Rules of Origin Minutes
summary: HM Treasury published minutes of the third UK-EU Trade Specialised Committee on Customs Cooperation and Rules of Origin under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement. It is an informational policy paper about customs cooperation, rules of origin and related trade facilitation topics, with no new requirements or deadlines stated.

title: Sovereign Infrastructure Guarantee
summary: HMT published an amendment and restatement agreement for the Sovereign Infrastructure Guarantee between HMT and the UK Infrastructure Bank. It updates the terms of an existing government guarantee arrangement, effective on the date of the agreement. No new sector-wide regulatory obligations are set out for firms.

title: Treasury Minutes – January 2024
summary: HM Treasury’s January 2024 Treasury Minutes is the government’s response to PAC reports on issues including smart meters, urgent care, Bulb Energy and active travel. It records whether recommendations are accepted or rejected and describes progress, but it does not itself create new regulatory requirements for firms. No direct compliance action or deadline is set for banks.

title: Report on the annual review of National Insurance contributions
summary: HM Treasury published a policy paper explaining why it did not lay a draft order to change certain National Insurance contribution rates and thresholds for 2024/25. It notes that Class 2 and Class 3 rates, the Small Profits Threshold, and Class 4 profit limits remain unchanged for 2024/25, while earlier NIC reductions were already legislated separately.

title: Public service pensions increase: 2024
summary: HM Treasury publishes 2024 public service pensions increase multiplier tables and note. Public service pensions in payment for a year will rise by 6.7% from 8 April 2024, with shorter-payment pensions receiving a pro rata increase. Scheme administrators should use the tables to apply the annual increase correctly.

title: The Digital Pound Taskforce and Forums
summary: HM Treasury publishes updated terms of reference for the Digital Pound Taskforce, explaining its role in overseeing the design phase of a possible UK retail CBDC. It is governance and strategy information only; no digital pound is being introduced yet and no firm obligations are created.

title: National Infrastructure and Construction Pipeline 2023
summary: HMT and the Infrastructure and Projects Authority publish the 2023 National Infrastructure and Construction Pipeline, setting out planned and projected UK public and private infrastructure investment over the next 10 years, including procurement volumes, regional split, funding mix and MMC use. It is an informational pipeline update for the market and government, with no new rules, deadlines or obligations for firms.

title: Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes Minutes: 4 December 2023
summary: Minutes of the UK-EU Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes meeting held on 4 December 2023. It is an informational policy paper about the committee’s discussions and has no direct regulatory change, deadline, or obligation for firms.

title: Joint statement on the UK-U.S. Financial Regulatory Working Group meeting - January 2024
summary: HM Treasury and US Treasury published a joint statement summarising the ninth UK-US Financial Regulatory Working Group meeting held on 31 January 2024. It is a public record of discussions and outcomes only; it does not set new rules, deadlines or obligations for firms.

title: Treasury Minutes – February 2024
summary: HMT’s Treasury Minutes is a government response to the Public Accounts Committee on several departments’ reports, including Making Tax Digital. It summarises HMRC’s planned rollout of Making Tax Digital for Income Tax Self Assessment and other public-sector issues, but it does not itself create or change rules for firms.

title: Update to the Transition from Existing Digital Services Taxes to Pillar 1
summary: HMT published a policy paper updating the political compromise on the transition from existing digital services taxes to Pillar 1. The UK and several other countries agreed to extend the compromise through 30 June 2024 while multilateral negotiations continue. This is an informational update for firms with cross-border tax exposure, not a binding rule change.

title: Joint Statement: UK – U.S. Covered Agreement. Third meeting of the Joint Committee
summary: HM Treasury and US Treasury issued a joint statement recording the third Joint Committee meeting under the UK-U.S. Covered Agreement on prudential measures for insurance and reinsurance. It summarises what was discussed and any outcomes from the meeting held on 20 February 2024. No new rules, deadlines or obligations are created.

title: Economic Evidence to the Pay Review Bodies: February 2024
summary: HM Treasury publishes economic evidence for the 2024-25 Pay Review Bodies pay round. It sets out inflation, labour market and fiscal context for public sector pay recommendations, but does not create rules or obligations for financial firms. No action is required by a bank unless it is using this as macroeconomic background.

title: Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023: Factsheets
summary: HMT and partner departments published factsheets explaining measures in the Economic Crime and Corporate Transparency Act 2023, including Companies House reform, beneficial ownership, identity verification, company names, limited partnerships, SLAPPs and cryptoassets. This is an informational package about the Act’s measures, not a new rule or consultation. It helps firms understand the regime but does not itself set a compliance date.

title: Investment Zones update
summary: The government published an update giving further details on six Investment Zones in England, including spending and tax interventions for five zones and location, sector and anchor investor information for Tees. It is informational and does not set out a new regulatory requirement for firms.

title: Spring Budget 2024: Non-UK domiciled individuals - Policy Summary
summary: The UK government published a policy summary announcing that from April 2025 it will abolish the current tax regime for non-UK domiciled individuals and replace domicile with a residence-based tax regime. This is a policy announcement and summary, not the legislation itself.

title: Spring Budget 2024: Personal Tax Factsheet
summary: HM Treasury published a Spring Budget 2024 personal tax factsheet describing changes to National Insurance and the High Income Child Benefit Charge. This is a government policy paper announcing tax changes, not a regulatory consultation or FCA/PRA rule. Firms should assess any payroll, benefits, and employer tax impacts once the underlying legislation or finance bill measures are available.

title: Spring Budget 2024
summary: The Spring Budget 2024 announces tax changes, including cuts to employee and self-employed National Insurance from 6 April 2024. It is a government fiscal statement, not a financial-services rule, but it may affect payroll, tax, and financial planning for firms and staff once the changes take effect.

title: Memorandum of Understanding for the "Trailblazer" Single Settlements for Greater Manchester and West Midlands Combined Authorities
summary: HM Treasury sets out a memorandum of understanding for single settlements with Greater Manchester and West Midlands combined authorities. It explains the funding scope, governance, risk management, accountability and next steps, including further annexes to be published by spring 2024. This is a policy/intelligence document about local government devolution, not a financial-services rule or supervisory notice.

title: The Payment Services (Amendment) Regulations 2024 – policy note
primary_functions: Legal; Regulatory change; Compliance; Financial crime; Ops
summary: HM Treasury’s policy note accompanies a near-final statutory instrument amending the Payment Services Regulations 2017. It would let payment service providers delay outbound payment execution by up to four business days where there are reasonable grounds to suspect fraud or dishonesty, to help tackle APP fraud. This is a draft near-final SI published for technical comments before it is laid before Parliament.

title: British Council framework document
summary: HMT has published the British Council framework document, which sets out the governance, accountability and working relationship between the FCDO and the British Council. It is a framework document for a public body, not a financial-services rule or supervisory notice, and it does not impose compliance deadlines on firms.

title: Payment service contract termination rule changes – Draft SI and Policy Note
summary: HM Treasury has published a draft Statutory Instrument and policy note to change payment service contract termination rules under the Payment Services Regulations 2017. The reforms would apply to providers of payment services and to indefinite framework contracts entered into on or after commencement, with targeted exceptions for intermediated business models. This is a near-final draft for technical checking before being laid before Parliament.

title: Communiqués from the Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee
summary: A policy paper publishing communiqués from the Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee, which records meetings between the UK Government Chief Secretary to the Treasury and devolved finance ministers. It is an informational record of discussions on economic and finance matters and does not set rules or deadlines for firms.

title: Building a Smarter Financial Services Regulatory Framework: Next Phase
primary_functions: Regulatory change; Compliance; Legal; Prudential; Product
summary: HM Treasury’s March 2024 policy paper updates progress on the Smarter Financial Services Regulatory Framework and explains the next phase of replacing assimilated law with UK rules. It highlights completed and expected statutory changes across insurer capital, prospectuses, market data reporting, securitisation and payment services. The paper is informational, but it signals further legislative and rulemaking work for affected firms.

title: Public Service Pensions and Judicial Offices Act 2022: Treasury Directions - December 2022 to March 2024
summary: The Treasury made and brought into force amendments to directions under the Public Service Pensions and Judicial Offices Act 2022 on 21 March 2024. The changes update pension scheme transfer, compensation and interest calculation rules for Chapter 1 schemes, judicial schemes and local government schemes, including references to tax penalties and NS&I-linked interest rates.

title: Sovereign Grant Act 2011: report of the Royal Trustees on the Sovereign Grant for 2024-25
summary: This HMT report sets out the Sovereign Grant 2024-25 calculation and records that £86.3 million will be paid to the Royal Household. It also reflects the amended statutory formula under the Sovereign Grant Act 2011 and SI 2024/52, which changed the step 1 percentage to 12%.

title: Accelerated Settlement Taskforce
summary: HMT published the Accelerated Settlement Taskforce report and government response. The government accepted the recommendations to move UK securities settlement to T+1 no later than 31 December 2027 and to create a Technical Group to work through implementation, including a 2025 date for mandated technical and operational changes. This is policy/market direction rather than a binding rule.

title: Treasury Minutes – March 2024
summary: HM Treasury’s March 2024 Treasury Minutes set out the government’s responses to Public Accounts Committee reports on flooding, defence inventory management, whole of government accounts, HS2/Euston, and reducing illegal drugs harm. It is a parliamentary response document and does not itself create new rules or obligations for firms. The only date-specific commitments are government implementation targets for its own actions, including end-2024 and end-2025 milestones.

title: Seizing the Opportunity: Delivering Efficiency for the Public
summary: HM Treasury published a policy paper setting out the government’s plan to improve efficiency across public services, including procurement, fraud reduction, major projects, asset management and digital transformation. It is an overview of intended government activity and savings ambitions, not a rule, consultation or supervisory notice for firms. No direct obligations or firm-specific deadlines are stated.

title: UK Independent Film Tax Credit
summary: HM Treasury and HMRC published a policy note giving extra detail on the UK Independent Film Tax Credit, including eligibility criteria and how the credit will be calculated. It explains the measure announced at Spring Budget 2024 but does not itself create or change obligations for banks.

title: Memorandum of understanding: between the Financial Conduct Authority and the Bank of England (exercising its prudential regulation functions)
