summary: The FCA and the Bank of England (acting as PRA) have updated their Memorandum of Understanding on coordination and cooperation, replacing the 2019 version. It sets out each regulator’s roles and information-sharing arrangements across FSMA and related legislation. This is a framework document rather than a new rule, and it does not itself create new obligations for firms.

title: Proposals for the design of the future entity for UK Open Banking
summary: HMT-led JROC published consultation proposals on the design of the future entity for UK open banking and the interim entity. It asks for comments by 20 May 2024 on governance, funding, scope and transition arrangements for the body that will replace Open Banking Limited and may extend beyond current CMA Order activities.

title: Changes to the taxation of non-UK domiciled individuals
summary: HMT published a technical policy note on planned changes to the taxation of non-UK domiciled individuals, describing main changes applying from 6 April 2025. It is aimed at affected individuals and practitioners and says further updates and draft legislation will follow later in the year. No direct obligations are created by this note itself.

title: World Bank 109th Development Committee Meeting: UK Governor's statement
summary: UK ministers’ statement at the World Bank Development Committee meeting calls on the World Bank Group, IMF and international community to increase development financing and ambition, including a strong 21st replenishment of the International Development Association. It is an international policy statement, not a UK regulatory change or obligation for firms.

title: Joint statement from the Specialised Committee on Financial Provisions, 24 April 2024
summary: HMT published a joint statement with the European Commission noting good progress on work streams around invoices the EU sends to the UK under the Financial Settlement. It is an informational policy paper with no new rules, deadlines or obligations for firms.

title: Basic bank accounts: July 2022 to June 2023
summary: HM Treasury publishes annual data on basic bank accounts held by the nine designated PCA providers for July 2022 to June 2023. It also explains the current PARs framework and notes planned future changes to refusal and termination rules for basic bank accounts, but this document itself does not change the rules. No immediate action date is set in the publication.

title: Anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism: Supervision Report 2022-23
summary: HM Treasury published its 2022-23 AML/CTF Supervision Report, summarising how UK AML supervisors performed over the year and highlighting supervisory strengths and weaknesses across sectors. It also notes ongoing government work on wider AML/CTF supervision reforms and updates to the Money Laundering Regulations, but the report itself does not create new requirements.

title: Anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism: Supervision Report 2020-22
summary: HM Treasury’s AML/CFT Supervision Report 2020-22 reviews supervisory and enforcement activity by UK AML/CFT supervisors over 6 April 2020 to 5 April 2022. It highlights weaknesses and improvements in supervision, notes recent enforcement examples, and says Treasury will consult on reforms to the supervisory landscape. It is a report and policy update, not a rule change.

title: Record of Financial Stability Report meetings: December 2020 to April 2024
summary: HMT published a record of Chancellor–Governor meetings on the Bank of England’s Financial Stability Report covering December 2020 to April 2024. It is an informational policy paper and does not impose new requirements or deadlines on firms.

title: UK and Singapore strengthen collaboration in sustainable finance and FinTech
summary: HM Treasury and the Monetary Authority of Singapore issued a joint statement recording discussions at the ninth UK-Singapore Financial Dialogue on collaboration in sustainable finance and fintech. It is informational only and does not impose any new requirements or deadlines.

title: Sustainability Disclosure Requirements: Implementation Update 2024
summary: HMT updates its sustainability disclosure roadmap and next steps for UK-endorsed ISSB standards, transition plan disclosures and possible future requirements for UK-listed and other UK companies. It says UK-endorsed standards are expected in Q1 2025, with any new government requirements no earlier than accounting periods beginning on or after 2026-01-01. Future FCA and government action will follow consultation.

title: Privacy policy for the Green Book Network
summary: HM Treasury published a privacy notice for the Green Book Network mailing list. It explains what personal data is collected, the lawful basis for processing, who may access it, retention, and how individuals can exercise UK GDPR rights or complain. No new regulatory requirements are created for firms.

title: Northern Ireland Executive’s Interim Fiscal Framework
summary: HM Treasury and the Northern Ireland Executive published an interim Fiscal Framework setting out agreed funding principles, including a 24% needs-based factor in the Barnett formula from 2024-25, higher capital borrowing from 2024-25, and further work towards a final fiscal framework. It is a policy agreement and update on devolved funding arrangements, not a financial-services rule or supervisory notice.

title: Joint Statement: EU-UK Financial Regulatory Forum, May 2024
summary: HM Treasury and the European Commission published a joint statement recording topics discussed at the second EU-UK Financial Regulatory Forum on 24 May 2024. It is a public record of the meeting, not a rule, consultation or supervisory notice, and creates no direct compliance deadline.

title: Treasury Minutes progress report – May 2024
summary: The Treasury published a progress report updating Parliament on how government departments are implementing accepted Public Accounts Committee recommendations across multiple sessions. It is an accountability/status document, not a new rule, consultation, or supervisory requirement. No direct obligations for firms are created.

title: Government Action on Fraud in Covid Support Schemes
summary: The government published a policy paper on action to tackle fraud in Covid support schemes and recover taxpayer money. It is an update on enforcement and recovery efforts, not a new rule or obligation. No compliance date or sector-specific requirement is stated.

title: Policy statement on onshore wind
summary: The government published a policy statement revising planning policy so onshore wind is treated the same as other energy development in the National Planning Policy Framework. It is a general policy announcement, not a financial-services rule or supervisory notice.

title: Draft Charter for Budget Responsibility text on the fiscal lock
summary: HM Treasury published draft Charter for Budget Responsibility text on the new fiscal lock, tied to the Budget Responsibility Bill. The draft explains how fiscally significant government announcements will be subject to independent OBR assessment and will be incorporated into the Charter in due course. No firm-specific action is set out, but it signals an imminent legislative change affecting the fiscal framework.

title: Four major high street banks broke CMA rules
summary: The CMA has published the Retail Banking Market Investigation Order 2017, which imposes binding remedies on retail banks and related providers of personal current accounts, business current accounts and SME banking. It sets staggered commencement dates for different articles, including some starting the day after the Order is made and others within 3, 6, 12 or 15 months. Firms in scope need to assess which remedies apply and when.

title: Changes to the Energy (Oil and Gas) Profits Levy
summary: The government announced changes to the Energy (Oil and Gas) Profits Levy. The levy rate rises to 38% from 1 November 2024, the levy is extended to 31 March 2030, and key investment allowances are being removed or reduced for qualifying expenditure on or after 1 November 2024. This affects upstream oil and gas activities.

title: Fixing the foundations: public spending audit 2024-25
summary: HM Treasury’s public spending audit sets out the government’s spending pressures, immediate savings, and the timetable for further decisions in the Budget on 30 October and the Spending Review. It is a policy document and correction slip, not a rule, guidance, or legal notice. No direct obligations are created for firms, though the document references wider tax and spending reforms.

title: 2024: Non-UK domiciled individuals- Policy Summary
summary: HM Treasury published a policy summary on planned tax changes for non-UK domiciled individuals. It says the government will remove domicile status from the tax system and introduce a new residence-based regime from 6 April 2025. The document is informational and invites further technical comments, but it does not itself create rules for firms.

title: User and Preparer Advisory Group Minutes: October 2023
summary: Minutes of the Government Financial Reporting User and Preparer Advisory Group meeting on 10 October 2023. The paper records discussion updates on local government, a performance report thematic review, ICAEW matters, GFR review progress and future thematic reviews, and notes the group’s terms of reference. It does not impose any requirements or set deadlines for firms.

title: CMA letter to Starling Bank about breaching Part 3 of the Retail Banking Order
summary: The CMA wrote to Starling Bank about a breach of Part 3 of the Retail Banking Market Investigation Order 2017, relating to the Business Current Account service quality survey. Starling must report any non-compliance within 14 days once aware, and the letter notes remediation already underway. The CMA will monitor the survey boost and future compliance; the public letter was copied to the FCA.

title: Treasury Minutes – September 2024
summary: This Treasury Minutes document is the government’s response to Committee of Public Accounts reports on a range of topics, including BBC reform, government resilience, student loans, Universal Credit, legal aid, asylum accommodation, mobile connectivity, whistleblowing, home heating and rail reform. It records ministerial responses to parliamentary recommendations but does not itself set regulatory rules or obligations for firms.

title: Joint statement on the UK-U.S. Financial Regulatory Working Group meeting - September 2024
summary: HM Treasury and US Treasury published a joint statement recording the tenth meeting of the UK-US Financial Regulatory Working Group on 3 September 2024. It summarises discussions and outcomes only; it does not set new requirements, deadlines, or guidance for firms.

title: Government financial reporting review: Best practice examples from 2018-19
summary: HM Treasury publishes best-practice examples for central government annual reports and accounts, focused on performance reporting, accountability and financial information. It reinforces expectations under the FReM for clearer narrative, trend data and accessible presentation. It is aimed at departments and other bodies preparing ARAs, with the examples intended to inform future reporting practice.

title: The Payment Services (Amendment) Regulations 2024
summary: HM Treasury has drafted amendments to the Payment Services Regulations 2017 to let a payer’s PSP delay executing certain payment orders where it suspects fraud or dishonesty by a third party. The PSP must notify the payer promptly and the delay cannot exceed the specified time limit. The instrument also makes the PSP liable for charges and interest caused by the delay. Commencement is stated as to be set.

title: Welsh Rates of Income Tax outturn reconciliation for 2022-23
summary: HMT publishes an explanatory policy note on the 2022-23 Welsh Rates of Income Tax outturn reconciliation. It explains that HMRC’s actual income tax data updates the Welsh Government’s funding, increasing overall funding for 2025-26 by £53 million. No action is required from regulated firms.

title: National Wealth Fund: Mobilising Private Investment
summary: HMT sets out the policy rationale and intended operating model for the new National Wealth Fund, replacing UKIB’s role with a broader mandate to mobilise private investment into clean energy and wider industrial strategy priorities. It describes funding, governance and investment approach, but does not impose immediate requirements on firms. No deadline or consultation close date is stated.

title: Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee - 3 October 2024
summary: HMT published a communiqué from the Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee meeting held on 3 October 2024. It is an informational policy paper describing regular ministerial discussion of economic and finance matters affecting the UK, with no new requirements or deadlines.

title: Financial Services Policy Update
summary: HM Treasury’s Financial Services Policy Update says the government supports the Bank of England’s consultation on changes to MREL setting for banks and plans draft updates to the Special Resolution Regime Code of Practice. It also notes that some proposals will need secondary legislation and further industry engagement, but no immediate rule change is made here.

title: UK Government Green Financing: Allocation Report 2024
summary: HM Treasury’s annual UK Green Financing Allocation Report 2024 sets out how £10.9 billion raised in 2023-24 through green gilts and Green Savings Bonds was allocated to eligible green expenditures. It also updates cumulative programme issuance and notes the next impact report is due in autumn 2025. This is reporting and transparency information only, with no new obligations for firms.

title: Treasury Minutes – October 2024
summary: HM Treasury’s October 2024 Treasury Minutes sets out the government’s responses to several Public Accounts Committee reports on public spending, BBC performance, non-executive appointments and major projects. It is an accountability and response document, not a rule, consultation or enforcement notice, and it creates no direct obligations for firms.

title: World Bank 110th Development Committee meeting 2024: UK Governor's statement
summary: UK ministers’ statement to the World Bank Development Committee sets out the UK’s view on global financial system reform, support for fragile states, and a larger IDA replenishment. It is a policy/political statement with no direct FCA/PRA rule changes, deadlines, or obligations for firms.

title: Joint statement from the Specialised Committee on Financial Provisions, 25 October 2024
summary: The UK government and European Commission issued a joint statement noting progress at the tenth meeting of the Specialised Committee on Financial Provisions. It is an informational policy paper about the Financial Settlement workstreams, with no new requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: Post-implementation review of the Bank Referral Scheme
summary: HM Treasury has published a statutory post-implementation review of the Bank Referral Scheme under the Small and Medium Sized Business (Finance Platforms) Regulations 2015. It concludes the scheme still meets its objectives but identifies frictions and data-quality issues, and says a future consultation will consider possible changes to the statutory and operational design. The review notes the next PIR is due by 2025-10-14.

title: Tackling offshore tax non-compliance
summary: HMT publishes a policy paper on the government’s approach to offshore tax non-compliance, describing HMRC’s strategy to help taxpayers get tax right and take robust enforcement action. It notes additional resources announced at Autumn Budget 2024 to support HMRC’s work. This is an informational statement only and does not create new requirements for firms.

title: Corporate Tax Roadmap 2024
summary: HM Treasury sets out a Corporate Tax Roadmap for the rest of Parliament, describing intended stability in corporation tax, capital allowances, R&D reliefs, intangible assets and territorial taxation. It also signals future consultations and improved guidance, but this is a policy paper rather than a binding rule or consultation. No immediate compliance date is created for firms.

title: Response to the OBR review of the March 2024 forecast for departmental expenditure limits
summary: HM Treasury published a government response to the OBR review of the March 2024 departmental expenditure limits forecast. It explains evidence given to the OBR, updates on spending pressures and reserve management, and the Treasury’s response to the review. It is informational and does not create regulatory obligations for firms.

title: Government financial reporting review: Best practice examples from 2022-23
summary: HM Treasury published a best-practice review for 2022-23 government annual reports and accounts. It gives illustrative examples and criteria for clearer narrative, performance, accountability and financial reporting, aimed at central government accounts preparers. It is guidance and exemplars only, with no new requirements or deadline.

title: Transforming business rates
summary: HM Treasury has published a policy paper on reforming business rates in England, setting out priorities and inviting views from businesses and other stakeholders. It signals intended changes such as lower multipliers for retail, hospitality and leisure properties from 2026-27, but does not itself make rules. No immediate compliance action is required beyond monitoring and engaging in the reform process.

title: Terms of reference for the review of technology adoption
summary: HM Treasury published terms of reference for a cross-government review of barriers businesses face when adopting established and novel technologies. The review will be led by the Government Chief Scientific Adviser and National Technology Adviser and its recommendations will inform the industrial strategy and sector plans to be published alongside the spring Spending Review.

title: Autumn Budget 2024
summary: The Autumn Budget 2024 sets out the UK government’s fiscal framework, tax, spending and welfare plans, including new fiscal rules and a new Charter for Budget Responsibility. It is a government Budget laid before Parliament, not a regulator rule or supervisory notice. Where later Finance Bill or statutory instrument measures affect financial firms, those will be the binding follow-on steps.

title: Reforming the taxation of non-UK domiciled individuals
summary: HMT sets out draft legislation to replace the non-domicile tax regime from 6 April 2025 with a residence-based system, including a 4-year foreign income and gains regime, new inheritance tax rules, temporary repatriation facility, and changes to overseas workday relief and anti-avoidance rules. It is aimed at affected individuals and advisers, but will also matter to firms with internationally mobile clients and payroll/trust exposure.

title: Post-implementation review of the Commercial Credit Data Sharing scheme
summary: HM Treasury published a post-implementation review of the Commercial Credit Data Sharing scheme under the 2015 Regulations. It says CCDS has had a positive impact but identifies issues with data quality and market effects, and says HM Treasury intends to explore enhancements through a consultation. No immediate rule change or compliance deadline is set in this review.

title: A strong fiscal framework
summary: HMT published a policy paper explaining the government’s new fiscal framework and fiscal rules in Autumn Budget 2024. It is an informational document about public finance policy, not a binding rule for firms. No direct compliance deadline or firm-level obligation is set out.

title: Agricultural property relief and business property relief reforms
summary: HM Treasury published a policy paper summarising planned reforms to agricultural property relief and business property relief, with changes due from 6 April 2026. It also says agricultural property relief will be extended to certain environmental land management agreements from 6 April 2025. This is informational rather than a rule change notice for financial firms.

title: Soft Drinks Industry Levy review
summary: HM Treasury/HMRC has published a policy paper announcing a review of the Soft Drinks Industry Levy’s sugar thresholds and exemptions for milk-based and milk substitute drinks. It says the review has concluded with a formal consultation open for responses until 21 July 2025. This is an awareness item rather than the consultation itself.

title: National Insurance Fund Investment Account Report & Accounts 2023 to 2024
summary: HM Treasury’s National Insurance Fund Investment Account annual report and accounts for 2023-24 set out how the fund was invested, its performance, governance and audit information for the year ended 31 March 2024. It is an annual statutory account laid before Parliament, not a rule change or supervisory notice. No new requirements are created for firms.

title: Memorandum of Understanding between the Bank of England, FCA and PRA
summary: The FCA, PRA and Bank of England have published a Memorandum of Understanding on how they will coordinate their functions under the CTP regime in FSMA Chapter 3C. It sets out shared objectives, operating principles and the new CTP Consultation and Coordination Forum. No firm deadline is set, but it frames how future CTP-related decisions and consultations will be handled.

title: Next steps for reforming the UK Markets in Financial Instruments Directive
summary: HM Treasury has published a policy paper setting out its intention to make technical changes to the UK MiFID framework, including FCA powers over off-exchange commodity derivatives, revocation of some detailed investment firm rules, and transaction reporting changes. The changes require legislation, and revocations will only start when replacement rules are ready to take effect.

title: Pensions Investment Review: interim report
summary: HMT’s interim Pensions Investment Review sets out the government’s long-term vision for consolidation and scale in workplace defined contribution pensions and for reform of the LGPS to support higher returns and more UK investment. It is an interim policy paper and accompanying consultation context, not a final rule or binding change. The text says further proposals and a consultation will follow.

title: Home Credit Market Investigation Order
summary: The CMA has made the Home Credit Market Investigation Order 2007 Variation Order 2024, in force on 20 November 2024. It updates and trims the 2007 home credit market remedies, including replacing references to the CMA, removing certain website publication requirements, and revising information that must be disclosed for agreements.

title: Meeting minutes – October 2024
summary: HMT published meeting minutes for the Chancellor’s October 2024 discussion with the Bank of England Governor after the latest Financial Stability Report. The note records a statutory meeting required by the Bank of England Act 1998, but it does not itself change rules or create new obligations.

title: Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes Provisional Agenda: 11 December 2024
summary: HMT published a provisional agenda for the 11 December 2024 meeting of the UK-EU Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes. It is a meeting notice for a joint forum under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement and does not itself create or change requirements for firms.

title: Economic Evidence to the Pay Review Bodies: 2025-26 Pay Round
summary: HMT published economic evidence for the 2025-26 public sector pay round, setting out inflation, productivity, labour market and fiscal context for the Pay Review Bodies. It is background material to support government pay decisions, not a rule, consultation or supervisory notice. No direct action or compliance deadline is created for banks.

title: New rules and guidance for water references
summary: The CMA has issued new rules for water references under the Water Industry Act 1991, effective from 10 December 2024. They replace the relevant parts of CMA17 for redetermination references involving appointed water undertakers/sewerage undertakers in England and Wales. Firms involved in these references should use the new procedure set out in CMA204 from the effective date.

title: India-UK 3rd Financial Markets Dialogue: Joint Statement
summary: HM Treasury published a joint statement on the third India-UK Financial Markets Dialogue. It says UK and Indian governments and regulators discussed cooperation on capital markets, insurance, pensions, fintech, financial data and sustainable finance to support growth and investment. No specific obligations, deadlines or rule changes are set out.

title: Private Motor Insurance Market Investigation Order 2015
summary: The CMA published the Private Motor Insurance Market Investigation Order 2015, which sets binding requirements for the private motor insurance market and related price comparison websites in the UK. It includes compliance statements and NCB protection information, with Article 3’s implementation date moved to 1 August 2016. The Order applies to affected PMI insurers, brokers, providers and PCWs.

title: Energy network mergers: CMA190
summary: CMA guidance sets out the special merger regime for energy network enterprises under the Energy Act 2023 as applied in the Enterprise Act 2002. It explains how the CMA will assess and process qualifying mergers in Great Britain, including investigation steps, analytical approach and remedies. It is relevant immediately for merger activity involving energy network enterprises.

title: Rules of procedure for merger, market and special reference groups: CMA17
summary: The CMA has republished its procedural rules for merger, market and special reference groups (CMA17), replacing the March 2014 version and reflecting the DMCC Act 2024. The rules apply from 1 January 2025 and are binding on CMA chairs, groups and panel members. This is mainly relevant where the firm is involved in a CMA merger or market reference.

title: Mergers exceptions to the duty to refer and undertakings in lieu
summary: The CMA has updated its guidance on when it may decide not to refer a merger for a phase 2 investigation, including the ‘de minimis’ exception, insufficiently advanced transactions, and relevant customer benefits. It replaces the 2018 version and reflects current CMA practice under the Enterprise Act 2002, with the updated guidance published on 2 January 2025.

title: 2025 UK-China Economic and Financial Dialogue: policy outcomes
summary: HMT published a policy paper and fact sheet on the outcomes of the 2025 UK-China Economic and Financial Dialogue, concluded on 11 January 2025 by the UK Chancellor and Chinese Vice Premier. It is an informational publication describing bilateral discussion outcomes, not a rule, supervisory notice, or legal change for firms.

title: Further updated rules and guide for energy code modification appeals
summary: The CMA has published updated Energy Code Modification Appeals Rules (CMA196), made under the Energy Act 2004 and effective from 15 January 2024. The rules set the procedure for appeals under section 173, including applications, responses, interventions, hearings and document production. They replace the previous CC10 rules.

title: Scottish Income Tax outturn reconciliation for 2022-23
summary: HMT explains the 2022-23 Scottish Income Tax outturn reconciliation and its effect on Scottish Government funding. It states that updated HMRC and population data increase self-funding by £1,498 million, reduce block grant funding by £1,048 million, and lift overall 2025-26 funding by £451 million. It is informational only and creates no obligations for firms.

title: Working with the Funerals Market Investigation Order
summary: The CMA published guidance to help funeral directors and crematorium operators comply with the Funeral Market Investigation Order and related compliance checklist. It explains how affected firms should understand their legal obligations and submit financial information and compliance statements online.

title: Charter for Budget Responsibility: Autumn 2024
summary: HM Treasury has updated and republished the Charter for Budget Responsibility for autumn 2024, setting out the government’s fiscal policy framework, debt management approach and guidance to the OBR. It is laid before Parliament under the Budget Responsibility and National Audit Act 2011 and includes statutory provisions affecting fiscal policy governance, with the updated charter presented in January 2025.

title: UK-Japan Financial Regulatory Forum Joint Statement
summary: HM Treasury and the Japan Financial Services Agency published a joint statement recording the third UK-Japan Financial Regulatory Forum meeting and the topics discussed. It is a public record of the meeting outcomes and does not set new requirements or deadlines.

title: Payment Protection Insurance Market Investigation Order 2011: Directions to Cardif Pinnacle
summary: The CMA has issued directions to Cardif Pinnacle under the Payment Protection Insurance Market Investigation Order 2011 after finding four breaches in annual review statements sent to PPI customers. The directions relate to correcting and preventing inaccurate Annual Reviews and updating the CMA on progress. The order already applies to PPI providers; no new publication date for compliance action is stated in the excerpt.

title: 2025 Retrocession Agreement between HM Treasury and Pool Re
summary: HM Treasury has published the 2025 Retrocession Agreement between HM Treasury and Pool Re, which sets the contractual terms for government retrocession protection for terrorism reinsurance business. It replaces the prior 2022 arrangement for new and renewed relevant instruments from 1 April 2025, and terminates the 1993, 2015 and 2019 retrocession agreements. The document is presented to Parliament and contains the operative terms of the arrangement.

title: Public service pensions increase: 2025
summary: HM Treasury published the 2025 public service pensions increase note and multiplier tables. It says public service pensions in payment for a year will rise by 1.7% from 7 April 2025, with shorter-duration pensions increased proportionately. This is a general information/publishing notice for scheme administrators, not a new financial-services rule for firms.

title: UK CBAM International Group
summary: HM Treasury has published terms of reference for a UK CBAM International Group to share updates on UK CBAM policy design and gather feedback from international stakeholders. Countries can apply for membership by email, and the group will meet at least annually, with extra meetings if needed. No firm obligations or implementation dates are set out.

title: NS&I main estimates memorandum 2024 to 2025 (July 2024)
summary: HMT publishes NS&I’s 2024-25 main estimates memorandum, setting out spending controls, budget totals, and drivers of change for the year. It explains NS&I’s objectives, funding, efficiency plans and cash requirement, but does not create new regulatory obligations for firms. The document is informational and targeted at Parliament and public accountability rather than market participants.

title: Joint Statement: EU-UK Financial Regulatory Forum, February 2025
summary: HM Treasury and the European Commission published a joint statement recording topics covered at the third EU-UK Financial Regulatory Forum on 12 February 2025. It is a record of discussions under the UK-EU Memorandum of Understanding on Financial Services Cooperation, not a rule, consultation or supervisory requirement.

title: Memorandum of Understanding Between HM Treasury and the Bank of England 2025
summary: HM Treasury and the Bank of England have updated their Memorandum of Understanding after a 5-year review of the Bank’s capital framework parameters. The review says the existing capital target, floor and ceiling remain adequate and that the financial arrangements support the Bank’s transition to a demand-driven repo-backed operating framework. This is relevant to firms that interface with the Bank’s balance sheet and reserve operations, with no specific firm deadline stated.

title: Meeting minutes – January 2025
summary: These are January 2025 meeting minutes between the Chancellor and the Bank of England Governor about the latest Financial Stability Report. The minutes note the statutory duty to meet after each FSR publication and discuss the report and wider financial stability matters. No new rules, deadlines or obligations are created.

title: Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee - 27 February 2025
summary: This is a government communiqué from the Finance Interministerial Standing Committee summarising a ministerial meeting on economic and finance matters. It does not set out any new rules, consultations, deadlines or supervisory expectations for firms.

title: Fourth Trade Specialised Committee on Customs Cooperation and Rules of Origin Minutes
summary: HM Treasury published minutes of the fourth UK-EU Trade Specialised Committee on Customs Cooperation and Rules of Origin. The paper records discussions under the UK-EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement on customs cooperation, rules of origin and related trade facilitation topics. It is informational only and does not create new requirements or deadlines.

title: Chancellor meeting with Gilt-edged Market Makers: Minutes
summary: HM Treasury published summary minutes of the Chancellor’s meeting with primary dealer firms in the gilt market (GEMMs) on 6 March 2025. It is an inaugural engagement in a twice-yearly series and discusses views on global and UK economic prospects. No rule changes, deadlines, or obligations are set out.

title: Women in Finance Charter: Treasury Progress Update 2024
summary: HM Treasury publishes a progress update on its own Women in Finance Charter commitments, including an increase in female senior management representation to 50% by March 2024. It is an informational progress report, not a new rule or consultation, and does not create obligations for firms.

title: Performance Review of Digital Spend
summary: HMT published a review of digital spend across government, setting out findings and recommendations to improve how DDaT investment is funded, governed and evaluated. It proposes pathfinders, targeted training, updated Green Book guidance and better outcome metrics to inform SR25/SR27 decisions. This is an intelligence paper for government departments, not a binding rule for firms.

title: Anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism: Supervision Report 2023-24
summary: HM Treasury published its 2023-24 AML/CTF Supervision Report, describing how UK AML supervisors registered firms, assessed risk, monitored compliance and used enforcement during the year. It also highlights supervisory collaboration, guidance and planned improvements to the AML/CTF regime, but does not itself change rules or set a compliance deadline.

title: Markets in Financial Instruments Directive Organisational Regulation – Draft Statutory Instrument and Policy Note
summary: This draft Statutory Instrument amends FSMA 2000 and related secondary legislation on MiFID organisational and market-structure provisions. It sets out changes on suspension/removal from trading, position reporting, order execution and related definitions, and will come into force when the FSMA 2023 revocation of retained MiFID organisational rules takes effect. Parliament has already approved the draft; firms in scope should prepare for the new regime.

title: Announcement of Preliminary Market Engagement Exercise for the Digital Gilt Instrument (DIGIT) Pilot
summary: HM Treasury and the DMO launched preliminary market engagement for the DIGIT pilot, asking potential suppliers and market participants for views to shape the design and delivery of a digital gilt issuance. Responses to the engagement notice are requested by 11:59pm on 13 April 2025.

title: Statement of Strategic Priorities to the National Wealth Fund
summary: HM Treasury issued a statement of strategic priorities to the National Wealth Fund for this Parliament. It sets the government’s growth and clean energy expectations for the NWF and asks it to produce a new Strategic Plan reflecting those priorities. The paper also says legislation will be introduced later to broaden the NWF’s mandate beyond infrastructure, when parliamentary time allows.

title: Launch of the UK Strategic Public Investment Forum
summary: HM Treasury published a policy paper on the UK public financial institutions landscape and announced a new CEO-level Forum to improve strategic alignment and cooperation between public financial organisations and government. It is a high-level information piece, with no new rules, deadlines or compliance requirements for banks.

title: Sovereign Grant Act 2011: report of the Royal Trustees on the Sovereign Grant Review 2025-26
summary: This is a statutory report under the Sovereign Grant Act 2011 setting the Sovereign Grant for 2025-26 and explaining how it was calculated. It is addressed to Parliament and uses the Act’s formula; it does not create new obligations for regulated firms. No action date applies to a bank unless it has a specific public-sector dependency or interest.

title: Spring Statement 2025 document
summary: The Chancellor’s Spring Statement 2025 sets out the government’s fiscal and spending plans, including defence spending, planning reform, public service reform and growth measures. It is a policy/political statement rather than a regulatory rule, so it does not itself create compliance deadlines for firms. Financial-services teams should monitor for later legislation, consultations or rule changes that follow from it.

title: Treasury Minutes progress report – March 2025
summary: HMT published its March 2025 Treasury Minutes progress report, a record of government progress on implementing Committee of Public Accounts recommendations across multiple parliamentary sessions. It is a parliamentary update with references to various departmental actions and no direct regulatory requirements for firms.

title: Debt management report 2025-26
summary: HM Treasury’s annual Debt Management Report 2025-26 sets out the government’s borrowing plans, debt management policy and remit for the DMO, NS&I and Exchequer cash management for 2025-26. It includes the planned size and maturity structure of gilt issuance and NS&I net financing targets, but does not itself create obligations for firms. It is mainly background and market information.

title: Supporting documents for Spring Statement 2025
summary: HM Treasury published supporting analysis for Spring Statement 2025 showing the estimated household income impacts of tax, welfare and public service spending decisions. It is an informational distributional report, not a rule, consultation or supervisory notice. No direct actions or compliance deadlines are created for firms.

title: Treasury Minutes – April 2025
summary: HM Treasury’s April 2025 Treasury Minutes set out the government’s responses to Public Accounts Committee reports across several departments, including HMRC, DfE, DWP, Home Office and others. It is a parliamentary response document summarising agreed actions and target implementation dates where relevant, not a rule, notice or enforcement instrument. No direct obligations are created for banks.

title: UK-India 13th Economic and Financial Dialogue: Joint Statement
summary: HMT and India’s finance ministry issued a joint statement on the 13th Economic and Financial Dialogue, highlighting continued cooperation on trade, financial services, capital markets, listings, pensions, insurance and rupee internationalisation. It also notes plans for future dialogue and an FCA-IFSCA exchange of letters to support regulatory cooperation. No direct requirements are imposed on firms in this statement.

title: HM Treasury and Financial Conduct Authority Regulatory Perimeter Meeting – March 2025
summary: This is a record of a meeting between HMT and the FCA about the FCA’s Perimeter Report and the financial services regulatory perimeter. It does not set new rules or deadlines; it simply summarises the discussion on 24 March 2025.

title: Memorandum of Understanding between the OBR and HMT – macroeconomic models
summary: HM Treasury and the OBR published a non-binding memorandum of understanding on joint governance, maintenance and development of shared macroeconomic models. It covers several named models and sets expectations for collaboration, record-keeping, quality assurance and review arrangements. It is an internal/public administration agreement rather than a rule, consultation or supervisory notice, and creates no direct obligations for regulated firms.

title: Reappointment of Financial Conduct Authority Chief Executive Officer
summary: HM Treasury announces the reappointment of the FCA Chief Executive for a second five-year term and sets out ministerial expectations for the FCA to support growth, competitiveness and informed risk-taking. It is an intelligence-style letter, not a rule, consultation or supervisory notice, and it creates no direct obligations for firms.

title: Economic Crime Levy Report 2023-24
summary: HM Treasury published an annual report on the Economic Crime Levy for 2023-24. It explains how levy receipts were collected and allocated to anti-money laundering and economic crime activity, including funding for investigators, intelligence teams and AML supervision reform. It is informational only and does not set new requirements for firms.

title: Sanctions implementation and enforcement: cross-government review, May 2025
summary: HMT and other government bodies published a policy paper setting out conclusions from a cross-government review of UK sanctions implementation and enforcement. It provides background, objectives, strategic context and summary engagement, but does not itself change sanctions rules or impose new obligations.

title: Treasury Minutes – May 2025
summary: HM Treasury published its May 2025 Treasury Minutes, which are the government’s responses to Public Accounts Committee reports across several departments, including an NHS financial sustainability report. The document sets out government agreement or disagreement with recommendations and target implementation dates where relevant, but it does not itself create new regulatory requirements for firms.

title: Pensions Investment Review: Final Report
summary: HMT’s final report on the Pensions Investment Review sets out the government’s conclusions and intended reforms for defined contribution pensions and the Local Government Pension Scheme, including planned legislation to support larger, more consolidated schemes and a shift toward value over cost. It also outlines future work on the investment pipeline and a forthcoming pensions roadmap. No immediate compliance deadline is stated in the excerpt.

title: Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes Minutes: 11 December 2024
summary: HMT published minutes of the 11 December 2024 UK-EU Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes. The discussion covers UK association to Horizon Europe and Copernicus, participation trends, exclusion issues, future framework programme plans, and visa/health surcharge costs for researchers. It is informational only and does not create any new requirements.

title: Green Book Review 2025: Findings and actions
summary: HM Treasury published a review of the Green Book and set out actions to simplify appraisal guidance, clarify business case expectations, improve place-based assessment, and publish business cases for major projects and programmes. It is aimed at government departments and public-sector decision makers, not regulated firms. No compliance deadline or direct obligation for banks is created.

title: Government Response to the 2024 Fiscal Risks and Sustainability Report
summary: HM Treasury’s response explains the government’s fiscal framework reforms and how they relate to the 2024 Fiscal Risks and Sustainability Report. It discusses spending, debt sustainability, welfare controls, OBR reporting and related fiscal-policy commitments, but does not create new regulatory requirements for firms.

title: Northern Ireland Interim Fiscal Framework Implementation Update: Relative Funding Methodology
summary: HMT publishes an implementation update setting out the agreed relative funding methodology for assessing Northern Ireland Executive funding against comparable UK Government funding. It explains how the 124% threshold, transitional factor, tax devolution adjustments, non-domestic rates and population data are used in the calculation. No direct compliance action or deadline is created for firms.

title: Departmental Efficiency Delivery Plans
summary: HMT publishes government departmental efficiency plans for Spending Review 2025, setting out non-binding efficiency targets and delivery themes across departments through 2028-29. It is an informational policy paper for public transparency, not a financial-services rule or supervisory action. No direct obligations are created for banks or other regulated firms.

title: Tax Policy Making Principles
summary: HMT has published a policy paper setting out high-level principles for how it will make tax policy, including a single major fiscal event cycle, more targeted consultation, and greater transparency. It does not create any firm obligations or set a compliance date.

title: Update: domestic premises suppliers and Buy-Now, Pay-Later (BNPL)
summary: The government will lay a negative statutory instrument to exempt domestic premises suppliers from needing credit broking permissions to offer BNPL as a payment option. This affects firms using BNPL in domestic premises sales. No implementation date is stated in the text, but the measure is intended to take effect through secondary legislation.

title: Treasury Minutes – June 2025
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes is the government’s response to Committee of Public Accounts reports, including recommendations on AI in government, energy bills support, NHS dentistry, and biomass. It sets out departmental responses and target implementation dates for some actions, but it does not create financial-services obligations for firms.

title: User and Preparer Advisory Group Minutes: March 2025
summary: HM Treasury published minutes and agenda papers for the User and Preparer Advisory Group meeting held on 5 March 2025. The papers discuss IFRS 18/19, Whole of Government Accounts, local government updates, and proposed changes to the Financial Reporting Manual for non-investment assets, including valuation and intangible asset guidance from 1 April 2025.

title: User and Preparer Advisory Group Minutes: October 2024
summary: Minutes of HM Treasury’s User and Preparer Advisory Group meeting on 10 October 2024. The agenda covered IFRS 18 and 19, a thematic review update on non-investment assets, Whole of Government Accounts, local government updates, and GFR review progress. This is a record of discussion only and does not set new requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: User and Preparer Advisory Group Minutes: April 2024
summary: HM Treasury published minutes from the User and Preparer Advisory Group meeting held on 11 April 2024. The papers and discussion cover public-sector financial reporting topics including local government updates, the performance report thematic review, FReM changes, SOPS reporting, sustainability reporting and NAO updates. This is an informational meeting record; it does not itself create new obligations.

title: UK Infrastructure: A 10 Year Strategy
summary: HM Treasury sets out a 10-year UK infrastructure strategy covering economic, housing and social infrastructure, with NISTA overseeing implementation and progress reporting. It is a policy paper and strategic statement, not a rule, consultation or enforcement notice. No direct regulatory obligations are created for firms in the publication itself.

title: UK-U.S. Financial Regulatory Working Group June 2025: Joint Statement
summary: HM Treasury and the U.S. Treasury published a joint statement recording the 11th UK-U.S. Financial Regulatory Working Group meeting and summarising topics discussed and outcomes. It is informational only and does not set new requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: Joint statement from the Specialised Committee on Financial Provisions, 25 June 2025
summary: HMT and the European Commission issued a joint statement noting progress at the Specialised Committee on Financial Provisions. It is a policy paper about workstreams on invoices the EU sends to the UK under the Financial Settlement, with no firm-facing obligations or deadlines.

title: Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee – 26 June 2025
summary: This is a UK government communiqué from a Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee meeting on 26 June 2025. It is an informational policy paper about discussions between UK and devolved finance ministers, with no specific regulatory rule, consultation, or requirement for firms.

title: Supporting documents for Spending Review 2025
summary: HM Treasury published an analytical paper on the distributional impact of tax, welfare and public service spending decisions for Spending Review 2025. It models household impacts in 2028-29 and explains the data and methodology used. The document is informational only and does not create or change requirements for firms.

title: 10 Year Infrastructure Strategy Working Paper
summary: HMT has published a working paper on a 10-year infrastructure strategy for the UK. It sets out high-level principles, objectives and next steps for developing a cross-government plan covering economic, housing and social infrastructure, with consultation continuing and publication planned for June alongside the spending review.

title: Spending Review 2025 document
summary: HM Treasury has published the full Spending Review 2025 document and a correction slip. It is a government policy paper setting out spending plans, not a financial-services rule, supervisory notice, or obligation for firms.

title: Ancillary Activities Exemption – Draft Legislation
summary: HMT has published near-final draft legislation to replace the current ancillary activities test with a new, simpler regime and give the FCA rulemaking powers. It affects firms using the ancillary activities exemption for commodity derivatives, emissions allowances or related derivatives. The new regime is due to come into force on 1 January 2027, and technical comments on the draft SI are requested by 28 August 2025.

title: 10th UK-Singapore Financial Dialogue July 2025: Joint Statement
summary: HM Treasury and the Monetary Authority of Singapore published a joint statement recording discussions and outcomes from the 10th UK-Singapore Financial Dialogue held on 2 July 2025. It is a record of the meeting and does not set new rules or deadlines.

title: FSCS Annual Report and Class Statements 2024/25
summary: FSCS’s 2024/25 annual report and accounts summarises activity, finances, governance and strategy for the year ended 31 March 2025. It highlights compensation paid, recoveries from failed firms, customer outcomes and future priorities, including preparations for any outcome of the deposit protection limit consultation. No new binding requirements are created by the report itself.

title: Thematic Review of Sustainability Reporting
summary: HM Treasury’s thematic review assesses central government sustainability reporting and says it will decouple Sustainability Reporting Guidance from Greening Government Commitments, remove some mandatory environmental metrics, keep TCFD-aligned disclosures and key GGC metrics, and develop further principles-based guidance. HMT plans to set out a proposal for FRAB in November 2025.

title: Post Implementation Review of IFRS 16
summary: HMT published a post-implementation review of IFRS 16 Leases in central government financial reporting. It summarises feedback from preparers, users and FRAB on the 2022-23 implementation process and disclosure quality, and says lessons will inform future standards including IFRS 17, IFRS 18 and IFRS 19. No new compliance date or rule change is set out.

title: Updating the UK’s regulatory framework for central counterparties
summary: HMT publishes a policy note on draft statutory instruments to replace the CCP framework in assimilated law with a new UK regime under FSMA 2023. It explains how the Central Counterparties (Amendment) Regulations 2025 and related overseas CCP rules will take effect when the relevant UK EMIR provisions are revoked. The paper is for technical comment; the new Bank rulebook is expected to be published for consultation on 18 July 2025.

title: Memorandum of Understanding: Overseas Recognition Regimes
summary: HM Treasury, the Bank of England, PRA and FCA published a memorandum of understanding on how they will coordinate on Overseas Recognition Regimes. It explains the process for assessing overseas jurisdictions, seeking regulator advice, and monitoring existing designations. It does not itself change rules or impose a compliance deadline.

title: Overseas Recognition Regimes Guidance Document
summary: HM Treasury published guidance on Overseas Recognition Regimes, explaining how it will assess, designate and review overseas jurisdictions whose regulatory frameworks produce similar outcomes to the UK’s. It describes the recognition framework, the factors Treasury may consider, and how monitoring and reviews work. It is informational and does not itself create new obligations.

title: Digital Gilt Instrument (DIGIT) Pilot Update
summary: HM Treasury sets out additional features to be tested in the Digital Gilt Instrument (DIGIT) pilot after reviewing responses to the earlier procurement process. This is an update on the pilot design for potential suppliers and the wider financial services sector; no binding rule changes are made and no dates are stated.

title: Wholesale Financial Markets Digital Strategy
summary: HMT published a policy paper setting out the government’s strategy for digitalising UK wholesale financial markets, including use of distributed ledger technology and coordination with regulators and industry via a Digital Markets Champion. It is an agenda-setting document rather than a binding rule or consultation, and it names no compliance deadline.

title: Reclaim Fund Ltd Annual Report and Accounts 2024/25
summary: Reclaim Fund Ltd’s annual report and accounts for 2024/25 describes the Dormant Assets Scheme’s activity, governance and financial results, including distributions to good causes and participating financial institutions. It is an informational annual report laid before Parliament, not a new rule or supervisory action.

title: Financial Services Regulators Complaints Commissioner Annual Report and Accounts 2024-25 and regulator responses
summary: HMT published the Financial Services Regulators Complaints Commissioner’s Annual Report and Accounts for 2024-25. It reviews complaint handling by the FCA, PRA and PSR over the year ended 31 March 2025 and discusses themes such as P2P lending and SIPPs. It is an informational report with no new obligations or deadlines for firms.

title: Treasury Minutes – July 2025
summary: Treasury Minutes is HM Treasury’s response to Public Accounts Committee reports on HMRC, government cyber resilience, DHSC accounts and tackling violence against women and girls. It records agreed recommendations and target implementation dates for HMRC, including a summer 2025 Transformation Roadmap, but does not itself create binding requirements for firms.

title: National risk assessment of money laundering and terrorist financing 2025
summary: HMT published the 2025 National Risk Assessment of money laundering and terrorist financing. It sets out UK ML/TF risks, including sector-specific risks and cross-cutting issues such as cryptoassets and AI, and is intended to inform future policy, regulatory and operational priorities. No immediate rule changes or deadlines are created in the publication itself.

title: Digitisation Taskforce - July 2025
summary: HMT’s Digitisation Taskforce final report sets out recommendations to modernise UK shareholding by moving away from paper share certificates and improving the intermediated system. It discusses an implementation timetable, possible legislative and regulatory changes, and protections for investors. It is a policy/intelligence document, not a binding rule or consultation with a closing date.

title: Treasury Minutes – August 2025
summary: HM Treasury’s August 2025 Treasury Minutes sets out the government’s responses to Public Accounts Committee reports across several departments. It is primarily an informational government response document, summarising agreed recommendations and implementation status, including digital procurement changes and other departmental matters. No direct regulatory obligations for banks or firms are created.

title: Welsh Rates of Income Tax outturn reconciliation for 2023-24
summary: HMT published an explanatory policy paper on the 2023-24 Welsh Rates of Income Tax outturn reconciliation. It explains how HMRC outturn data updates Welsh Government funding, with a net £53 million increase to overall funding for 2026-27. No action is required for firms and no regulatory obligations are created.

title: Scottish Income Tax outturn reconciliation for 2023-24
summary: HMT published an explanatory policy paper on the 2023-24 Scottish Income Tax outturn reconciliation. It updates how HMRC outturn data and revised population estimates affect the Scottish Government’s funding for 2026-27, increasing overall funding by £406 million. This is informational and does not create obligations for firms.

title: Memorandum of Understanding on financial crisis management
primary_functions: Board; Regulatory change; Compliance; Prudential; Risk
summary: HMT published a policy paper setting out the Memorandum of Understanding between the Treasury, Bank of England and PRA on resolution planning and financial crisis management. It explains how the authorities will coordinate to manage potential financial crises; it does not itself impose new firm obligations or set a compliance date.

title: Proposed amendments to the Money Laundering Regulations - draft SI and policy note
primary_functions: Regulatory change; Legal; Compliance; Financial crime
summary: HM Treasury publishes a draft statutory instrument and policy note amending the Money Laundering Regulations and related legislation. It is a four-week technical consultation closing on 2025-09-30. The final instrument is expected in early 2026 and to commence 21 days after being made, with some cryptoasset provisions tied to the FSMA cryptoasset perimeter.

title: Get Britain Working White Paper
summary: This is a government policy paper setting out proposed reforms to employment, health and skills support to reduce economic inactivity and improve labour market participation. It is not a regulatory rule, supervisory notice, or binding requirement for firms. No direct compliance deadline or obligation is created for financial firms.

title: EM on EU excise duty applied to tobacco products COM(2025)581)
summary: HMT has submitted an explanatory memorandum on EU proposals to recast tobacco excise duty rules and amend excise movement arrangements. The paper explains the likely Northern Ireland and policy implications, but notes the EU measures are still under consideration and may change or not be adopted. The proposals are expected to start from 2028, with a four-year transition for some rate increases if enacted.

title: Business rates: forward look
summary: HMT has published a policy paper giving a high-level forward look at planned business rates reforms. It says the government intends to work with stakeholders over this Parliament, alongside 2026 and 2029 revaluations, and recalls the Autumn Budget 2024 plan for two lower multipliers for Retail, Hospitality and Leisure properties below £500,000 rateable value.

title: Transforming Business Rates: Interim Report
summary: HM Treasury’s interim report on business rates summarises stakeholder feedback and signals further engagement on possible reforms, including a move from a “slab” to “slice” tax structure, changes to Small Business Rates Relief, Improvement Relief, valuation methodology and VOA/HMRC administrative changes. It is not a policy statement and does not itself change rules. A further update is promised at Autumn Budget 2025; one tax rate change for retail, hospitality and leisure properties was previously announced for April 2026.

title: Treasury Minutes – September 2025
summary: Treasury Minutes sets out the government’s responses to Public Accounts Committee reports across several departments, including education, immigration, tax, research and water regulation. It is a parliamentary response document, not a rule, consultation, supervisory notice or enforcement action. No direct obligations are created for firms, though the paper contains policy updates and planned departmental actions.

title: Chancellor meeting with Gilt-edged Market Makers: Minutes - September 2025
summary: HM Treasury published summary minutes of the Chancellor’s meeting with gilt-edged market makers on 22 September 2025. It is an informational record of discussions on global and UK economic prospects and creates no new requirements or deadlines for firms.

title: UK-Australia Financial Regulatory Forum September 2025: Joint Statement
summary: HM Treasury and the Australian Treasury published a joint statement recording the first UK-Australia Financial Regulatory Forum held on 24 September 2025. It summarises what was discussed and the key outcomes, but does not set out new rules, obligations or deadlines for firms.

title: Rules for the digital markets competition regime levy (SMS Levy)
summary: The CMA has made binding rules setting how the SMS Levy is calculated, invoiced and paid for firms with strategic market status under the DMCC Act. The rules apply from the chargeable year starting 1 April 2025 and cover the inaugural 2025-26 year and later years unless amended or replaced.

title: Joint Statement: EU-UK Financial Regulatory Forum- October 2025
summary: HM Treasury and the European Commission published a joint statement recording what was discussed at the fourth EU-UK Financial Regulatory Forum on 1 October 2025. It is a public record and does not set new requirements or deadlines.

title: G7 Cyber Expert Group Statement on AI and Cybersecurity
summary: The G7 Cyber Expert Group issued a statement on AI and cybersecurity, encouraging jurisdictions to monitor AI developments, promote collaboration, and address emerging cyber risks from AI. It is an informational policy statement with no direct UK firm obligations or deadlines.

title: Block Grant Transparency: October 2025
summary: HM Treasury published the seventh Block Grant Transparency update and explanatory note, showing how block grants for the Scottish Government, Welsh Government and Northern Ireland Executive are calculated. It is an informational policy paper with no new regulatory requirements for financial firms.

title: Reclaim Fund Limited – Framework Document 2025
summary: HM Treasury published the 2025 Framework Document for Reclaim Fund Ltd, setting out its governance, accountability, reporting and risk arrangements. It confirms RFL’s status as a central government NDPB and its FCA regulation as a dormant account fund operator. The document is an updated governance framework for RFL rather than a new rule or supervisory action.

title: World Bank Group and International Monetary Fund 2025 Annual Meetings, Development Committee: UK Governors' statement
summary: UK ministers’ statement at the World Bank/IMF Development Committee meeting on 16 October 2025. It is a policy paper and speech-style publication with no new rules, deadlines or obligations for firms.

title: An introduction to the UK public investment landscape
summary: HMT published an explainer on the UK public investment landscape, describing the roles of bodies such as the British Business Bank, National Wealth Fund, Innovate UK, UK Export Finance, Homes England and devolved investment bodies. It highlights how they collaborate to crowd in private capital and support growth, clean energy, exports and regional development. No new rules, obligations or deadlines are created.

title: Joint statement on regional investment from UK public investment bodies
summary: UK public investment bodies’ CEOs issue a joint statement saying they will work with government and the private sector to support regional growth, Local Growth Plans and regional investment across the UK. It is a policy/intelligence statement with no new requirements or deadlines.

title: Statement of strategic priorities to the British Business Bank
summary: HMT and the Department for Business and Trade published a 5-year statement of strategic priorities for the British Business Bank. It sets the bank’s mission from April 2026, four priorities, and increases its economic capital limit to £25.6 billion. This is a government policy paper, not a rule or supervisory notice for regulated firms.

title: Joint Exchequer Committee (Scotland) – 17 October 2025
summary: This is a government communique reporting that the UK Chief Secretary to the Treasury and the Scottish Finance Secretary met to discuss Scotland’s Fiscal Framework. It does not announce any rule, guidance, consultation, or binding requirement for firms.

title: Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee – 17 October 2025
summary: A Treasury policy paper publishes a communiqué from the Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee meeting held on 17 October 2025. It is an informational government update on finance matters affecting the UK, with no specific regulatory requirement, deadline, or firm action set out.

title: Meeting minutes – July 2025
summary: HM Treasury published minutes of the Chancellor’s July 2025 meeting with the Bank of England Governor after the Financial Stability Report. The note records discussion of financial stability matters and the statutory meeting requirement, but it does not itself change any rules or impose new obligations.

title: Social Impact Investment Advisory Group
summary: HMT’s Social Impact Investment Advisory Group report sets out a non-binding roadmap for government to mobilise impact capital and the wider impact economy. It recommends stronger leadership, an Office for the Impact Economy, a mobilisation mindset in public-sector delivery, and targeted reforms on pensions, giving and philanthropy. No firm obligations or compliance dates are created for regulated firms.

title: Financial Inclusion Strategy
summary: HM Treasury has published a Financial Inclusion Strategy setting out a cross-government programme to improve access to banking, products and services for underserved groups. It signals future initiatives such as banking hubs, inclusive design work, payroll savings schemes and small-sum loans pilots, but does not itself create binding requirements for firms.

title: Updating the UK’s exemption framework for intragroup Over the Counter Derivatives
summary: Draft UK statutory regulations amend the EMIR intragroup exemption framework for OTC derivatives. They change the intragroup transaction definition and exemption conditions for UK and third-country counterparties, including FCA notification and non-objection mechanics. The draft is laid before Parliament and will come into force when the related revocation in FSMA 2023 commencement takes effect.

title: Strategy for future retail payments infrastructure
summary: HM Treasury sets out its strategy for future UK retail payments infrastructure, following the National Payments Vision. It describes desired outcomes for the next-generation infrastructure, including innovation, competition, security and financial inclusion, and the role of the new governance model and future Retail Payments Infrastructure Board/Delivery Company. No binding requirements are created in this document.

title: Accelerated Settlement (T+1)
summary: Draft regulations are laid before Parliament to shorten settlement for transferable securities executed on a UK trading venue from T+2 to T+1, with exemptions for certain trades. They come into force on 11 October 2027 and amend the settlement date rules in Regulation (EU) No 909/2014 as onshored/modified for the UK.

title: Entrepreneurship in the UK
summary: HMT has published a policy paper setting out its entrepreneurship agenda for the UK, including support for scale-ups, R&D, procurement reform, tax reliefs and public finance institutions. It also says it will publish a Call for Evidence on tax policies alongside the paper and indicates further work over the next year. This is strategic policy direction, not a binding rule change.

title: Effects of the business rates retail, hospitality and leisure multipliers and high-value multiplier
summary: HMT published analysis of the business rates retail, hospitality and leisure multipliers and the higher multiplier for valuable properties in England. It explains the 2026-27 rates and scope by property type, but does not itself set the rules. The document is informational and supports changes announced in earlier legislation and budget measures.

title: Independent Review of the Loan Charge
summary: HMT publishes an independent review of the Loan Charge, a tax-avoidance measure affecting individuals caught in disguised remuneration loan schemes. It recommends a new final settlement approach to bring outstanding cases to a close. This is an intelligence/reporting publication only; it does not itself change law or impose deadlines.

title: Digital Services Tax Review
summary: HMT has published a review of the Digital Services Tax, explaining its purpose, performance and administration since its introduction in April 2020. It is an informational report laid before Parliament and does not itself change tax law or impose new requirements. The review discusses the interim nature of DST pending a global tax solution and its impacts on digital businesses.

title: Reforming the spending control and accountability framework
summary: HM Treasury and the Office for Value for Money set out plans to reform central government spending controls, approvals and accountability. The paper proposes a phased update to rules and guidance, with departments expected to streamline internal approvals and improve transparency to Parliament. It is a policy paper only; no direct obligations are created for financial firms.

title: Evaluation of the Office for Value for Money
summary: HM Treasury publishes an evaluation of the Office for Value for Money, a time-limited unit that closed alongside Budget 2025. The report assesses whether the OVfM met its remit, likely lasting impact and value for money, using interviews and document review. It is an informational evaluation only and does not create obligations for firms.

title: 10 Year Efficiency Projections
summary: HM Treasury published a policy paper setting out 10-year efficiency projections for selected government programmes funded at Spending Review 2025. It explains the prototype methodology and gives illustrative long-term value-for-money and efficiency forecasts for departments; it does not create rules or deadlines for regulated firms.

title: Government Response to the 2025 Fiscal Risks and Sustainability Report
summary: HM Treasury’s response to the OBR’s 2025 Fiscal Risks and Sustainability Report explains the government’s approach to long-term fiscal sustainability, debt reduction, and balance-sheet management. It discusses Budget 2025 measures, tax base changes, pensions, climate and financial-asset reforms, but does not set new requirements for firms in this document.

title: Supporting documents for Budget 2025
summary: HM Treasury’s Budget 2025 supporting document provides distributional analysis of how tax, welfare and public spending decisions affect household incomes. It is an informational background paper accompanying the Budget, not a rule, consultation or supervisory notice. The document references policy measures with implementation dates, but it does not itself create obligations.

title: Budget 2025 document
summary: HMT has published the Budget 2025 document. This is an informational government budget paper rather than a regulatory rule, consultation or supervisory notice, so firms should review it for any relevant tax or policy announcements but there is no direct compliance action stated in this publication.

title: G7 Fundamental Elements of Collective Cyber Incident Response and Recovery in the Financial Sector
summary: HMT publishes non-binding G7 principles for collective cyber incident response and recovery in the financial sector. The document sets out high-level elements for establishing, using, maintaining and testing collective response arrangements, but it does not create regulatory requirements or deadlines. It is aimed at financial authorities, financial entities and relevant third-party service providers.

title: Creating a Provisional Licences Authorisation Regime: Policy Update 2025
summary: HM Treasury sets out a policy update on a proposed provisional licences regime that would need primary legislation before it can be created. The regime would let certain new FCA-authorised firms carry on limited regulated activities under time-limited, modified conditions while they work towards full authorisation. No immediate compliance date is set; the FCA will develop more detailed proposals later.

title: Treasury Minutes progress report – December 2025
summary: This Treasury Minutes progress report records the government’s progress on implementing agreed recommendations from the Committee of Public Accounts across multiple sessions. It is a parliamentary update on outstanding and completed reports, not a rule, supervision document, or enforcement notice, and it does not create new obligations for firms.

title: Joint Statement for the automatic exchange of information on immovable property
summary: HMT published a policy paper joint statement announcing the UK and 24 other jurisdictions aim to implement the OECD’s framework for automatic exchange of information on immovable property by 2029 or 2030. It is a transparency and anti-evasion initiative, but it does not itself create binding requirements for firms.

title: Targeted Support
summary: The government publishes a consultation response on the targeted support regime for pensions and investments. It confirms the policy direction, notes the final SI will be corrected, and says targeted support is expected to roll out from early April 2026, with the FCA authorisation gateway opening in March 2026. Firms wanting to provide targeted support should review the near-final FCA rules and prepare for permissions.

title: Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes Provisional Agenda 15 December 2025
summary: HMT published a provisional agenda for the UK-EU Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes meeting on 15 December 2025. It is a meeting agenda only and does not create or change requirements for firms.

title: Economic Evidence to the Pay Review Bodies: 2026-27 Pay Round
summary: HM Treasury published economic evidence for the 2026-27 Pay Review Bodies pay round, setting the wider economic, labour market and fiscal context for independent recommendations. It is background policy material for public-sector pay setting, with no direct rule change or compliance deadline for firms.

title: Treasury Minutes – December 2025
summary: This Treasury Minute is HMT’s government response to Public Accounts Committee reports on defence, justice, housing, civil service delivery and pensions. It records departmental answers and target implementation dates, including a March 2026 plan for MoD reserve-force reforms and legislative measures to remove barriers to movement between Regular and Reserve Service. It is informational rather than a regulatory change for financial firms.

title: Regulatory regime for cryptoassets (regulated activities) – Draft SI and Policy Note
summary: Draft statutory instrument and policy note to create a new UK regulated activities regime for cryptoassets, including qualifying stablecoins, trading platforms, dealing, safeguarding and staking, and related amendments to the FCA/PRA rulemaking and permission framework. It is laid before Parliament and would come into force in stages, including 21 days after made for preparatory FCA/PRA powers and applications, with full commencement on a date left blank.

title: NS&I Contingent Liabilities Arising from Transitioning to a Multi Supplier Model
summary: HMT published a policy paper/Departmental Minute explaining why NS&I took on operational and fraud loss liabilities when moving to a multi-supplier delivery model. It notes a combined potential exposure of £2m to 2029 and says assurance has been strengthened. This is informational only and does not set obligations for firms.

title: Merger remedies
summary: The CMA has published an updated merger remedies guidance document (CMA87) setting out how it assesses and designs merger remedies, including divestitures, behavioural remedies, trustees and monitoring arrangements. It is guidance for merger parties and practitioners, not a new rule. No compliance date is stated and no direct obligations are created by the publication itself.

title: Public transport ticketing schemes block exemption guidance
summary: The CMA has published updated guidance on the Public Transport Ticketing Schemes Block Exemption (CMA53), explaining when multi-operator public transport ticketing schemes are exempt from the Chapter I prohibition under the Competition Act 1998. It applies to operators, local authorities and scheme administrators for public transport ticketing schemes, including existing and new schemes. The guidance references the amended block exemption order, which was most recently amended in 2025.

title: Advancing a Coordinated Roadmap for the Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography in the Financial Sector
summary: The G7 Cyber Expert Group published a non-binding roadmap encouraging financial authorities and financial entities to plan a coordinated transition to post-quantum cryptography. It gives high-level considerations on governance, risk-based planning, standards, metrics, and third-party coordination, but states it does not set guidance or regulatory expectations. No compliance date or mandatory requirement is set.

title: Treasury Minutes – January 2026
summary: HM Treasury’s January 2026 Treasury Minutes set out the government’s responses to the Public Accounts Committee’s reports across several departments, including transport, defence, animal disease resilience, overseas estates, Afghanistan response, NHS waiting times and BBC accounts. It records agreed recommendations and target implementation dates for departmental follow-up, but does not itself create new regulatory requirements for firms.

title: Women in Finance Charter: Treasury Progress Update 2025
