summary: HM Treasury publishes a progress update on its own Women in Finance Charter commitments, reporting senior female representation rose to 50% by March 2025. It is an update and future priorities note, not a new rule or obligation for firms.

title: Joint readout of the first UK-China Financial Working Group
summary: HMT and Chinese authorities issued a joint readout of the first UK-China Financial Working Group meeting in Beijing. It summarises discussions on financial stability, CCP supervision, crisis management, counterfeiting, AML/FATF cooperation, capital markets, RMB business, wealth management, pensions and green finance. It is informational only and sets no direct deadlines or new requirements.

title: Budget Information Security Review
summary: HM Treasury’s review explains Budget information-security failures and sets out tighter controls for future Budget-related communications and sensitive fiscal information. It says a new 'BUDGET - MARKET-SENSITIVE' classification will be introduced, with fewer officials able to access sensitive material, and that the March 2026 EFO will be published on GOV.UK by HMT on the OBR’s behalf. The changes are aimed at government processes, not firms.

title: Applying the FSMA 2000 model of regulation to the Capital Requirements Regulation
summary: Draft Treasury regulations would create the Overseas Prudential Requirements Regime for credit institutions and investment firms, with a 1 January 2027 commencement date. They set how overseas jurisdictions may be designated and how exposures and capital instruments of overseas firms are treated for CRR firms and CRR consolidation entities. The instrument is laid before Parliament for approval.

title: Public service pensions increase: 2026
summary: HM Treasury published the 2026 public service pensions increase policy paper and multiplier tables. Public service pensions in payment for at least one year will rise by 3.8% from 6 April 2026, with proportionate increases for shorter periods in payment. Scheme administrators should use the tables to apply the annual uplift correctly.

title: Payments Forward Plan
summary: HMT’s Payments Forward Plan sets out a three-year roadmap for payments regulation, including consultations and later rulemaking on consolidating the PSR into the FCA, reviewing assimilated payments law, Open Banking, stablecoins and related payments reforms. It is a planning document, not a rule or decision. Key milestones begin in 2026, with further consultations, responses and legislation expected through 2028.

title: Debt Management Report 2026-27
summary: HM Treasury’s annual Debt Management Report sets out the UK government’s borrowing and debt-management plans for 2026-27, including the financing remit for the DMO and NS&I and the Exchequer cash management remit. It explains the framework, objectives and planned issuance mix for the coming financial year. No direct obligations are imposed on firms, but it is relevant to banks active in gilt markets and government debt operations.

title: Treasury Minutes – March 2026
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes responds to the Public Accounts Committee on government fees and charges, setting out planned improvements to oversight, guidance and good-practice sharing for fee-charging public bodies. It is a government response to parliamentary recommendations, with some actions targeted for Spring 2026, but it does not itself create binding requirements for regulated firms.

title: Joint Statement: EU-UK Financial Regulatory Forum, March 2026
summary: HM Treasury and the European Commission published a joint statement recording discussion points from the fifth EU-UK Financial Regulatory Forum held on 11 March 2026. It is a record of the forum, not a rule, consultation or supervisory notice, and it creates no direct obligations.

title: Fifth Trade Specialised Committee on Customs Cooperation and Rules of Origin Meeting Minutes
summary: HM Treasury published minutes of the fifth UK-EU Trade Specialised Committee on Customs Cooperation and Rules of Origin meeting, held on 16 October 2025. The minutes describe discussions under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement on customs cooperation, rules of origin and related trade facilitation topics. No new obligations, deadlines or rule changes are set out.

title: UK-Japan Financial Regulatory Forum Joint Statement, March 2026
summary: HM Treasury and Japan’s Financial Services Agency published a joint statement recording discussions at the fourth UK-Japan Financial Regulatory Forum. It is a public record of the meeting and does not set out new rules, guidance, deadlines, or obligations for firms.

title: Northern Growth Strategy: Case for change
summary: HM Treasury has published a policy paper setting out the next steps for its Northern Growth Strategy, focused on regional growth, transport, investment, skills and devolution. It is a government strategy and invitation to future engagement, not a binding regulatory change. No compliance deadline or obligation is created in the document.

title: Sovereign Grant Act 2011: report of the Royal Trustees on the Sovereign Grant 2026-27
summary: This is HMT’s statutory report to Parliament under the Sovereign Grant Act 2011 setting the Sovereign Grant for 2026-27 and explaining how it was calculated. It is part of the annual legislative machinery for the Royal Household funding, not a banking or FCA/PRA rule change. No action is required for financial firms unless they have a specific interest in public-sector legal updates.

title: Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee – 19 March 2026
summary: This is a communiqué from the Finance: Interministerial Standing Committee meeting of 19 March 2026. It is an informational government publication about discussions between UK and devolved finance ministers, with no stated rule changes, deadlines, or obligations for firms.

title: Cabinet Office and HM Treasury small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) action plan: 2025 to 2028
summary: Cabinet Office and HM Treasury published a policy paper setting out an SME action plan for 2025 to 2028. It describes government procurement spend targets and actions to reduce barriers and increase SME participation in public sector supply chains from April 2025 to March 2028.

title: Chancellor meeting with Gilt-edged Market Makers: Minutes - March 2026
summary: HM Treasury published summary minutes of the Chancellor’s 23 March 2026 meeting with wholesale Gilt-edged Market Makers. The meeting discussed views on global and UK economic prospects. It is informational only and does not impose any requirements or deadlines.

title: Joint Exchequer Committee (Scotland) - 19 March 2026
summary: This is a government policy paper/communique on the Joint Exchequer Committee (Scotland) discussing Scotland’s Fiscal Framework. It is informational only and does not set or change any regulatory requirements for firms.

title: Mortgage Charter 2026
summary: HMT published a policy paper describing the 2026 Mortgage Charter. Lenders signing up to the charter will offer borrowers extra short-term flexibility if they are worried about mortgage payments, following discussions on mortgage rate pressures. No new legal requirement or implementation date is set out in the text.

title: User and Preparer Advisory Group Minutes: November 2025
summary: Minutes/agenda for a government financial reporting advisory group meeting, listing discussion items and attendees. It is informational only and does not set or change any regulatory requirements for firms.

title: Treasury Minutes – April 2026
summary: HM Treasury’s April 2026 Treasury Minutes responds to Committee of Public Accounts reports across several departments, including energy efficiency installations, police productivity, clinical negligence, probation, fraud and NS&I transformation. It sets out the government’s answers to PAC recommendations and mentions ongoing work, including on ECO/GBIS and an Autumn 2026 target implementation date in one area. It does not itself create binding requirements for firms.

title: U.S. – UK Financial Regulatory Working Group Winter 2026: Joint Statement
summary: HM Treasury and the U.S. Treasury published a joint statement recording the discussions and outcomes of the 12th Financial Regulatory Working Group meeting held on 25 February 2026. It is a public record and does not create new rules, deadlines or obligations for firms.

title: Decision No 1/2026 of the Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement, amending Protocol I of the Trade and Cooperation Agreement
summary: This Decision amends Protocol I to the UK-EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement to set the UK’s participation terms for Erasmus+ from 1 January 2027, including contribution, eligibility and governance requirements. It applies from 1 January 2027 and requires designation of a national authority, national agency and independent audit body for participation.

title: OFSI Strategy: 2026 - 2029
summary: OFSI publishes its 2026-2029 strategy setting out how it will implement UK financial sanctions over the next three years. It highlights stronger enforcement, clearer expectations, faster support, and more use of data and AI, but it does not itself change rules or create new legal obligations.

title: EM on EU Decision on TCA Specialised Committee Erasmus+ position
summary: HM Treasury explains an EU Council Decision and related TCA amendments that would let the UK associate to Erasmus+ from 1 January 2027. It sets out the UK’s role, eligibility, financial contribution mechanics and review arrangements. No firm-facing compliance deadline is created for banks, but the decision becomes part of the TCA once adopted.

title: World Bank Group and International Monetary Fund 2026 Spring Meetings, Development Committee: UK Governors' statement
summary: UK ministers’ statement at the World Bank Group and IMF Development Committee 2026 Spring Meetings. It is a policy speech/statement for awareness only and does not create or change any UK regulatory obligations for firms.

title: Policy note: Draft statutory instrument amending the Cryptoasset Regulations
summary: HM Treasury has published a draft statutory instrument and policy note to amend the Cryptoassets Regulations 2026, mainly to carve UK-issued qualifying stablecoin payment activity out of the cryptoasset dealing and arranging perimeter ahead of wider payments reforms. It is seeking industry views during an informal consultation period and says it will consult more fully on payments services reforms soon. No final compliance date is set in this note.

title: HM Treasury and Financial Conduct Authority Performance Reviews
summary: HM Treasury has published records of six-monthly performance review meetings between the Economic Secretary to the Treasury and the FCA Chief Executive. The paper explains the government’s commitment to formalise regulator performance reviews and provides meeting minutes for February 2026 and July 2025. It is informational only and creates no direct obligations for firms.

title: HM Treasury and Prudential Regulation Authority Performance Reviews
summary: HM Treasury has published records of six-monthly performance review meetings between the Economic Secretary and the PRA Chief Executive. The document is informational and explains that these minutes relate to the regulator performance review process committed to in the March 2025 Regulation Action Plan.

title: Changes to the Risk Transformation Regulations
summary: HMT has published a consultation response on changes to the Risk Transformation Regulations. It will take forward reforms through primary and secondary legislation, including clearer funding expectations for transformer vehicles and a new power to let protected cell companies carry out insurance contracts. Further legislation will follow as Parliamentary time allows; regulators will then consider rule changes.

title: Oxford-Cambridge Growth Corridor Investment Prospectus
summary: HMT published an investment prospectus promoting the Oxford-Cambridge Growth Corridor to investors, developers and businesses. It highlights regional opportunities, government support, infrastructure, tax and talent measures, and sector strengths, but does not create or change regulatory requirements. No action date is set.

title: Safeguarding Stability, Enabling Growth: The Ring-Fencing Review
summary: HM Treasury’s Ring-Fencing Review sets out a reform package for ring-fenced banks, including planned primary legislation, later secondary-legislation changes and future consultations on new flexibilities such as a New Growth Allowance and wider permitted products. It also signals reviews by the PRA, FPC and Bank of England on capital and resolution interactions. No immediate rule changes are made in this paper.

title: Public service pensions: 2024 valuations
summary: HM Treasury has made the Public Service Pensions (Valuations and Employer Cost Cap) (Amendment) Directions 2026. The directions amend the valuation and employer cost cap framework for public service pension schemes, including updated assumptions, definitions and timing provisions. They take effect the day after signing and apply across England and Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland.

title: Getting Britain Building: Reforming Judicial Review for Infrastructure
summary: HMT is consulting on reforms to judicial review for major infrastructure, including a parliamentary authorisation route for critical energy projects and a structured challenge window for all NSIPs. The paper says these options would depend on detailed design and underpinning legislation, with further detail to follow before legislation is introduced. No immediate obligations arise from this paper.

title: Treasury Minutes – May 2026
summary: HM Treasury’s Treasury Minutes sets out the government’s responses to Committee of Public Accounts reports from Session 2024-26, including excess votes and other public-spending matters. It is a parliamentary response document, not a rule, guidance or enforcement notice. Some items mention actions already implemented in March 2026, but the publication itself creates no new obligations for firms.

title: Whole of Government Accounts, 2023-24
summary: HM Treasury published the 2023-24 Whole of Government Accounts, a retrospective financial-reporting document on the UK public sector and local audit backlog. It includes commentary on missing and unaudited local authority data, fiscal risk management, long-term trends, and future developments for WGA. No direct obligations are created for regulated firms.

title: National Wealth Fund Framework Document
summary: HMT has published the National Wealth Fund’s Framework Document, setting out its governance, accountability, reporting and financial control arrangements. It applies to the Fund, HMT and the Shareholder Representative, and is to be reviewed at least every 3 years, with the latest review date stated as April 2029. The document itself is not a rule change, but codifies the operating framework for the public body.

title: The National Wealth Fund and HM Treasury Keep Well Agreement
summary: HMT and the National Wealth Fund have executed a new keep well agreement, replacing the prior one and increasing the funding cap to £27.8 billion. The agreement also extends support to Sizewell C-related commitments and other NWF liabilities, with HMT required to provide funds up to the total cap if NWF cannot meet payment obligations.

title: Joint statement from the Specialised Committee on Financial Provisions, 4 June 2026
summary: HMT and the European Commission issued a joint statement on progress in Financial Provisions work streams, including invoices the EU sends to the UK under the Financial Settlement. It is informational only and does not set or change requirements for firms.

title: Treasury Minutes progress report – June 2026
summary: Treasury Minutes Progress is a government progress report updating Parliament on implementation of Committee of Public Accounts recommendations across multiple sessions. It records status updates on public-sector recommendations and does not create or change requirements for financial firms. No direct action dates or obligations for banks are stated.

title: Introducing the AI Economics Institute
summary: HMT announces a new AI Economics Institute, a joint HM Treasury–DSIT unit to study AI’s economic impacts and support evidence-based policy. It will build data, conduct research and develop models on adoption, productivity, labour markets, firms and income distribution. No compliance deadline or binding requirement is set out.

title: AI Economics Institute Prospectus
summary: HMT has published a policy paper prospectus for the new AI Economics Institute, describing its research remit on AI’s economic impacts and the modelling work it will develop. It is an informational outlook for government, industry and academia, with no firm-specific regulatory requirement or implementation date.

title: HM Treasury Market Engagement Group
summary: HM Treasury published the terms of reference for its Market Engagement Group, a senior forum for market participants to share views on UK financial markets with the Chancellor. It covers membership, meeting frequency, confidentiality, competition law and a privacy notice for applicants. There are no new regulatory requirements for firms, but participating members should note conduct, confidentiality and data-processing terms.

title: HM Treasury Market Engagement Group summary minutes – June 2026
summary: HM Treasury published summary minutes of the Market Engagement Group for June 2026. It is a high-level forum for financial market participants to share views with the Chancellor on UK financial market developments, including gilts and sterling. The note is informational only and does not set requirements or deadlines.

title: Report of the Royal Trustees on the Sovereign Grant Review 2026
summary: This HMT report reviews the Sovereign Grant under the Sovereign Grant Act 2011 and concludes the grant should be set lower for 2027-28 once legislation allows it. It also notes expected costs for 2027-28 to 2031-32, including palace maintenance, cyber-security upgrades and energy efficiency works, and explains the Crown Estate revenue assumptions used in the review.

title: Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes Minutes: 15 December 2025
summary: This is a published set of minutes from the UK-EU Specialised Committee on Participation in Union Programmes. It is informational only and does not create or change requirements for firms.

title: UK–Australia Investment Partnership Memorandum of Understanding
summary: HMT published a policy paper and voluntary MoU with Australia to encourage cooperation on cross-border investment, especially for pension and superannuation funds. It is non-binding and does not set a compliance date or new rule for firms. The document is mainly informational and aimed at supporting future policy and regulatory discussions.

title: The Defence Investment Plan
summary: HMT published a policy paper setting out the government’s Defence Investment Plan, including planned defence spending and capability investment over coming years. It is an official policy document on public spending priorities, not a financial-services rule or supervisory publication, and it states no compliance dates for firms.

title: Green Book discount rate review 2026
summary: HM Treasury published a policy paper and annexes on the 2026 Green Book discount rate review, summarising findings and recommendations on government appraisal discounting. It is informational and aimed at public-sector appraisal practice rather than regulated firms, with no stated compliance date or direct action for banks.

title: Green Book Review 2025: One year on
summary: HM Treasury publishes a one-year review of the Green Book Review 2025, describing progress on government appraisal reforms and related public investment actions. It is an informational report on public-sector policy and guidance, not a rule, consultation, or supervisory notice for firms. No direct compliance deadline or obligation is created for banks.

title: FSCS Annual Report and Accounts and Class Statements 2025/26
summary: FSCS’s 2025/26 annual report sets out performance, compensation paid, recoveries, governance and strategy for the year ended 31 March 2026. It notes developments including the higher deposit protection limit and FSCS preparation for expanded responsibilities under recent legislation, but it does not itself create new requirements.

title: National Payments Vision
summary: HMT’s National Payments Vision sets out the government’s strategic ambitions and planned coordination actions for the UK payments ecosystem, including Open Banking, infrastructure resilience and regulatory alignment. It is aimed at government, regulators and the payments sector, but does not itself create binding requirements or set implementation deadlines in the text provided.

title: A new approach to ensure regulators and regulation support growth
summary: HMT’s July 2026 Regulation Action Plan progress report sets out government policy on using regulation to support growth, including an upcoming Regulating for Growth Bill and an Enhancing Financial Services Bill. It is a policy update, not a binding rule change, and gives no financial-services compliance date.

title: HM Treasury British Sign Language (BSL) 5-year plan: 1-year update, July 2026
summary: HM Treasury published a one-year progress update on its 2025 to 2030 British Sign Language plan, explaining how it has used BSL in public communications. It applies to government departments reporting under the BSL Act 2022, not regulated firms. No new requirements or deadlines for financial services firms are created.

title: Recommendations of the Transatlantic Taskforce for Markets of the Future
summary: HMT published a policy paper setting out UK-US recommendations for cooperation on digital assets, tokenisation, capital markets and stablecoins. It signals future cross-border regulatory coordination and says progress will be reported through the UK-US Financial Regulatory Working Group. No binding UK requirements or implementation dates are set out in this paper.

title: Dematerialisation Market Action Taskforce
summary: A HMT-sponsored taskforce working draft sets out a non-binding implementation plan to withdraw paper share certificates and move to digital registers for UK-traded shares of UK incorporated companies. It targets Step 1 implementation before the end of 2027, with a recommended date still to be proposed and further consultation expected on some issues.

title: One Year On: Delivering the FS Growth and Competitiveness Strategy
summary: HMT’s policy paper is a one-year progress update on the Financial Services Growth and Competitiveness Strategy. It summarises government actions already taken or planned across regulation, capital markets, fintech, cryptoassets, skills and regional growth. It is relevant to the UK financial services sector generally, but does not itself impose requirements or set a compliance date.

title: Alternative Investment Fund Managers Regulation – Draft SI and Policy note
summary: HM Treasury has laid draft regulations for the Alternative Investment Fund Managers Regulations 2026. The draft updates the UK regime for AIFMs, including authorisation, depositaries, marketing, control acquisitions, registration/suspension of RVECA and SEF managers, and FCA information/reporting powers. The regulations come into force on [DATE] once made and approved by Parliament.

title: Financial Services Regulators Complaints Commissioner Annual Report and Accounts 2025-26 and regulator responses
summary: Annual report of the Financial Regulators Complaints Commissioner covering 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026, with regulator responses. It reviews complaints about the FCA, PRA, certain Bank of England oversight functions and the PSR, and highlights themes such as complaints linked to failed authorised firms. It does not create new requirements.

title: Meeting minutes - February 2026
summary: HMT published minutes of the Chancellor’s statutory post-Financial Stability Report meeting with the Bank of England Governor. The note explains the meeting required under the Bank of England Act 1998 (as amended) to discuss the latest Financial Stability Report and related financial stability matters. No new rules are created, but it records a legal obligation and statutory process relevant to financial stability oversight.

title: Update on the Digital Gilt Instrument (DIGIT) pilot issuance
summary: HMT provides a progress update on the Digital Gilt Instrument pilot. It says the first DIGIT transaction is expected by Q1 2027 on HSBC Orion and notes an HSBC-LSEG MoU to support investor access. This is an informational government update, not a rule change.

title: EM on customs duty on distance imported goods sales (C(2026)2760)
summary: HMRC’s explanatory memorandum summarises EU Delegated Regulation 2026/1022 on customs declarations and data for the temporary €3 duty on certain low-value distance-imported goods. It applies in the UK only for Northern Ireland under the Windsor Framework and has applied since 2026-07-01. Most parcels using Windsor facilitations are outside scope; declaration instructions may later change.

title: Treasury Minutes – July 2026
summary: HM Treasury’s July 2026 Treasury Minutes is a government response to Public Accounts Committee reports, including one on the Bank of England’s RTGS Renewal Programme. It does not create financial-services rules or obligations for firms. It is mainly relevant for awareness of public-sector programme oversight and implementation updates.

title: RWE energy code modification appeal
summary: Ofgem’s decision rejects CUSC modification CMP344 on clarification of transmission licensee revenue recovery and revenue adjustments. The publication explains the existing revenue framework for TOs and OFTOs and confirms no change is made to the charging methodology. It is directed to NESO, CUSC parties and the CUSC Panel, with publication dated 2026-05-01.

title: HM Treasury and Financial Conduct Authority Regulatory Perimeter Meeting – April 2026
summary: This is a record of a meeting between HM Treasury and the FCA about the FCA’s Perimeter Report and the financial services regulatory perimeter. It is informational only and does not change rules or create deadlines for firms.

title: G7 Cyber Expert Group: Reconnection Framework Technical Annex
summary: HMT published a G7 Cyber Expert Group technical annex on reconnection after a material cyber incident. It describes non-binding best practices on disconnection, assessment, remediation, assurance, reconnection and recovery, aimed primarily at financial sector organisations and usable by third parties. No compliance or implementation date is stated.
